# Rift: complete integration guide for AI agents and developers

> Rift is wallet and payments infrastructure. One REST API (plus an embeddable widget and TypeScript SDKs) gives your product: passkey-owned non-custodial smart-account wallets, gasless transactions, stablecoin payouts to mobile money, bank, till and paybill, onramp (local money to stablecoins), swaps and bridges, WalletConnect, a per-customer ledger, signed webhooks and an approvals flow so a server can start a payment that the customer approves with a passkey. Rift holds no key that can move customer funds.

This file is self-contained. It contains everything needed to integrate Rift: environments, authentication, every guide, error codes, webhook verification, SDK and widget reference, and a catalogue of every public endpoint. Canonical site: https://riftfi.com/docs/ . A shorter index is at https://riftfi.com/llms.txt .

## Facts you must get right

- Sandbox API base URL: https://sandbox.riftfi.com . Free. No payment. Start here.
- Production API base URL: https://api.riftfi.com . Access is a flat $88 per month subscription (no usage tiers).
- Sandbox and production are separate: keys, projects, customers and wallets do not cross environments. The optional header `X-Rift-Mode: sandbox|production` selects the environment's data.
- Widget scripts: sandbox https://widget.sandbox.riftfi.com/embed.js ; production https://widget.riftfi.com/embed.js . The widget origin decides which backend it talks to.
- Dashboard (create projects, keys, allowed origins, billing): https://portal.riftfi.com
- Credentials: project key `sk_...` (X-API-Key header; server side), public key `pk_...` (frontend; being introduced, existing keys keep working), platform key `psk_...` (server only; Platform API), and the customer access token (Authorization: Bearer).
- Never put an `sk_` or `psk_` key in browser or mobile code. Never commit keys. Read them from environment variables.
- Errors look like `{ "error": "CODE", "message": "..." }`. Branch on `body.code ?? body.error`, never on the message text.
- A server-initiated fund move without a passkey proof returns `202 { "status": "APPROVAL_REQUIRED", "approvalId": "...", "approvalUrl": "...", "expiresAt": "..." }`. Nothing has moved yet. The customer approves with their passkey (widget `Rift.open({ mode: "approve", approvalId })`, React `<RiftApprove>`, or the approvalUrl). Then `GET /v1/approvals/{id}` returns `approved` with `result.transactionHash`.
- NEVER retry a fund-moving or signing request automatically (including on timeout or 5xx): it may have succeeded. Look it up (approval, ledger entry, order) first. Set SDK `retries: 0` on servers.
- Rate limits return 429; see the Rate limits section. A 402 means the production subscription is not active.
- Read corridor availability at runtime from `GET /v1/payouts/countries` (public). Do not hard-code country lists or limits.

## Recommended integration procedure

1. Create a sandbox project at the dashboard. Copy the sandbox key into an environment variable (RIFT_API_KEY). Add your web origins to the project's allowed origins.
2. Verify connectivity: `curl https://sandbox.riftfi.com/v1/chains` (public) and `curl https://sandbox.riftfi.com/v1/payouts/countries -H "X-API-Key: $RIFT_API_KEY"`.
3. Sign customers in with the widget (one script tag), `@rift-finance/react`, or the auth endpoints, and keep the customer access token server-side or in memory.
4. From your server, call money endpoints with the project key and the customer token. Handle 202 APPROVAL_REQUIRED by storing approvalId against your own record and getting the customer to approve.
5. Reconcile with webhooks (verify Rift-Signature on the raw body) and the ledger.
6. Run the going-live checklist in sandbox, subscribe to production ($88/month), switch the base URL to https://api.riftfi.com, use a production key, and make one small real transfer.

## Try requests live

The API playground at https://riftfi.com/docs/playground/ runs requests from the browser against sandbox (default) or production with a key the user types in. The key is held in memory only: never stored, logged or sent anywhere except the chosen Rift API host.


# Authentication

Source: https://riftfi.com/docs/authentication/

Rift uses two kinds of credential and a few request headers.

## Credentials

| Credential | Looks like | Who holds it | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Project API key** | `sk_...` | Your server (and the widget embed) | Identifies your project and environment. Sent as `X-API-Key`. Required on project-scoped routes (recovery, invoices, widget config); optional on most customer routes because the customer token already binds the project. |
| **Public key** | `pk_...` | Frontend code | **Coming soon.** A key meant to be embedded in browser or mobile code. Existing keys keep working when `pk_` is introduced; you will not be forced to migrate on a deadline. |
| **Platform key** | `psk_...` | Your server only | For the Platform API (`/v1/platform/*`): customers, ledgers, webhooks, gas policy, usage. Created by the project owner in the dashboard and shown once. Never put it in any client. 60 requests per minute per key. |
| **Customer access token** | JWT | The customer's session | Proves who the customer is. Sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Returned by sign-in or by the widget's `signin-success` event. Bound to the project the customer signed in through. |

Treat `sk_` and `psk_` keys like passwords. If one leaks, rotate it in the dashboard (`POST /v1/projects/{id}/api-keys/rotate`).

## Headers

| Header | Value | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `X-API-Key` | Project or platform key | Also accepted for platform keys as `Authorization: Bearer psk_...`. |
| `Authorization` | `Bearer <customer token>` | For everything done as a customer. |
| `X-Rift-Mode` | `sandbox` or `production` | Selects which environment's data a request addresses on a shared host. The sandbox host defaults to sandbox. |
| `X-Rift-Device` | `<deviceId>.<unixSeconds>.<signature>` | Device proof on money-moving and security-changing calls where device binding is enforced. See [device binding](/docs/guides/device-binding/). |
| `Idempotency-Key` | Any unique string | Accepted on Rift Accounts and own-wallet ramp money endpoints. Elsewhere, see [errors: retries](/docs/guides/errors/#retries-and-idempotency). |
| `X-Request-Id` | Returned on every response | Log it and quote it to support. |

## Examples

```bash
# Public reference data: no credential
curl https://sandbox.riftfi.com/v1/chains

# Project-scoped call
curl https://sandbox.riftfi.com/v1/widget-config -H "X-API-Key: $RIFT_API_KEY"

# Customer call
curl https://sandbox.riftfi.com/v1/balances \
  -H "X-API-Key: $RIFT_API_KEY" -H "Authorization: Bearer $CUSTOMER_TOKEN"

# Platform call (server only)
curl "https://sandbox.riftfi.com/v1/platform/customers?limit=50" -H "X-API-Key: $RIFT_PLATFORM_KEY"
```

```ts
import Rift, { Environment } from "@rift-finance/wallet";

const rift = new Rift({
  apiKey: process.env.RIFT_API_KEY,       // sk_..., server side
  environment: Environment.SANDBOX,       // or Environment.PRODUCTION
  retries: 0,                              // never retry money calls
});
rift.setBearerToken(customerAccessToken);  // per instance: one client per request
```

## Passkeys and signing are separate from API authentication

Calling the API with a valid key and token proves who is asking. It does not authorise moving funds. Every fund move needs a **passkey signature from the customer**; without one the API answers `202 APPROVAL_REQUIRED`. Google and Apple sign-in are for login only and are never accepted as a signing proof (`PASSKEY_REQUIRED`). See [approvals](/docs/guides/approvals/) and [two-phase signing](/docs/guides/two-phase-signing/).

## Browser calls and CORS

The API accepts browser calls that carry `X-API-Key` and `Authorization` headers from any origin, without cookies. Cookie-based refresh sessions are only allowed from first-party Rift origins and from the origins you list for your project, so add every origin that runs your app (and the widget host, if you self-host it). `X-Rift-Mode`, `X-Rift-Device`, `X-Project-Id`, `X-Request-Id` and `Idempotency-Key` are allowed request headers.

Do not ship an `sk_` or `psk_` key in a public web page or a mobile app. Use the widget (which carries the project key in a way the embed is designed for), a `pk_` key once available, or your own server as a proxy.

## Sandbox and production keys

Keys, projects, customers and wallets are separate in each environment. Using a sandbox key against production (or the reverse) is rejected. Allowed origins and passkey relying-party IDs are also configured per environment.

## The API playground and your key

The [API playground](/docs/playground/) lets you enter a key at runtime. It keeps it in memory only; see the page for the exact guarantees. You can use the same key from any HTTP client.

# Capabilities

Source: https://riftfi.com/docs/capabilities/

Rift Wallets gives each customer a smart account owned only by their passkeys, with gas handled for them, and payment rails built in. Rift holds no key that can move a customer's funds. This page maps each capability group to the endpoints you call with your project API key, your platform key or your project id. Flows that belong to the signed-in end user (passkeys, device binding, approvals, balances, sending, payouts, onramp, KYC pages) are run by the Rift widget, the React components and the SDK on the customer's behalf; they are listed separately at the end. Every endpoint can be tried in the [API playground](/docs/playground/).

Beta features may change before general availability.

## Per-project endpoints (your API key or project id)

| Group | What you can do | Main endpoints | Read |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Sign-in and sign-up** | Create and sign in your project's customers with email or phone one-time codes, external id and password, Google or Apple. The project key selects the project | `POST /v1/auth/sign-up`, `/sign-in`, `/sign-in/google`, `/sign-in/apple`; `POST /v1/one-time-codes`, `/verify` | [Authentication](/docs/authentication/) |
| **Customer administration** | List your project's customers, look up, suspend and unsuspend them | `GET /v1/users`, `/v1/users/lookup`, `/v1/users/suspended`, `POST /v1/users/{id}/suspend`, `/unsuspend` | [API](/docs/api/core/) |
| **Account recovery** | Masked recovery options, password reset and account recovery for external-id accounts, for your own sign-in screens | `GET /v1/identifier-recovery/options`, `POST /v1/identifier-recovery/password-reset`, `/account-recovery` | [Passkeys and recovery](/docs/guides/passkeys-and-recovery/) |
| **Payment links and invoices** | Create invoices, list and cancel them, record payments, send the link by email or SMS | `POST /v1/invoices`, `GET /v1/invoices`, `DELETE /v1/invoices/{id}`, `POST /v1/invoices/{id}/payments`, `/notifications` | [API](/docs/api/core/) |

| **Widget configuration** | Branding and settings the widget loads for your project key | `GET /v1/widget-config` | [Widget](/docs/sdk/widget/) |
| **Your project** | Read and update your project, rotate the key, add allowed origins, set fee markup, read usage and API logs | `GET/PATCH /v1/projects/{id}`, `POST /v1/projects/{id}/api-keys/rotate`, `POST /v1/projects/{id}/origins`, `PATCH /v1/projects/{id}/markup`, `GET /v1/projects/{id}/stats`, `/api-logs` | [Going live](/docs/guides/going-live/) |
| **Billing** | Plans, payment details, your subscription state and payments | `GET /v1/billing/plans`, `/v1/billing/payment-info`, `GET /v1/projects/{id}/billing/subscription`, `GET/POST /v1/projects/{id}/billing/payments` | [Pricing](/docs/pricing/) |
| **Reference data (no key needed)** | Chains, tokens, assets, FX rates and fees, payout countries, institutions and payment methods per currency | `GET /v1/chains`, `/v1/tokens`, `/v1/assets`, `/v1/rates`, `/v1/payouts/countries`, `/v1/rails/{currency}/institutions` | [Chains and tokens](/docs/overview/chains-and-tokens/), [Corridors](/docs/guides/payment-corridors/) |

## Platform tier (platform key `psk_`, server only)

| Group | What you can do | Main endpoints | Read |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Platform API (Beta)** | Customers, per-customer ledgers and statements, consent-based history for lenders, usage, platform keys | `/v1/platform/customers...`, `/v1/platform/ledger`, `/v1/platform/usage`, `/v1/platform/keys` | [Platform quickstart](/docs/quickstarts/platform/), [Customer history](/docs/guides/customer-history-credit/) |
| **Webhooks (Beta)** | Signed events for transactions, customers, approvals, accounts and ramps | `/v1/platform/webhooks...` | [Webhooks](/docs/guides/webhooks/) |
| **Gas sponsorship (Beta)** | Sponsor gas for customers or let them pay in USDC or USDT; per-project policy | `/v1/platform/gas-policy` | [Gas sponsorship](/docs/guides/gas-sponsorship/) |
| **Rift Accounts (Beta)** | Local-currency accounts (KES, TZS, GHS, UGX, MWK): collect from mobile money, pay out to mobile money, banks, tills and paybills, statements | `/v1/accounts...` | [Accounts](/docs/guides/accounts/) |
| **Own-wallet ramps (Beta)** | Cash out stablecoins from your own wallet, or buy USDC with mobile money to any address, with no Rift wallet | `/v1/ramps/...`, `POST /v1/payouts/validate` | [Own-wallet ramps](/docs/guides/own-wallet-ramps/) |

## Run by the widget, React components and SDK

These are the end user's own flows. They are authenticated with the customer's access token rather than your project key, and several need a passkey signature that only the customer's device can produce, so the Rift widget or SDK calls them for you. They are not part of the per-project API reference; the operation pages are collected under [Used by the Rift widget and app](/docs/api/core/#used-by-the-rift-widget-and-app).

- Customer profile, balances, history, deposits, sending and signing (two-phase preview then submit), approvals, trusted devices, passkey registration.
- Payouts (offramp), onramp, beneficiaries, bridges, WalletConnect, ledger and statements, identity verification pages.

## Supported money rails

Payouts and onramp cover Kenya (KES), Nigeria (NGN), Tanzania (TZS), Uganda (UGX), Ghana (GHS) and Malawi (MWK), with mobile money, bank, till and paybill depending on the country. Availability changes during the day: always read `GET /v1/payouts/countries` (public, no authentication) rather than hard-coding a list. Details and per-transaction limits: [Corridors and limits](/docs/guides/payment-corridors/).

## Chains

Wallets have the same address on every supported chain. Read `GET /v1/chains` and `GET /v1/chains/{chainId}/tokens` for the live list.

## Platform conventions

- Errors: `{ "error": "CODE", "message": "..." }`. See [errors](/docs/guides/errors/).
- Fund-moving one-phase calls return `202 APPROVAL_REQUIRED` unless the request already carries a passkey proof.
- Money statuses use one vocabulary: `awaiting_payment`, `processing`, `completed`, `refunding`, `refunded`, `expired`, `cancelled`, `failed`.
- Lists page with `cursor` and `nextCursor`; date filters are inclusive ISO 8601.
- Limits: see [rate limits](/docs/rate-limits/).

# Getting started

Source: https://riftfi.com/docs/getting-started/

Rift gives your product wallets, payments and payouts through one REST API, an embeddable widget and TypeScript SDKs. This page takes you from nothing to a working call.

## 1. Pick an environment

| | Sandbox | Production |
|---|---|---|
| API base URL | `https://sandbox.riftfi.com` | `https://api.riftfi.com` |
| Cost | **Free. No payment needed.** | Flat **$88 per month** subscription |
| Widget script | `https://widget.sandbox.riftfi.com/embed.js` | `https://widget.riftfi.com/embed.js` |
| Funds | Test payment routes and sandbox wallets | Real customer funds |
| Keys and customers | Separate from production | Separate from sandbox |

Always build against sandbox first. A sandbox key does not work on production and the other way round. You can also send the header `X-Rift-Mode: sandbox` or `X-Rift-Mode: production` to say which environment's data a request is for; the base URLs above already imply it.

## 2. Get an API key

1. Open the Rift dashboard at [portal.riftfi.com](https://portal.riftfi.com) and create a project.
2. Copy the project's API key. Keys currently start with `sk_` (project secret key). Keys that start with `pk_` (public keys for frontend code) are being introduced; **existing keys keep working**. A `psk_` key is a separate server-only platform key for the Platform API.
3. Add every web origin that will load the widget or call the API from a browser (including `http://localhost:5173` while developing) to the project's allowed origins.

Store keys in environment variables or a secret manager. Never commit them. See [authentication](/docs/authentication/).

## 3. Make your first call

Reference data endpoints are public, so this works with no key at all:

```bash
curl https://sandbox.riftfi.com/v1/chains
```

Now an authenticated call with your sandbox project key:

```bash
export RIFT_API_KEY=sk_your_sandbox_key   # from the dashboard

curl https://sandbox.riftfi.com/v1/payouts/countries \
  -H "X-API-Key: $RIFT_API_KEY"
```

Prefer clicking? Open the [API playground](/docs/playground/), leave **Sandbox** selected, paste your key (it is kept in memory only) and send the same request from your browser.

## 4. Sign a customer in

Customer calls (balances, sending money, payouts) need a customer access token in addition to the project key. Three ways to get one:

- **Widget** (no build step): add `embed.js` and a button with `data-rift-trigger`. The widget signs the customer in, sets up a passkey wallet and hands your page an access token. See [integrate](/docs/integrate/).
- **React**: `<RiftProvider>` and `<RiftAuth>` from `@rift-finance/react`.
- **API**: `POST /v1/one-time-codes` then `POST /v1/auth/sign-in` (email or phone one-time code), or `/v1/auth/sign-in/google` and `/v1/auth/sign-in/apple`. Refresh with `POST /v1/auth/sessions/refresh`.

Then call as the customer:

```bash
curl https://sandbox.riftfi.com/v1/balances \
  -H "X-API-Key: $RIFT_API_KEY" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CUSTOMER_TOKEN"
```

## 5. Move money

Money never moves on a server call alone. A transfer or payout your server starts returns `202 APPROVAL_REQUIRED` with an `approvalId`. The customer approves it with their passkey (inside your app via the widget or React component, or on a Rift approval page). Poll `GET /v1/approvals/{id}` or receive a webhook until the status is `approved`. See [approvals](/docs/guides/approvals/) and the [server quickstart](/docs/quickstarts/server/).

## 6. Go to production

1. Subscribe to production access: **$88 per month, flat**, no usage tiers. New projects get a short trial; after a paid period lapses there is a short grace period during which requests still work. When access is lapsed, write requests return `402`. Billing details are returned by `GET /v1/billing/plans` and `GET /v1/billing/payment-info`.
2. Create a production project and key. Change your base URL to `https://api.riftfi.com` (or the SDK environment to production).
3. Work through the [going-live checklist](/docs/guides/going-live/) with one small real transaction.

## Where next

| I want to | Read |
|---|---|
| Understand every key and header | [Authentication](/docs/authentication/) |
| Choose widget, React, SDK or raw REST | [Integrate](/docs/integrate/) |
| See everything the API can do | [Capabilities](/docs/capabilities/) |
| Handle failures and limits | [Errors](/docs/guides/errors/), [Rate limits](/docs/rate-limits/) |
| Get events pushed to me | [Webhooks](/docs/guides/webhooks/) |
| Try requests live | [API playground](/docs/playground/) |
| Feed this to an AI coding agent | [llms.txt](/llms.txt) and [llms-full.txt](/llms-full.txt) |

# Integrate: widget, SDK or REST

Source: https://riftfi.com/docs/integrate/

Pick the lightest path that covers what you need. All of them talk to the same API, in sandbox or production.

| Path | Best for | Where it runs |
|---|---|---|
| **Widget** (`embed.js`) | Adding sign-in, passkey wallet setup and payment approvals to any web page with no build step | Browser |
| **React** (`@rift-finance/react`) | React apps that want typed components and hooks around the same widget | Browser |
| **TypeScript SDK** (`@rift-finance/wallet`) | Your backend: payouts, balances, approvals, ledger | Server (Node 18+) |
| **REST** | Any other language | Anywhere |
| **MCP server** | AI agents that prepare payments the customer approves | Agent runtime |

## Widget

Register your page origin in the dashboard first (allowed origins), then:

```html
<!-- Sandbox. For production use https://widget.riftfi.com/embed.js and a production key -->
<script src="https://widget.sandbox.riftfi.com/embed.js"
        data-project-key="YOUR_SANDBOX_PROJECT_KEY" async></script>

<button data-rift-trigger>Sign in</button>
<button data-rift-trigger data-rift-mode="signup">Create account</button>

<script>
  let accessToken = null;
  window.Rift.on("signin-success", (s) => { accessToken = s.accessToken; console.log("wallet", s.address); });
  window.Rift.on("approval-result", (r) => console.log(r.approvalId, r.status, r.result?.transactionHash));
  window.Rift.on("signin-error", (e) => console.warn(e.message));
  // After your server returns 202 APPROVAL_REQUIRED with an approvalId:
  // window.Rift.open({ mode: "approve", approvalId });
</script>
```

`Rift.open({ mode })` takes `"signin"`, `"signup"` or `"approve"` (with `approvalId`); `theme` is `"light"` or `"dark"`. Events: `ready`, `open`, `close`, `signin-success`, `signin-error`, `approval-result`, `approval-error`. The widget origin decides the backend, so use the sandbox widget with a sandbox key. The iframe needs `publickey-credentials-create; publickey-credentials-get` permissions (set by `embed.js`). Full reference: [widget reference](/docs/sdk/widget/) and [widget quickstart](/docs/quickstarts/widget/).

## React

```bash
npm install @rift-finance/react@^0.4.0
```

```tsx
import { RiftProvider, RiftAuth, RiftApprove, useRift, useRiftApproval } from "@rift-finance/react";

export function App() {
  return (
    <RiftProvider apiKey={import.meta.env.VITE_RIFT_KEY} environment="sandbox">
      <RiftAuth onSuccess={(user) => console.log(user)} />
      <SignInButton />
    </RiftProvider>
  );
}
function SignInButton() {
  const { open, user } = useRift();
  return <button onClick={() => open()}>{user ? "Signed in" : "Sign in"}</button>;
}
```

`environment` defaults to production, so set `"sandbox"` while building. See the [React quickstart](/docs/quickstarts/react/) and [reference](/docs/sdk/react/).

## TypeScript SDK (server)

```bash
npm install @rift-finance/wallet@^4.0.0
```

```ts
import Rift, { Environment, isApprovalRequired } from "@rift-finance/wallet";

function riftFor(customerToken?: string) {
  const rift = new Rift({
    apiKey: process.env.RIFT_API_KEY!,            // sk_..., server only
    environment: process.env.RIFT_ENV === "production" ? Environment.PRODUCTION : Environment.SANDBOX,
    retries: 0,                                    // mandatory for money calls
  });
  if (customerToken) rift.setBearerToken(customerToken);  // one client per request
  return rift;
}

const res = await riftFor(token).transactions.send({
  to: "0x...", value: "5", token: "USDC", chain: "BASE", type: "gasless",
});
if (isApprovalRequired(res)) {
  // 202: store res.approvalId, show it to the customer (widget / React / res.approvalUrl)
}
```

Services: `auth`, `wallet`, `passkeys`, `approvals`, `transactions`, `signer`, `bridge`, `offramp`, `walletConnect`, `kyc`, `assets`, `merchant`, `notifications`, `deposits`. Money methods return a result **or** an approval request; check with `isApprovalRequired()`. Reference: [SDK reference](/docs/sdk/wallet/), [server quickstart](/docs/quickstarts/server/).

Set `retries: 0` on servers that proxy non-idempotent calls. A retry after a silently successful request can duplicate or conflict.

## REST from any language

```python
import os, requests
BASE = "https://sandbox.riftfi.com"          # production: https://api.riftfi.com
r = requests.get(f"{BASE}/v1/payouts/countries", headers={"X-API-Key": os.environ["RIFT_API_KEY"]}, timeout=30)
r.raise_for_status()
print(r.json())
```

Send money as the customer:

```bash
curl -i https://sandbox.riftfi.com/v1/transactions \
  -H "X-API-Key: $RIFT_API_KEY" -H "Authorization: Bearer $CUSTOMER_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "to": "0x000000000000000000000000000000000000dEaD", "value": "5", "token": "USDC", "chain": "BASE", "type": "gasless" }'
# 202 { "status": "APPROVAL_REQUIRED", "approvalId": "...", "approvalUrl": "...", "expiresAt": "..." }
curl https://sandbox.riftfi.com/v1/approvals/$APPROVAL_ID -H "X-API-Key: $RIFT_API_KEY"
```

## Receive events

Register a webhook (Platform API, `psk_` key) and verify `Rift-Signature` (HMAC-SHA256 of `"<t>.<raw body>"`, five-minute tolerance). See [webhooks](/docs/guides/webhooks/).

## AI agents

Point your coding agent at [llms.txt](/llms.txt) (index) or [llms-full.txt](/llms-full.txt) (complete, self-contained). To let an agent operate Rift as tools, use the [MCP server](/docs/quickstarts/mcp/); fund-moving tools return approval links the customer approves with a passkey.

# Rate limits

Source: https://riftfi.com/docs/rate-limits/

Rift limits request rates to protect customers and the platform. When you exceed a limit you receive `429 Too Many Requests`. Limits can change; design your client to react to `429` rather than to hard-code numbers.

## Current limits

| Scope | Limit |
|---|---|
| Platform API (`/v1/platform/*`) | 60 requests per minute per key |
| General traffic | 1,000 requests per 15 minutes per IP address |
| Sign-in and authentication | 100 requests per 15 minutes per IP address |
| Money-moving transactions | 30 requests per minute per IP address |
| One-time code (OTP) sends | 5 per 5 minutes per IP address; repeated wrong codes lock the code out (also `429`) |
| Statements | 5 per hour |
| Payout recipient lookups | 30 per 10 minutes |
| Burst protection | 200 requests per minute per IP address |

Public reference endpoints (chains, tokens, rates, payout countries) change rarely; cache them in your own app.

## Responses

```http
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
RateLimit-Limit: 60
RateLimit-Remaining: 0
RateLimit-Reset: 41

{ "error": "RATE_LIMITED", "message": "60 requests per minute per key" }
```

Some older limiters return a plain `{ "error": "Too many requests..." }` sentence. Treat any `429` as rate limited. Standard `RateLimit-*` headers are sent where the limiter supports them.

## How to behave

- Back off exponentially with jitter on `429` and `503`. Start at one second.
- Do not retry fund-moving calls automatically, even on `429`. Check the operation's status first ([errors](/docs/guides/errors/#retries-and-idempotency)).
- Poll sparingly: prefer [webhooks](/docs/guides/webhooks/) to polling approvals or ledgers.
- Cache reference data and quotes briefly instead of calling per keystroke.
- Server-side traffic from a single IP (a NAT or a serverless platform) shares per-IP limits. If you need a higher ceiling for production traffic, contact Rift with your expected volume.

## Subscription limits are different

`402` is not a rate limit. It means the project's production subscription is not active (see [getting started](/docs/getting-started/#6-go-to-production)). Sandbox is free.

# Overview


## What is Rift Wallets

Source: https://riftfi.com/docs/overview/what-is-walletos/

Rift Wallets is Rift's wallet infrastructure for banks, fintechs and institutions. You put it inside your product; your customers never install a wallet, write down a seed phrase or buy a gas token.

Each customer signs in with email, phone, Google or Apple, creates a passkey on their device, and gets a **Safe smart account owned only by that passkey**. When money moves, the customer's device signs the exact operation and the Safe checks that signature on-chain. Rift holds no key that can move customer funds, and neither does your institution.

### What you get

| | |
|---|---|
| **Non-custodial passkey Safes** | Safe v1.4.1 smart accounts (ERC-4337, EntryPoint v0.7). Owners are the customer's passkeys (WebAuthn P-256). Same address on every supported chain. |
| **Approvals for server-initiated payments** | A payment your server starts without a passkey proof returns `202 APPROVAL_REQUIRED`. The customer approves it with a passkey, in your app or on a Rift approval page. |
| **Gas abstraction** | Gas is sponsored by you (through Rift) or paid by the customer in USDC/USDT. Customers never need ETH, POL or BNB. |
| **Payment rails** | Payouts to mobile money, bank accounts, tills and paybills. Onramp from KES, NGN, TZS, UGX, GHS and MWK. Recipient name lookups. See [payment corridors & limits](https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/payment-corridors/). |
| **Swaps, bridges, WalletConnect** | Cross-chain transfers through Rift's bridge, contract calls through the Safe, and WalletConnect v2 pairing with any dApp. |
| **Customer financial history** | One ledger of every customer transaction for statements and reconciliation and, with the customer's consent, credit scoring. |

### Ways to integrate

- **REST API**: every capability, from any language. See the [API reference](https://riftfi.com/docs/api/).
- **[`@rift-finance/wallet`](https://riftfi.com/docs/sdk/wallet/)** (v4): TypeScript SDK for servers and trusted runtimes, plus browser helpers for passkey signing.
- **[`@rift-finance/react`](https://riftfi.com/docs/sdk/react/)**: `<RiftProvider>`, `<RiftAuth>`, `<RiftApprove>` and `useRiftApproval()`.
- **[Embeddable widget](https://riftfi.com/docs/sdk/widget/)** (`embed.js`): sign-in, passkey setup and approvals on any web page.
- **[MCP server](https://riftfi.com/docs/quickstarts/mcp/)**: lets AI agents prepare payments that customers approve.

### Who it is for

- **Banks and microfinance institutions** offering stablecoin accounts, cross-border transfers and mobile-money cash-out without taking custody of digital assets.
- **Fintechs and payment companies** that need wallets, payouts and onramp behind one API, with customer data scoped to their project.
- **Lenders** that want a verifiable transaction history, shared with the customer's consent, to inform credit decisions.
- **Platforms and marketplaces** paying out to users across East and West Africa.

### What Rift Wallets is not

- **Not a custodian.** There is no MPC share, co-signer or recovery key held by Rift. If a customer loses every passkey, Rift cannot move their funds for them; that is why the [recovery guide](https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/passkeys-and-recovery/) asks for at least two passkeys.
- **Not a browser-extension wallet.** If you only need to connect existing MetaMask users, use a connect-wallet library. Rift Wallets is for products where the wallet *is* the account.

### Next

- [Architecture](https://riftfi.com/docs/overview/architecture/): how a request travels from your app to the chain.
- [Security model](https://riftfi.com/docs/overview/security/): what Rift can and cannot do with customer funds and data.
- [Sandbox vs production](https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/sandbox-vs-production/): base URLs and how to switch.

## Architecture

Source: https://riftfi.com/docs/overview/architecture/

Rift Wallets has one rule that shapes every component: **the only thing that can authorise a fund movement is a signature from one of the customer's passkeys, checked on-chain by their Safe.** Everything else carries that signature or prepares the operation it signs.

<ArchitectureDiagram />

### The pieces

**Your app** calls Rift over HTTPS with your project API key and, for customer operations, the customer's access token. Server-side code never signs anything: it either forwards a passkey proof the customer produced, or gets an approval request back.

**Widget and SDKs** run the WebAuthn ceremonies. The hosted widget (`embed.js`, `<RiftAuth>`, `<RiftApprove>`) runs them inside a Rift iframe under Rift's relying party. `@rift-finance/wallet` exposes `createPasskeyAuthProof()` and `registerPasskey()` when you run them on your own domain.

**Customer device** holds the passkey. The private key is created and kept in the authenticator (Secure Enclave, Android keystore, TPM or a security key) and may sync through iCloud Keychain or Google Password Manager. It never reaches Rift.

**Rift API** handles sign-in, builds two-phase signing tickets, stores approval requests, routes payouts and onramp to the right local rail and records every transaction in the ledger. Before submitting, it verifies the WebAuthn assertion off-chain (P-256 over the authenticator data and client data hash, challenge equal to the ticket's hash, credential belongs to the customer) so a bad signature fails fast with `400 INVALID_PASSKEY_SIGNATURE`.

**smart-wallet** is Rift's ERC-4337 service. It builds the Safe UserOperation, computes the hash the passkey must sign (the Safe4337Module EIP-712 SafeOp hash), and encodes the WebAuthn signature into the UserOperation's signature field.

**Bundler and paymaster** submit the UserOperation. The paymaster either sponsors gas or takes it from the Safe in USDC/USDT. See [gas sponsorship](https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/gas-sponsorship/).

**Chain.** The Safe (v1.4.1 with the Safe4337Module, EntryPoint v0.7) validates the operation. Its owner is a Safe WebAuthn signer contract that verifies the P-256 signature through the RIP-7212 precompile, with the FCL Solidity verifier as fallback. A request without a valid passkey signature does not execute.

### One transfer, step by step

1. **Preview.** Your app posts `{ token, chain, recipient, amount }` to `POST /v1/transactions/preview`. Rift builds the UserOperation and returns `{ ticketId, hashToSign, allowCredentials, expiresAt }`. Nothing is signed.
2. **Passkey.** The device signs `hashToSign` (the 32 raw bytes are the WebAuthn challenge, user verification required). The result is an `authProof`.
3. **Submit.** Your app posts `{ ticketId, authProof }` to `POST /v1/wallet/user-operations/submit-prepared`. Rift verifies the assertion, smart-wallet encodes it and the bundler submits.
4. **Verify on-chain.** The Safe checks the passkey signature and executes.

When the operation starts on a server instead, step 1 becomes `202 APPROVAL_REQUIRED` and steps 2 to 4 happen on the approval page. See [two-phase signing](https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/two-phase-signing/) and [approvals](https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/approvals/).

### Addresses and deployment

The Safe address is counterfactual: it is derived from the customer's first passkey and is the same on every supported chain. The Safe is deployed on a chain by the first operation there, signed by that passkey. When it deploys, the same operation adds every other active passkey as an owner, so later prompts work with any of them.

Customers who had a wallet before passkeys keep their address: on first use of each chain, the old owner key is swapped out for their passkeys in one operation, and is never used for anything else.

### On-chain contracts

Safe passkey module v0.2.1, same address on every supported chain:

| Contract | Address |
|---|---|
| Safe4337Module | `0x75cf11467937ce3F2f357CE24ffc3DBF8fD5c226` |
| SafeWebAuthnSharedSigner | `0x94a4F6affBd8975951142c3999aEAB7ecee555c2` |
| SafeWebAuthnSignerFactory | `0x1d31F259eE307358a26dFb23EB365939E8641195` |
| FCL P-256 verifier | `0xA86e0054C51E4894D88762a017ECc5E5235f5DBA` |

The signer factory is not deployed on Berachain yet; see [chains & tokens](https://riftfi.com/docs/overview/chains-and-tokens/).

## Security model

Source: https://riftfi.com/docs/overview/security/

The short version: **customer funds move only when the customer's passkey signs the exact operation, and the customer's Safe verifies that signature on-chain.** Rift's servers, your servers and AI agents can prepare operations and ask for approval. None of them can sign.

### What each party can do

| | Read balances and history | Prepare an operation | Move funds |
|---|---|---|---|
| Customer (passkey) | Yes | Yes | **Yes**, by signing |
| Your institution (project key + customer token, or platform key) | Yes, for your project's customers | Yes, as an approval request | No |
| Rift | Yes, to operate the service | Yes | No |
| AI agent via MCP | Yes, with the customer's session | Yes, as an approval request | No |

### No server keys

- Every Safe is owned only by the customer's passkeys (WebAuthn, ES256 / P-256). Registration accepts algorithm `-7` only, with a resident key and user verification.
- Signatures are made on the device and verified on-chain by the Safe through the Safe WebAuthn signer contracts. Rift also verifies them off-chain first, to reject a bad signature before it reaches a bundler.
- **Google and Apple are login methods only.** A sign-in session can read and prepare, but a signing route given an OIDC token instead of a passkey answers `400 PASSKEY_REQUIRED`.
- Raw EOA transaction signing no longer exists (`410 EOA_SIGNING_REMOVED`). Native-token sends go through the Safe like everything else.
- For wallets created before passkeys, the old owner key is used exactly once per chain, to swap itself out for the customer's passkeys. The code only signs that one call shape (add passkey owners, remove the old owner) and refuses anything else.

### Trusted devices

Passkeys sync between a customer's phones and laptops, so each app install also holds its own non-extractable P-256 key. Money-moving and security-changing calls carry a signed `X-Rift-Device` proof, and a new device has to be approved from a trusted one (passkey) or recovered with a one-time code and a 24-hour cooling-off period the customer can cancel by email. See [device binding](https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/device-binding/).

### Approvals instead of server signing

A fund-moving request that arrives without a passkey proof (your server, the SDK on a server, the MCP server, an automated job) does not fail and does not execute. It returns:

```json
HTTP/1.1 202 Accepted
{ "status": "APPROVAL_REQUIRED", "approvalId": "…", "approvalUrl": "https://app.riftfi.com/approve/…", "expiresAt": "…", "summary": { … } }
```

- The stored intent is the normalised operation. When the customer opens the approval, Rift builds a fresh ticket **from the stored intent**, never from anything the client sends at approval time.
- Approvals are single use and expire after 30 minutes.
- Only the customer (their session) can preview, approve or reject. The project that created an approval can read its status with the API key alone.

See [Approvals](https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/approvals/).

### Recovery is the customer's, by design

There is no recovery key at Rift. Customers recover by holding more than one passkey: a synced platform passkey plus a second device or a hardware security key. Removing the last passkey is refused (`409 LAST_PASSKEY`). Your onboarding should ask for a second passkey; see [passkey wallets & recovery](https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/passkeys-and-recovery/).

### Origins and relying parties

The widget runs passkey ceremonies in a Rift iframe, so browsers record the embedding page as the top origin. Rift rejects a cross-origin passkey registration or signature unless that top origin is in your project's **allowed origins** and the RP ID is one of its allowed RP IDs. Register every origin that renders the widget, `<RiftAuth>` or `<RiftApprove>` in the dashboard.

### API keys

A project has two kinds of key, for two places:

| Key | Where it lives | What it can do |
|---|---|---|
| Project key `sk_…` | In the page: the widget's `data-project-key` and `<RiftProvider apiKey>`; also your server for customer-scoped calls | Identifies your project. Customer operations still need the customer's own session, and money moves still need their passkey. Browser calls are checked against your allowed origins. **Cannot call the Platform API.** |
| Platform secret key `psk_…` (Beta) | Your servers only | Reads your project's customers, ledgers and statements, and manages consents, webhooks and gas policy through `/v1/platform/*`. Cannot move funds. |

- **Platform keys** are created, listed and revoked by the project owner in the dashboard (`GET` / `POST /v1/platform/keys`, `DELETE /v1/platform/keys/{id}`). The key is shown **once**; Rift stores only its SHA-256 hash. Send it as `X-API-Key: psk_…` or `Authorization: Bearer psk_…`. Create one key per service so you can revoke one without touching the others.
- The dashboard calls the Platform API with the owner's session and an `X-Project-Id` header instead of a key; a session that does not own that project gets `403`.
- Rotate the project key from the dashboard (`POST /v1/projects/{id}/api-keys/rotate`) if you need to. Revoke a leaked platform key immediately and issue a new one.

### Webhook signing

Platform webhooks (Beta) carry a `Rift-Signature` header: `t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<t>.<raw body>">`, keyed with the endpoint secret (`whsec_…`) shown once at creation. Verify it on the raw body with a constant-time compare and reject stale timestamps. Code in [Webhooks](https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/webhooks/).

Rift verifies every inbound payment callback by HMAC over the raw body with constant-time comparison, and confirms status updates before acting on them.

### Data scoping

- Every endpoint is scoped to the calling project. A customer's access token is bound to the project they signed in through; Platform API calls for another project's customers, webhooks or keys always return `404`, so they cannot even be discovered.
- Data use beyond operating the account (statements shared with you, credit scoring) is recorded as an explicit [consent](https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/customer-history-credit/) you can revoke, and every Platform ledger row carries the customer's consent flags.
- Customer statements require a fresh passkey signature and are rate limited (5 per hour per customer).

### Errors don't leak internals

`500` responses carry a generic message and a `requestId` (also in the `X-Request-Id` header), never stack traces or upstream payloads. Log the id and quote it to Rift support.

## Chains & tokens

Source: https://riftfi.com/docs/overview/chains-and-tokens/

A customer's Safe has the **same address on every chain below**. It is deployed on a chain the first time the customer transacts there.

### Supported chains

| Chain | Chain ID | API `chain` value | Passkey wallets |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ethereum | 1 | `ETHEREUM` | Full |
| Base | 8453 | `BASE` | Full |
| Polygon | 137 | `POLYGON` | Full |
| Arbitrum | 42161 | `ARBITRUM` | Full |
| Celo | 42220 | `CELO` | Full |
| Avalanche C-Chain | 43114 | `AVAX` | Full |
| BNB Chain | 56 | `BSC` | Full |
| Berachain | 80094 | `BERACHAIN` | First passkey only |

**Berachain:** the `SafeWebAuthnSignerFactory` is not deployed there yet, so adding or removing passkeys and migrating an existing wallet are not available on Berachain. Operations that need it fail with `400 PASSKEY_UNSUPPORTED_ON_CHAIN` instead of building a broken transaction.

Every chain above has the RIP-7212 P-256 precompile, which keeps passkey verification cheap. The FCL Solidity verifier is the fallback.

> **Live list**
Tokens and chains are configured server-side. Read the current catalog from [`GET /v1/chains`](https://riftfi.com/docs/api/public/operations/get_v1_chains/) and [`GET /v1/tokens`](https://riftfi.com/docs/api/public/operations/get_v1_tokens/) rather than hard-coding it.

### Tokens

Customers hold and send native tokens and ERC-20s on these chains. Rift Wallets is built around **USDC and USDT**:

- **Gas in stablecoins.** When the customer pays gas, it is paid in USDC or USDT through an ERC-20 paymaster. On Celo, Rift's own paymaster accepts USDC and USDT.
- **Native sends** go through the Safe as a UserOperation, like any other transfer.

#### Stablecoins per rail

| Rail | Chains and tokens |
|---|---|
| Payouts | USDC on Base everywhere; USDC and USDT on Ethereum, Polygon, Arbitrum, Celo and BNB Chain for most corridors |
| Onramp, Kenya, Uganda | Base + USDC, or Celo + USDT |
| Onramp, Tanzania, Ghana, Malawi | Base + USDC |
| Onramp, Nigeria | Base, Polygon, BNB Chain, Ethereum (USDC, USDT) |
| Bridges | See [`GET /v1/bridge/routes`](https://riftfi.com/docs/api/rift-wallet/operations/get_v1_bridge_routes/) |

Rift routes each payout per request; see [payment corridors & limits](https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/payment-corridors/).

# Quickstarts


## React quickstart

Source: https://riftfi.com/docs/quickstarts/react/

---
title: React quickstart
description: Sign customers in with RiftProvider and RiftAuth, then send USDC with a passkey approval, in about ten minutes.
---



You will build a page where a customer signs in, secures their wallet with a passkey and sends 5 USDC on Base. The send starts on your server, which keeps the API key; the customer approves it with their passkey in the Rift widget.

**You need:** React 18 or 19, a sandbox project and its API key from the Rift dashboard, and HTTPS in production (WebAuthn allows `http://localhost` in development).



1. **Register your origins.** In the dashboard, open your project → Origins and add every origin that renders the widget, for example `http://localhost:5173` and `https://app.example.com`. Passkey setup and approvals inside the widget are rejected from origins that are not listed.

2. **Install.**

   ```bash
   npm install @rift-finance/react@^0.4.0 @rift-finance/wallet@^4.0.0
   ```

   Approvals need `@rift-finance/react` 0.4 or later and `@rift-finance/wallet` 4 or later. `@rift-finance/react` runs in the browser. `@rift-finance/wallet` runs on your server in step 5.

3. **Wrap your app.** `environment="sandbox"` points the widget at `https://widget.sandbox.riftfi.com`, which talks to the sandbox API. Mount `<RiftAuth />` once; it renders nothing until you open it.

   ```tsx
// main.tsx: wrap the app once. <RiftAuth /> renders nothing until
// useRift().open() is called; it hosts the sign-in + passkey-setup modal.
import { StrictMode } from "react";
import { createRoot } from "react-dom/client";
import { RiftAuth, RiftProvider } from "@rift-finance/react";
import { App } from "./App";

createRoot(document.getElementById("root")!).render(
  <StrictMode>
    <RiftProvider apiKey={import.meta.env.VITE_RIFT_API_KEY} environment="sandbox">
      <RiftAuth
        maxHeight="80vh"
        onSuccess={(user) => {
          // user.walletStatus.needsPasskeySetup is false once the user has
          // created a passkey in the modal (the default step after login).
          console.log("signed in", user.address, user.passkeySetup?.status);
        }}
        onError={(message) => console.warn("sign-in failed:", message)}
      />
      <App />
    </RiftProvider>
  </StrictMode>
);
```

   After sign-in, if the customer has no passkey yet, the modal shows **Secure your wallet with a passkey**. New customers get a new Safe; existing customers keep their address. `user.passkeySetup.status` tells you which happened.

4. **Sign in and send.** `useRift()` gives you the session; `getAccessToken()` refreshes it when it is close to expiry. `useRiftApproval()` shows the approval widget for a `202` response and resolves with the outcome.

   ```tsx
// App.tsx: sign in, then send USDC. The send starts on your server; Rift
// answers 202 APPROVAL_REQUIRED and the user approves it with a passkey in
// the Rift widget (<RiftApprove>, rendered by useRiftApproval).
import { useState } from "react";
import { useRift, useRiftApproval } from "@rift-finance/react";

export function App() {
  const { user, isAuthenticated, open, signOut, getAccessToken } = useRift();
  const { requestApproval, approvalElement } = useRiftApproval();
  const [status, setStatus] = useState<string>("");

  async function sendFive() {
    setStatus("Preparing…");
    const res = await fetch("/api/send", {
      method: "POST",
      headers: {
        "Content-Type": "application/json",
        // Your server forwards this to Rift as the user's bearer token.
        Authorization: `Bearer ${await getAccessToken()}`,
      },
      body: JSON.stringify({ to: "0x000000000000000000000000000000000000dEaD", amount: "5" }),
    });

    if (res.status === 202) {
      // { status: "APPROVAL_REQUIRED", approvalId, approvalUrl, expiresAt, summary }
      const outcome = await requestApproval(await res.json());
      if (outcome.status === "approved") {
        setStatus(`Sent: ${outcome.result?.transactionHash ?? "submitted"}`);
      } else {
        setStatus(`Not sent (${outcome.status})`);
      }
      return;
    }
    setStatus(res.ok ? "Sent" : `Failed: ${res.status}`);
  }

  if (!isAuthenticated) {
    return <button onClick={() => open({ mode: "signin" })}>Sign in</button>;
  }

  return (
    <main>
      <p>Wallet {user!.address}</p>
      <button onClick={sendFive}>Send 5 USDC on Base</button>
      <button onClick={signOut}>Sign out</button>
      <p role="status">{status}</p>
      {approvalElement}
    </main>
  );
}
```

5. **Add the server route.** Your server forwards the customer's token to Rift with your API key. Without a passkey proof, Rift answers `202 APPROVAL_REQUIRED` instead of moving funds.

   ```ts
// rift.ts: one SDK client per request. The bearer token is per instance,
// so never share an instance between two customers' requests.
import Rift, { Environment } from "@rift-finance/wallet";

export function riftFor(customerAccessToken?: string): Rift {
  const rift = new Rift({
    apiKey: process.env.RIFT_API_KEY!, // sk_… from the dashboard; server-side only
    environment: process.env.RIFT_ENV === "production" ? Environment.PRODUCTION : Environment.SANDBOX,
    // Money calls are never retried by the SDK. Set 0 so nothing else is
    // either: a retry after a silently successful request can duplicate it.
    retries: 0,
  });
  if (customerAccessToken) rift.setBearerToken(customerAccessToken);
  return rift;
}
```
   ```ts
// send.ts: server-initiated transfer. Without a passkey proof Rift returns
// 202 APPROVAL_REQUIRED; nothing moves until the customer approves.
import { isApprovalRequired } from "@rift-finance/wallet";
import { riftFor } from "./rift";

export async function sendUsdc(customerAccessToken: string, to: string, amount: string) {
  const rift = riftFor(customerAccessToken);

  const res = await rift.transactions.send({
    to,
    value: amount,
    token: "USDC",
    chain: "BASE",
    type: "gasless",
  });

  if (isApprovalRequired(res)) {
    // Store res.approvalId against your own payment record, then hand the
    // approval to the customer: <RiftApprove>, Rift.open({ mode: "approve" })
    // or a link to res.approvalUrl. It expires at res.expiresAt (30 min).
    return { httpStatus: 202, body: res };
  }

  // Only reached when the request carried ticketId + authProof.
  return { httpStatus: 200, body: res };
}
```
   ```ts
// route.ts: POST /api/send as a Web-standard handler (Next.js route
// handler, Hono, Remix, Bun, Deno). The browser sends the customer's Rift
// access token; the secret API key stays here.
import { sendUsdc } from "./send";

export async function POST(req: Request): Promise<Response> {
  const token = req.headers.get("authorization")?.replace(/^Bearer\s+/i, "");
  if (!token) return Response.json({ error: "UNAUTHENTICATED" }, { status: 401 });

  const { to, amount } = (await req.json()) as { to: string; amount: string };
  // Validate `to` and `amount` against your own limits and records here.

  const { httpStatus, body } = await sendUsdc(token, to, amount);
  return Response.json(body, { status: httpStatus });
}
```

6. **Try it.** Sign in with an email OTP, create the passkey, press **Send**. The widget shows what is being approved and asks for the passkey. On approval, `outcome.result.transactionHash` is the on-chain transaction.



### What just happened

- Sign-in (email, phone, Google or Apple) created a session. It did not create a key on Rift's side.
- The passkey you created is the **only owner** of the customer's Safe.
- Your server asked Rift to send funds and got an approval request, because it cannot sign.
- The customer's passkey signed the exact operation inside the widget; the Safe verified it on-chain.

### Next

- Approve on your own page instead of a modal: [`<RiftApprove inline />`](https://riftfi.com/docs/sdk/react/#riftapprove).
- Run the passkey prompt on your own domain instead of in the widget: [two-phase signing](https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/two-phase-signing/).
- Ask for a second passkey: [passkey wallets & recovery](https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/passkeys-and-recovery/).
- Every prop and hook: [React SDK reference](https://riftfi.com/docs/sdk/react/).

## Server quickstart (Node)

Source: https://riftfi.com/docs/quickstarts/server/

---
title: Server quickstart (Node)
description: Call Rift Wallets from your backend with your project API key. Fund moves return 202 APPROVAL_REQUIRED; track the approval to completion.
---



Your server orchestrates; your customer signs. This quickstart sends USDC from a customer's wallet, gets an approval request back, and waits for the customer to approve it.

**You need:** Node 18+ (for global `fetch`), a sandbox project API key (`sk_…`) and a customer access token. In production the token comes from your front end after the customer signs in through [`<RiftAuth>`](https://riftfi.com/docs/quickstarts/react/) or the [widget](https://riftfi.com/docs/quickstarts/widget/); for a first test, sign a sandbox customer in with `rift.auth.sendOtp()` + `rift.auth.login()`.



1. **Install and configure.**

   ```bash
   npm install @rift-finance/wallet@^4.0.0
   export RIFT_API_KEY=sk_your_sandbox_key
   ```

   ```ts
// rift.ts: one SDK client per request. The bearer token is per instance,
// so never share an instance between two customers' requests.
import Rift, { Environment } from "@rift-finance/wallet";

export function riftFor(customerAccessToken?: string): Rift {
  const rift = new Rift({
    apiKey: process.env.RIFT_API_KEY!, // sk_… from the dashboard; server-side only
    environment: process.env.RIFT_ENV === "production" ? Environment.PRODUCTION : Environment.SANDBOX,
    // Money calls are never retried by the SDK. Set 0 so nothing else is
    // either: a retry after a silently successful request can duplicate it.
    retries: 0,
  });
  if (customerAccessToken) rift.setBearerToken(customerAccessToken);
  return rift;
}
```

   Create a client per request. The SDK stores the bearer token on the instance, so a shared instance would mix customers.

2. **Request the transfer.** `transactions.send()` without a passkey proof **returns** (does not throw) an approval request:

   ```ts
// send.ts: server-initiated transfer. Without a passkey proof Rift returns
// 202 APPROVAL_REQUIRED; nothing moves until the customer approves.
import { isApprovalRequired } from "@rift-finance/wallet";
import { riftFor } from "./rift";

export async function sendUsdc(customerAccessToken: string, to: string, amount: string) {
  const rift = riftFor(customerAccessToken);

  const res = await rift.transactions.send({
    to,
    value: amount,
    token: "USDC",
    chain: "BASE",
    type: "gasless",
  });

  if (isApprovalRequired(res)) {
    // Store res.approvalId against your own payment record, then hand the
    // approval to the customer: <RiftApprove>, Rift.open({ mode: "approve" })
    // or a link to res.approvalUrl. It expires at res.expiresAt (30 min).
    return { httpStatus: 202, body: res };
  }

  // Only reached when the request carried ticketId + authProof.
  return { httpStatus: 200, body: res };
}
```

   The wire response:

   ```json
   HTTP/1.1 202 Accepted
   {
     "status": "APPROVAL_REQUIRED",
     "approvalId": "6f1c2a3e-…",
     "approvalUrl": "https://app.riftfi.com/approve/6f1c2a3e-…",
     "expiresAt": "2026-11-10T12:30:00.000Z",
     "summary": { "opType": "transfer", "token": "USDC", "amount": "5", "to": "0x…dEaD", "chain": "BASE" }
   }
   ```

3. **Get the customer to approve.** Pick one:
   - In your web app: pass the body to `useRiftApproval().requestApproval()` ([React](https://riftfi.com/docs/quickstarts/react/)) or call `Rift.open({ mode: "approve", approvalId })` ([widget](https://riftfi.com/docs/quickstarts/widget/)).
   - Anywhere else: send the customer `approvalUrl` (push, SMS, email). It opens the Rift approval page.

   Rift also notifies the customer through its notification channels when the approval is created.

4. **Track the outcome.** The project that created an approval can read it with the API key alone:

   ```ts
// wait-for-approval.ts: track the outcome with the API key alone (the
// project that created an approval can read it without the customer's JWT).
import type { Approval } from "@rift-finance/wallet";
import { riftFor } from "./rift";

const FINAL = new Set(["approved", "rejected", "expired", "failed"]);

export async function waitForApproval(approvalId: string, timeoutMs = 30 * 60_000): Promise<Approval> {
  const rift = riftFor(); // no bearer token needed
  const deadline = Date.now() + timeoutMs;
  for (;;) {
    const approval = await rift.approvals.get(approvalId);
    if (FINAL.has(approval.status)) return approval; // result.transactionHash when approved
    if (Date.now() > deadline) return approval;
    await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 3_000));
  }
}
```

   `status` ends as `approved` (with `result.transactionHash`), `rejected`, `expired` (30 minutes) or `failed`.



### The same call over HTTP

```bash
curl -i https://sandbox.riftfi.com/v1/transactions \
  -H "X-API-Key: $RIFT_API_KEY" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CUSTOMER_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "to": "0x000000000000000000000000000000000000dEaD", "value": "5", "token": "USDC", "chain": "BASE", "type": "gasless" }'

curl https://sandbox.riftfi.com/v1/approvals/$APPROVAL_ID -H "X-API-Key: $RIFT_API_KEY"
```

### Rules for server code

- **Never retry a fund-moving call automatically.** If a request timed out, look the operation up (approval status, ledger, order status) before doing anything else. See [errors](https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/errors/#retries-and-idempotency).
- **Store `approvalId`** against your own payment record before you hand the approval to the customer. It is your reconciliation key.
- **Treat `202` as success of the request, not of the payment.** Funds have not moved until the approval is `approved`.
- Every fund-moving SDK method behaves the same way: `transactions.send`, `signer.sendTransaction`, `signer.signMessage`, `bridge.execute`, `offramp.pay` / `offramp.createOrder` and `walletConnect.approveRequest`. Each returns `MaybeApproval<T>`; check it with `isApprovalRequired()`, or use `assertNoApproval()` to get an `ApprovalRequiredError` instead.

### Next

- [Offramp & refunds](https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/offramp/): look up a recipient and cash out to M-Pesa, a bank, till or paybill.
- [Webhooks](https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/webhooks/) (Beta): receive `approval.updated` instead of polling.
- [Platform API](https://riftfi.com/docs/api/own-wallet/) (Beta): list customers, ledgers and usage for your whole project. It uses a separate server-only **platform key** (`psk_…`) created by the project owner in the dashboard; your `sk_` key is not accepted there.

## Embed widget quickstart

Source: https://riftfi.com/docs/quickstarts/widget/

The hosted widget is a Rift-branded modal in an iframe. It signs customers in (email OTP, phone OTP, Google, Apple), walks them through passkey setup, and approves payments with their passkey. Your page gets events and a short-lived access token.

1. **Register your origin.** Dashboard → your project → Origins → add the origin of every page that loads the widget (and your dev origin, such as `http://localhost:5173`).

2. **Add the script.** Use the sandbox origin while you build:

   ```html
   <!-- Sandbox -->
   <script src="https://widget.sandbox.riftfi.com/embed.js" data-project-key="sk_YOUR_SANDBOX_KEY" async></script>

   <!-- Production -->
   <script src="https://widget.riftfi.xyz/embed.js" data-project-key="sk_YOUR_PROJECT_KEY" async></script>
   ```

   The widget talks to the backend of the environment it is loaded from.

3. **Add a trigger.** Any element with `data-rift-trigger` opens the modal. `data-rift-mode="signup"` opens the sign-up view.

   ```html
   <button data-rift-trigger>Sign in</button>
   <button data-rift-trigger data-rift-mode="signup">Create account</button>
   ```

4. **Listen for events and approve payments.**

   ```ts
// embed.ts: page script next to
//   <script src="https://widget.riftfi.xyz/embed.js" data-project-key="sk_…" async></script>
//   <button data-rift-trigger>Sign in</button>

let accessToken: string | null = null;

window.Rift.on("signin-success", (session: { user: string; address: string; accessToken: string }) => {
  accessToken = session.accessToken;
  console.log("wallet", session.address);
});

window.Rift.on("approval-result", ({ approvalId, status, result }) => {
  // status: approved | rejected | expired | failed
  console.log(approvalId, status, result?.transactionHash);
});

window.Rift.on("approval-error", ({ message }) => console.warn(message)); // not terminal

export async function payFromServer() {
  const res = await fetch("/api/send", {
    method: "POST",
    headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${accessToken}` },
  });
  if (res.status === 202) {
    const { approvalId } = (await res.json()) as { approvalId: string };
    window.Rift.open({ mode: "approve", approvalId });
  }
}
```

### The `window.Rift` API

| Call | What it does |
|---|---|
| `Rift.open({ mode })` | Opens the modal. `mode` is `"signin"` (default), `"signup"` or `"approve"`. |
| `Rift.open({ mode: "approve", approvalId })` | Shows an approval request and asks for the customer's passkey. |
| `Rift.open({ theme })` | Forces `"light"` or `"dark"`. Otherwise the widget follows `data-theme` / a `dark` class on `<html>`, then the system setting. |
| `Rift.close()` | Closes the modal. |
| `Rift.on(event, fn)` / `Rift.off(event, fn)` | Subscribe / unsubscribe. |

### Events

| Event | Payload |
|---|---|
| `ready` | `{}`: the iframe has loaded. |
| `open` / `close` | `{ mode }` / `{}` |
| `signin-success` | `{ user, address, btcAddress, accessToken, walletStatus, passkeySetup }`. The modal closes itself afterwards. |
| `signin-error` | `{ message }` |
| `approval-result` | `{ approvalId, status, result }`. `status` is `approved`, `rejected`, `expired` or `failed`; `result` is `{ transactionHash, userOpHash }` when approved. |
| `approval-error` | `{ approvalId, message }`. Not terminal; the customer can retry in the widget. |

`passkeySetup.status` after sign-in is `active` (new wallet), `migrated` / `migrating` (existing wallet, same address), `new_wallet` (the old wallet's key was unrecoverable; `previousAddress` is the old one) or `pending_signature`.

### Good to know

- **The widget owns the session.** Your page receives an access token for API calls; it never sees a passkey or a refresh token.
- **Customers may skip passkey setup.** They stay signed in, but every fund move returns `409 PASSKEY_SETUP_REQUIRED` until they add one. Open the modal again to finish setup.
- **The iframe needs WebAuthn permissions.** `embed.js` sets `allow="publickey-credentials-create; publickey-credentials-get"`. If you build your own iframe, set the same.
- **Branding.** The modal themes itself from your project's branding in the dashboard. The frame around it is yours; the content stays Rift-branded so customers know where they are signing.

Using React? [`@rift-finance/react`](https://riftfi.com/docs/quickstarts/react/) wraps the same widget with typed components.

## Platform API quickstart

Source: https://riftfi.com/docs/quickstarts/platform/

---
title: Platform API quickstart
description: Create a server-only platform key, list your customers, read ledgers and usage, and register a webhook.
---




> Beta: this feature is rolling out and may change.


The Platform API (`/v1/platform/*`) is how your institution sees its whole book: every customer, their balances and ledger, statements, consents, webhooks, gas policy and monthly usage. It **cannot move funds**. It runs server-to-server with a dedicated **platform secret key**.



1. **Create a platform key.** As the project owner, create a platform key for the project in the dashboard (it calls `POST /v1/platform/keys`). Copy the `psk_…` value now: it is shown **once** and Rift stores only its hash. Create one key per service so you can revoke them independently.

   ```bash
   export RIFT_PLATFORM_KEY=psk_your_key
   ```

   The project key (`sk_…`) used by the widget is **not accepted** by `/v1/platform/*`.

2. **Call it from your server.** Send the key as `X-API-Key: psk_…` or `Authorization: Bearer psk_…`:

   ```bash
   curl https://sandbox.riftfi.com/v1/platform/customers?limit=20 -H "X-API-Key: $RIFT_PLATFORM_KEY"
   ```

   ```ts
// platform-customers.ts (Beta): page through your customers with a platform
// secret key (psk_…). Server-to-server only; the browser sk_ key is not
// accepted by /v1/platform/*. 60 requests per minute per key.
const BASE_URL = process.env.RIFT_BASE_URL ?? "https://sandbox.riftfi.com";
const PLATFORM_KEY = process.env.RIFT_PLATFORM_KEY!; // psk_… from the dashboard, shown once

interface Customer {
  id: string;
  externalId?: string;
  email?: string;
  phone?: string;
  walletAddress: string;
  kycStatus: "verified" | "unverified" | "pending";
  consent: { credit_scoring: boolean };
  createdAt: string;
}

async function platformGet<T>(path: string, params: Record<string, string> = {}): Promise<T> {
  const url = new URL(path, BASE_URL);
  for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(params)) url.searchParams.set(k, v);
  for (;;) {
    const res = await fetch(url, { headers: { "X-API-Key": PLATFORM_KEY } });
    if (res.status === 429) {
      await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 1_000)); // reads are safe to retry
      continue;
    }
    if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`${path}: ${res.status}`); // 404 also for other projects' ids
    return (await res.json()) as T;
  }
}

export async function* allCustomers(): AsyncGenerator<Customer> {
  let cursor: string | null = null;
  do {
    const page: { customers: Customer[]; nextCursor: string | null } = await platformGet("/v1/platform/customers", {
      limit: "100",
      ...(cursor ? { cursor } : {}),
    });
    yield* page.customers;
    cursor = page.nextCursor;
  } while (cursor);
}

export function monthlyUsage(month: string) {
  return platformGet<{
    month: string;
    transactions: number;
    activeCustomers: number;
    gasSponsoredUsd: number; // estimate
    gasPaidByCustomersUsd: number; // estimate
    payoutVolumeUsd: number;
    onrampVolumeUsd: number;
  }>("/v1/platform/usage", { month });
}
```

3. **Register a webhook** instead of polling:

   ```bash
   curl -X POST https://sandbox.riftfi.com/v1/platform/webhooks \
     -H "X-API-Key: $RIFT_PLATFORM_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{ "url": "https://api.example.com/webhooks/rift", "events": ["transaction.updated", "approval.updated"] }'
   ```

   Store the returned `secret` (`whsec_…`, shown once) and [verify every delivery](https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/webhooks/).



### Rules

- **Scoped to your project.** Another project's customers, webhooks or keys always answer `404`.
- **60 requests per minute per key.** Back off on `429`; reads are safe to retry.
- **Keys are revocable.** The owner revokes a key in the dashboard (`DELETE /v1/platform/keys/{id}`); calls with it fail with `401` from then on.
- **Dashboard sessions** reach the same endpoints with the owner's session plus `X-Project-Id`. That is for the dashboard itself; your services should use platform keys.

### What to read next

- [Ledger & statements](https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/ledger-and-statements/): entry shape, filters, CSV export, statements.
- [Customer history for credit](https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/customer-history-credit/): record consent before using data beyond operating the account.
- [Gas sponsorship & policies](https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/gas-sponsorship/): `GET` / `PUT /v1/platform/gas-policy`.
- [Platform API reference](https://riftfi.com/docs/api/own-wallet/).

## MCP quickstart for AI agents

Source: https://riftfi.com/docs/quickstarts/mcp/

---
title: MCP quickstart for AI agents
description: Connect Claude, Cursor or any MCP client to Rift Wallets. Agents can read and prepare payments; customers approve every fund move with a passkey.
---




> Not yet verified end to end: Written from the MCP server source and README; not yet exercised against a live environment. The package is not published to npm; build it from source.



The Rift MCP server (`@rift-finance/mcp-server`, v3) exposes Rift Wallets as tools an AI assistant can call: balances, history, rates, payouts, bridges, WalletConnect and more. It cannot move funds. Fund-moving tools return an **approval link** that the agent gives to the customer, who approves with a passkey.



1. **Build the server.**

   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/Rift-FI/rift-mcp-server.git
   cd rift-mcp-server && npm install && npm run build
   ```

2. **Add it to your MCP client.** Claude Desktop (`claude_desktop_config.json`), Claude Code, Cursor and other stdio clients take the same block:

   ```json
   {
     "mcpServers": {
       "rift-finance": {
         "command": "node",
         "args": ["/absolute/path/to/rift-mcp-server/dist/index.js"],
         "env": { "RIFT_API_KEY": "sk_your_project_api_key" }
       }
     }
   }
   ```

   `RIFT_API_KEY` is optional in the config; a user can also set it at runtime ("my Rift API key is sk_…"), which calls `rift_set_api_key`. `RIFT_API_URL` overrides the API the server talks to.

3. **Talk to it.** A typical session:

   ```text
   User:  Send 50 USDC to 0xABC… on Base.
   Agent: [rift_send_otp] → [rift_login] → [rift_get_balance] You have 150.25 USDC on Base.
          [rift_send_crypto] → APPROVAL REQUIRED
          Open https://app.riftfi.com/approve/6f1c… and approve with your passkey.
          It expires in 30 minutes.
   User:  Done.
   Agent: [rift_get_approval] → approved. Tx hash 0xdef…
   ```



### Fund-moving tools return approvals

`rift_send_crypto`, `rift_offramp`, `rift_offramp_create_order`, `rift_bridge_execute`, `rift_swap`, `rift_wc_approve`, `rift_send_transaction` and `rift_sign_message` return an approval link instead of executing. `rift_get_approval` reports the outcome; `rift_list_approvals` lists the customer's pending approvals. No OTP or password is needed for these, and Google/Apple sign-in is login only.

If `rift_get_wallet_status` reports `needsPasskeySetup: true`, the customer must create a passkey in the Rift app first.

### Remote (HTTP) mode

For claude.ai connectors and other remote clients, run the server in HTTP mode:

```bash
MCP_TRANSPORT=http PORT=8800 MCP_BEARER_TOKEN=$(openssl rand -hex 32) \
RIFT_API_KEY=sk_your_project_api_key node dist/index.js
```

- `POST /mcp` speaks MCP streamable HTTP and requires `Authorization: Bearer <MCP_BEARER_TOKEN>`. `GET /health` is open for health checks.
- The API key is shared by every caller in this mode: **deploy one instance per project**, never one instance for several projects.
- An empty `MCP_BEARER_TOKEN` disables auth. Only do that inside a private network.

### Guardrails worth keeping

- Give agents a sandbox key while you evaluate them.
- Let the agent read and prepare; never put a passkey, OTP-on-behalf or approval step in the agent's hands.
- Log the `approvalId` of every approval an agent creates so you can see who asked for what.

All tools: [MCP server tools](https://riftfi.com/docs/sdk/mcp/).

# Guides: wallets and signing


## Passkey wallets & recovery

Source: https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/passkeys-and-recovery/

---
title: Passkey wallets & recovery
description: How a customer's first passkey creates their Safe, how extra passkeys make the wallet recoverable, and how to add and remove them.
---



Every Rift wallet is a Safe whose owners are the customer's passkeys. Each passkey is an **independent owner with threshold 1**: any one of them can approve. That is the recovery model. There is no recovery key at Rift.

### The lifecycle

| Stage | What happens | API |
|---|---|---|
| Sign-in | Session only. No key is created anywhere. The response includes `walletStatus`. | `POST /v1/auth/sign-in` |
| First passkey | Creates the customer's Safe address (new customer), or swaps an existing wallet's owner to the passkey (same address). | `POST /v1/wallet/passkeys/options` → `POST /v1/wallet/passkeys` |
| More passkeys | Each is added as an owner on every chain where the Safe is deployed, signed by an existing passkey. | `POST /v1/wallet/passkeys` → `POST /v1/wallet/passkeys/confirm` |
| Remove | Removes the owner on every deployed chain, signed by a remaining passkey. The last passkey cannot be removed. | `DELETE /v1/wallet/passkeys/{id}` → `POST /v1/wallet/passkeys/{id}/confirm-removal` |

Until the first passkey exists, `walletStatus.needsPasskeySetup` is `true` and every signing route answers `409 PASSKEY_SETUP_REQUIRED`.

### Check wallet status

`GET /v1/wallet/status` (SDK: `rift.wallet.status()`):

```json
{
  "mode": "passkey",
  "walletAddress": "0x…",
  "passkeyCount": 1,
  "chains": [{ "chainId": 8453, "deployed": true, "ownerMode": "passkey" }],
  "needsPasskeySetup": false
}
```

`mode` is `none` (no wallet yet), `legacy` (an older wallet not yet moved to passkeys) or `passkey`.

### With the hosted widget

`<RiftAuth>` and `embed.js` show **Secure your wallet with a passkey** right after sign-in when it is needed. That is all most integrations need for the first passkey. The passkey is created under Rift's relying party, inside the widget.

### On your own domain (wallet SDK)

If you run passkey ceremonies in your own UI, they are created under your domain as RP ID. Add that RP ID and origin to the project's allowed list in the dashboard first.

```ts
// passkeys.ts: first passkey, recovery passkeys and removal.
import Rift, { createPasskeyAuthProof, type PasskeyTicket } from "@rift-finance/wallet";

const RP_ID = "app.example.com";

// An EXISTING passkey signs owner changes (one ticket per deployed chain).
const signWithExisting = (t: PasskeyTicket) =>
  createPasskeyAuthProof(t.hashToSign, { rpId: RP_ID, allowCredentials: t.allowCredentials });

export async function securePasskeys(rift: Rift) {
  const status = await rift.wallet.status();

  if (status.needsPasskeySetup) {
    // Two prompts: create the passkey, then prove possession of it.
    const res = await rift.passkeys.setup({ label: "This device" });
    // "active" (new wallet) | "migrated" / "migrating" (same address) | "new_wallet"
    console.log(res.status);
    return;
  }

  if (status.passkeyCount < 2) {
    // Add a recovery passkey: another device or a hardware security key.
    await rift.passkeys.setup({
      label: "Security key",
      authenticatorAttachment: "cross-platform",
      signWithExisting,
    });
  }
}

export async function removePasskey(rift: Rift, id: string) {
  // Refused for the last passkey (409 LAST_PASSKEY).
  await rift.passkeys.removeWithPasskey(id, signWithExisting);
}
```

- `registerPasskey()` prompts **twice**: `navigator.credentials.create()` (ES256 only, resident key and user verification required), then `navigator.credentials.get()` with the new credential over the same challenge. The second prompt proves the customer really holds the new key. Without it the backend answers `400 PASSKEY_POSSESSION_REQUIRED`.
- Registration options are single use and expire after 5 minutes.
- `setup()` result `status`:
  - `active`: new customer, new passkey-native Safe.
  - `migrated` / `migrating`: existing wallet, **same address**, now owned by the passkey. `chains` lists each chain's migration.
  - `new_wallet`: the old wallet's key could not be recovered; the customer has a fresh wallet and `previousAddress` is the old one.
  - `pending_signature`: an additional passkey; existing-passkey signatures are needed (handled by `signWithExisting`).

### Recovery guidance for your customers

- **Ask for two passkeys at onboarding.** For example a phone (synced through iCloud Keychain or Google Password Manager) plus a laptop or a hardware security key.
- **A synced passkey is one passkey.** It survives a lost phone if the customer can sign in to the same Apple or Google account on a new device. A security key or a second ecosystem covers the case where they cannot.
- **Show the passkey list** (`GET /v1/wallet/passkeys`) in your security settings, with labels and `lastUsedAt`, and warn when only one is active.
- **Cross-device works.** A phone can approve for a desktop through the browser's QR flow.
- If a customer loses every passkey, neither Rift nor your institution can move their funds. Make that clear in your terms and onboarding.

### Deployment on new chains

The Safe address is fixed by the first passkey, and so is the code that deploys it. Deploying on a chain where the customer has never transacted needs that first passkey. When the Safe deploys, the same operation adds every other active passkey as an owner. Because passkeys usually sync, this rarely matters, but say so on your recovery screen.

On Berachain the signer factory is not deployed yet, so additional passkeys and migration are unavailable there (`400 PASSKEY_UNSUPPORTED_ON_CHAIN`).

### Errors

| Code | When |
|---|---|
| `409 PASSKEY_SETUP_REQUIRED` | No passkey yet; register one. |
| `400 PASSKEY_POSSESSION_REQUIRED` | Registration without the possession assertion. Use `registerPasskey()`. |
| `400 INVALID_PASSKEY_SIGNATURE` | A possession proof or ticket signature did not verify. Request fresh options or tickets. |
| `400 CHALLENGE_EXPIRED` | Registration options older than 5 minutes or already used. |
| `409 CREDENTIAL_EXISTS` | That credential is already registered. |
| `409 LAST_PASSKEY` | Tried to remove the only passkey. Add another first. |
| `404 PASSKEY_NOT_FOUND` | Unknown passkey id. |
| `400 PASSKEY_UNSUPPORTED_ON_CHAIN` | The chain lacks a passkey contract the operation needs. |
| `410 REPLACED_BY_PASSKEY_WALLETS` | An old pre-passkey endpoint was called. Use `/v1/wallet/passkeys`. |

## Two-phase signing

Source: https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/two-phase-signing/

---
title: Two-phase signing
description: Preview → passkey → submit. How every fund-moving operation is bound to one hash, signed on the customer's device and verified on-chain.
---





> Not yet verified end to end: Running the passkey prompt on your own domain depends on your project allowing your RP ID and origin; this path is written from the SDK and backend source and has not been exercised end-to-end against a live environment.



Every operation that moves funds or signs on the customer's behalf has two phases:

1. **Preview**: Rift builds the operation and returns the exact hash the passkey must sign, plus a single-use ticket.
2. **Submit**: you send the ticket and the passkey's signature over that hash.

Between them, the customer's device signs. Nothing else can produce a signature their Safe accepts.

### Preview

Every preview returns the same core shape:

```json
{
```
