```json
  "ticketId": "…",
  "hashToSign": "0x9b1a…c9",
  "chainId": 8453,
  "allowCredentials": ["AQID…"],
  "expiresAt": "2026-11-10T12:10:00.000Z",
  "summary": { "opType": "transfer", "token": "USDC", "amount": "5", "to": "0x…" }
}
```

- `hashToSign` is 32 bytes (`0x` + 64 hex). For a UserOperation it is the Safe4337Module EIP-712 SafeOp hash; for a message signature it is the Safe `SafeMessage` hash. Some responses also carry it as `userOpHashHex` or `hash_to_sign`; the SDK's `getHashToSign()` reads any of them.
- `allowCredentials` lists the customer's passkey credential ids (standard base64) that may sign.
- Tickets are single use. Submit before `expiresAt`, or preview again.

| Operation | Preview | Submit |
|---|---|---|
| Token transfer | `POST /v1/transactions/preview` | `POST /v1/wallet/user-operations/submit-prepared` |
| Contract call / batch | `POST /v1/wallet/user-operations/preview` | `POST /v1/wallet/user-operations/submit-prepared` |
| Bridge | `POST /v1/bridge/transfers/preview` | `POST /v1/wallet/user-operations/submit-prepared` |
| Payout | `POST /v1/offramps/init` | `POST /v1/offramps/finalize` |
| Message (ERC-1271) | `POST /v1/wallet/signatures/message/preview` | `POST /v1/wallet/signatures/message` |
| WalletConnect request | `POST /v1/wallet-connect/requests/{id}/preview` | `POST /v1/wallet-connect/requests/{id}/approve` |
| Approval request | `POST /v1/approvals/{id}/preview` | `POST /v1/approvals/{id}/approve` |

### Sign

The WebAuthn challenge is the **32 raw bytes** of `hashToSign`, with user verification required:

```ts
const assertion = await navigator.credentials.get({
  publicKey: {
    challenge: hexToBytes(hashToSign),          // 32 bytes, not the hex string
    rpId: "app.example.com",
    allowCredentials: allowCredentials.map((id) => ({ type: "public-key", id: base64ToBytes(id) })),
    userVerification: "required",
  },
});
```

The result is sent as an `authProof` (standard base64 of the raw bytes; the signature is the DER signature from the authenticator):

```json
{
  "kind": "passkey",
  "cred_id_b64": "…",
  "client_data_json_b64": "…",
  "authenticator_data_b64": "…",
  "signature_b64": "…"
}
```

`createPasskeyAuthProof(hashToSign, { rpId, allowCredentials })` from `@rift-finance/wallet` does both steps.

### Submit

```json
POST /v1/wallet/user-operations/submit-prepared
{ "ticketId": "…", "authProof": { "kind": "passkey", … } }
```

Rift verifies the assertion off-chain first (P-256 over `authenticatorData ‖ sha256(clientDataJSON)`, challenge equal to `hashToSign`, type `webauthn.get`, credential belongs to the customer, origin and RP ID allowed for the project). Then smart-wallet places it in the UserOperation, the bundler submits it, and the Safe verifies it again on-chain.

Submits also carry an `X-Rift-Device` proof from the customer's trusted device once [device binding](https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/device-binding/) is enforced on the environment. Previews do not need one.

### End to end with the SDK

```ts
// two-phase-send.ts: preview → passkey → submit, in the browser.
// Requires passkeys registered under an RP ID your page can use (your
// domain, listed in the project's allowed RP IDs). With the hosted widget,
// use approvals instead (the widget signs under Rift's RP ID).
import Rift, { Environment, createPasskeyAuthProof, getHashToSign } from "@rift-finance/wallet";

const RP_ID = "app.example.com";

export async function sendWithPasskey(accessToken: string, recipient: string, amount: string) {
  const rift = new Rift({ apiKey: import.meta.env.VITE_RIFT_API_KEY, environment: Environment.SANDBOX });
  rift.setBearerToken(accessToken);

  // 1. Preview: Rift builds the UserOperation and returns the hash to sign.
  const preview = await rift.transactions.previewSpend({ token: "USDC", chain: "BASE", recipient, amount });

  // 2. Passkey: the device signs exactly that hash (Face ID / Touch ID / PIN).
  const authProof = await createPasskeyAuthProof(getHashToSign(preview), {
    rpId: RP_ID,
    allowCredentials: preview.allowCredentials,
  });

  // 3. Submit: the Safe verifies the passkey signature on-chain.
  const receipt = await rift.signer.submitPreparedUserOp({ ticketId: preview.ticketId, authProof });
  return receipt.transactionHash ?? receipt.hash;
}
```

### Where the passkey prompt runs

The RP ID decides which passkeys a page can use. A passkey created in the hosted widget belongs to Rift's RP ID, so only the widget can prompt for it. You have two options:

| You want | Use |
|---|---|
| The widget to handle passkeys | One-phase calls that return `202`, approved with `<RiftApprove>` or `Rift.open({ mode: "approve" })`. See [approvals](https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/approvals/). |
| The prompt on your own domain | Register passkeys on your domain with the wallet SDK and run two-phase signing yourself (this page). Add your origin and RP ID in the dashboard. |

### One-phase routes

The classic routes (`POST /v1/transactions`, `/v1/wallet/user-operations`, `/v1/bridge/transfers`, `/v1/offramps`, WalletConnect approve) accept `ticketId` + `authProof` in the body as a submit. Without them they create an [approval request](https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/approvals/) and return `202`.

### Errors

| Code | Fix |
|---|---|
| `400 PASSKEY_REQUIRED` | An OIDC (Google/Apple) proof or no proof on a submit. Sign with a passkey. |
| `400 INVALID_PASSKEY_SIGNATURE` | The assertion does not match this ticket's hash, or is not the customer's passkey. Sign the current ticket again. |
| `400 TICKET_MISMATCH` | The ticket belongs to another operation or customer. |
| `404 TICKET_NOT_FOUND` / `410 TICKET_EXPIRED` | Preview again. |
| `409 PASSKEY_SETUP_REQUIRED` | The customer has no passkey yet. |
| `502 SUBMIT_FAILED` | The bundler or chain rejected the operation. **Do not resubmit blindly**: check the transaction history first. |

## Approvals

Source: https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/approvals/

An approval request is how anything other than the customer's own device asks to move the customer's money. Your server, the SDK on a server, a partner integration, the MCP server and Rift's own automated jobs (such as auto-swap on deposit) all create approvals instead of signing.

### When you get one

Any one-phase fund-moving call made without `ticketId` + `authProof` returns **HTTP 202**:

```json
{
  "status": "APPROVAL_REQUIRED",
  "approvalId": "6f1c2a3e-…",
  "approvalUrl": "https://app.riftfi.com/approve/6f1c2a3e-…",
  "expiresAt": "2026-11-10T12:30:00.000Z",
  "summary": { "opType": "transfer", "token": "USDC", "amount": "5", "to": "0x…", "chain": "BASE" }
}
```

Routes that do this: `POST /v1/transactions`, `POST /v1/wallet/user-operations`, `POST /v1/wallet/signatures/message`, `POST /v1/bridge/transfers`, `POST /v1/offramps`, `POST /v1/wallet-connect/requests/{id}/approve`.

The SDK **returns** this object from those methods (type `MaybeApproval<T>`) rather than throwing. Narrow it with `isApprovalRequired(res)`, or call `assertNoApproval(res)` to throw an `ApprovalRequiredError` with the same fields.

### Lifecycle

Every approval starts as `pending` and ends in exactly one final status:

| Status | Reached when | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `approved` | The customer approves with a passkey. | `{ transactionHash, userOpHash }` |
| `rejected` | The customer rejects the request. | None |
| `expired` | 30 minutes pass without a decision. | None |
| `failed` | The customer approves, but submitting the operation fails. | Details of the failure |

- **Single use.** Once approved, rejected or expired, an approval cannot be reused. Create a new one if the customer still wants the payment.
- **Built from the stored intent.** At approval time Rift builds a fresh ticket from what was stored when the request was created. Nothing the approving client sends can change the operation.
- **Customer notified.** Rift sends the customer a notification with the approval link when it is created.

### Getting it approved

| Where the customer is | Do this |
|---|---|
| Your React app | `useRiftApproval().requestApproval(body)` or render `<RiftApprove approvalId />`. |
| Any web page | `Rift.open({ mode: "approve", approvalId })` with `embed.js`. |
| Mobile app, SMS, email, chat | Send `approvalUrl`. It opens Rift's approval page. |
| Your own UI with passkeys on your domain | `rift.approvals.approveWithPasskey(id, sign)` (preview → passkey → approve). |

Approving (`POST /v1/approvals/{id}/approve`) needs the customer's passkey and, once [device binding](https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/device-binding/) is enforced, an `X-Rift-Device` proof from a trusted device. When enforcement is on, the call that creates the approval also carries a customer token and is gated the same way; see the caution on the device binding page.

A dedicated approval page in your app:

```tsx
// A dedicated /approve/:id page in your own app, instead of the modal.
import { RiftApprove } from "@rift-finance/react";

export function ApprovePage({ approvalId }: { approvalId: string }) {
  return (
    <RiftApprove
      approvalId={approvalId}
      inline
      onResult={({ status, result }) => {
        // approved | rejected | expired | failed
        console.log(status, result?.transactionHash);
      }}
      onError={(message) => console.warn(message)} // not terminal; the user can retry
    />
  );
}
```

### Tracking the outcome

`GET /v1/approvals/{id}` works with either the customer's token or **your API key alone**, as long as your project created the approval.

```ts
// wait-for-approval.ts: track the outcome with the API key alone (the
// project that created an approval can read it without the customer's JWT).
import type { Approval } from "@rift-finance/wallet";
import { riftFor } from "./rift";

const FINAL = new Set(["approved", "rejected", "expired", "failed"]);

export async function waitForApproval(approvalId: string, timeoutMs = 30 * 60_000): Promise<Approval> {
  const rift = riftFor(); // no bearer token needed
  const deadline = Date.now() + timeoutMs;
  for (;;) {
    const approval = await rift.approvals.get(approvalId);
    if (FINAL.has(approval.status)) return approval; // result.transactionHash when approved
    if (Date.now() > deadline) return approval;
    await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 3_000));
  }
}
```

```json
{
  "id": "6f1c2a3e-…",
  "status": "approved",
  "summary": { … },
  "chainId": 8453,
  "createdAt": "…",
  "expiresAt": "…",
  "result": { "transactionHash": "0x…", "userOpHash": "0x…" }
}
```

With [platform webhooks](https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/webhooks/) (Beta) you receive `approval.created` and `approval.updated` instead of polling.

### Customer-side endpoints

These need the customer's token and are what the approval page uses. Use them only if you build your own approval UI.

| Endpoint | SDK |
|---|---|
| `GET /v1/approvals?status=pending` | `rift.approvals.list({ status: "pending" })` |
| `POST /v1/approvals/{id}/preview` | `rift.approvals.preview(id)` |
| `POST /v1/approvals/{id}/approve` `{ ticketId, authProof }` | `rift.approvals.approve(id, …)` |
| `POST /v1/approvals/{id}/reject` | `rift.approvals.reject(id)` |

### Errors

| Code | When |
|---|---|
| `404 APPROVAL_NOT_FOUND` | Unknown id, or the caller is neither the customer nor the creating project. |
| `409 APPROVAL_NOT_PENDING` | Already approved, rejected or expired. |
| `409 PASSKEY_SETUP_REQUIRED` | The customer has to create a passkey before they can approve. |

### Design tips

- Show the customer the same `summary` you are asking them to approve, in your own words, before you send them to the widget.
- Keep your own payment record in a `pending_approval` state keyed by `approvalId`; move it on `approved`, `rejected`, `expired` or `failed`.
- Do not create a second approval for the same payment while the first is pending. Wait for it to expire or be rejected.

## Device binding

Source: https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/device-binding/

> Beta: Device binding runs in **shadow mode** until Rift switches enforcement on for an environment: proofs are verified and logged, nothing is blocked. `GET /v1/devices/policy` returns `{ "enforced": true | false }`. Integrate now; trust granted during shadow mode carries over when enforcement starts.

Passkeys sync across a customer's Apple or Google devices, so a passkey alone cannot tell one phone from another. Device binding adds a second factor that does not sync: every app or widget install generates its own non-extractable P-256 key, registers the public half, and signs each sensitive request with it. A request then needs **both** the customer's passkey (as before) **and** a fresh signature from a device the customer has trusted.

### How a request is proven

Send one header per request:

```text
X-Rift-Device: <deviceId>.<unixSeconds>.<signature>
```

`signature` is base64url ECDSA P-256 / SHA-256 (raw `r||s` as WebCrypto produces, or DER) over these six lines joined with `\n`:

```text
rift-device-v1
<deviceId>
<unixSeconds>
<METHOD>                 e.g. POST
<pathWithQuery>          e.g. /v1/offramps/finalize, exactly as sent
<hex sha256 of the raw request body bytes, or of "" when there is no body>
```

- The timestamp must be within **120 seconds** of Rift's clock.
- Each proof is accepted **once** (5-minute replay window). Generate a new proof for every request, including a retry of the same request.
- Sign the exact bytes you send. Serialise the JSON body once and send that same string.

```ts
// device-binding.ts: a per-install P-256 key that signs X-Rift-Device.
// The private key is generated non-extractable and kept in IndexedDB, so
// it never leaves this browser profile.
const BASE_URL = "https://sandbox.riftfi.com";

interface StoredDevice {
  id: string;
  keys: CryptoKeyPair;
}

const DB = "rift-device";
const STORE = "keys";

function idb<T>(mode: IDBTransactionMode, fn: (s: IDBObjectStore) => IDBRequest): Promise<T> {
  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    const open = indexedDB.open(DB, 1);
    open.onupgradeneeded = () => open.result.createObjectStore(STORE);
    open.onerror = () => reject(open.error);
    open.onsuccess = () => {
      const req = fn(open.result.transaction(STORE, mode).objectStore(STORE));
      req.onsuccess = () => resolve(req.result as T);
      req.onerror = () => reject(req.error);
    };
  });
}

const b64 = (buf: ArrayBuffer) => btoa(String.fromCharCode(...new Uint8Array(buf)));
const b64url = (buf: ArrayBuffer) => b64(buf).replace(/\+/g, "-").replace(/\//g, "_").replace(/=+$/, "");
const hex = (buf: ArrayBuffer) => [...new Uint8Array(buf)].map((b) => b.toString(16).padStart(2, "0")).join("");

/** Register this install once per signed-in customer; returns the device id and status. */
export async function ensureDevice(accessToken: string): Promise<{ id: string; status: string }> {
  let stored = await idb<StoredDevice | undefined>("readonly", (s) => s.get("device"));
  const keys =
    stored?.keys ??
    (await crypto.subtle.generateKey({ name: "ECDSA", namedCurve: "P-256" }, false, ["sign", "verify"]));
  const spki = await crypto.subtle.exportKey("spki", keys.publicKey); // public half only

  // Idempotent per (customer, publicKey): re-registering returns the same id.
  const res = await fetch(`${BASE_URL}/v1/devices`, {
    method: "POST",
    headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json", Authorization: `Bearer ${accessToken}` },
    body: JSON.stringify({ publicKey: b64(spki), label: "Web browser", platform: "web" }),
  });
  if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`device registration failed: ${res.status}`);
  const device = (await res.json()) as { id: string; status: string };

  stored = { id: device.id, keys };
  await idb("readwrite", (s) => s.put(stored, "device"));
  return device; // "trusted" for the first device, otherwise "pending"
}

/**
 * X-Rift-Device for one request. `body` must be the exact string you send
 * (or "" for no body); `pathWithQuery` is the path as sent, e.g.
 * "/v1/offramps/finalize". Each value is single use and valid for 120 s.
 */
export async function deviceHeader(method: string, pathWithQuery: string, body = ""): Promise<string> {
  const stored = await idb<StoredDevice | undefined>("readonly", (s) => s.get("device"));
  if (!stored) throw new Error("call ensureDevice() first");
  const ts = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000).toString();
  const bodyHash = hex(await crypto.subtle.digest("SHA-256", new TextEncoder().encode(body)));
  const message = ["rift-device-v1", stored.id, ts, method.toUpperCase(), pathWithQuery, bodyHash].join("\n");
  // WebCrypto returns the raw r||s form, which Rift accepts (DER is accepted too).
  const sig = await crypto.subtle.sign({ name: "ECDSA", hash: "SHA-256" }, stored.keys.privateKey, new TextEncoder().encode(message));
  return `${stored.id}.${ts}.${b64url(sig)}`;
}

/** POST with both the customer token and a fresh device proof. */
export async function signedPost<T>(accessToken: string, path: string, payload: unknown): Promise<T> {
  const body = JSON.stringify(payload);
  const res = await fetch(`${BASE_URL}${path}`, {
    method: "POST",
    headers: {
      "Content-Type": "application/json",
      Authorization: `Bearer ${accessToken}`,
      "X-Rift-Device": await deviceHeader("POST", path, body),
    },
    body,
  });
  const json = await res.json();
  if (!res.ok) throw Object.assign(new Error(json.message ?? json.error), { status: res.status, body: json });
  return json as T;
}
```

### Device lifecycle

| Status | Meaning | Can move money |
|---|---|---|
| `trusted` | Registered and trusted. The first device of a customer with no trusted device is trusted on registration, so existing customers are not locked out. | Yes |
| `pending` | Registered; waiting for approval from a trusted device or for lost-device recovery. | No |
| `cooling_off` | Recovered by one-time code; becomes `trusted` automatically when `coolingOffUntil` passes (24 hours by default). | No, until then |
| `revoked` | Removed, or cancelled from the cooling-off email. Final. | No |

#### Register

Every device endpoint is in the [Core API reference](https://riftfi.com/docs/api/rift-wallet/operations/post_v1_devices/) under Devices.

```bash
curl -X POST https://sandbox.riftfi.com/v1/devices \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CUSTOMER_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "publicKey": "<SPKI, base64>", "label": "Pixel 8", "platform": "android" }'
## → { "id": "3f6c…", "status": "trusted" | "pending" }
```

Registration is idempotent per customer and public key. Register on every sign-in; keep the private key on the device.

#### Add a new device: approve from a trusted one

On the **trusted** device (its own `X-Rift-Device` on both calls):

1. `POST /v1/devices/{pendingId}/approve/challenge` → `{ challengeId, hashToSign, allowCredentials, rpId, expiresAt }` (single use, 5 minutes).
2. The customer's passkey signs `hashToSign`.
3. `POST /v1/devices/{pendingId}/approve` `{ challengeId, authProof }` → `{ "status": "trusted" }`.

`GET /v1/devices` lists the customer's devices (`current: true` marks the one whose `X-Rift-Device` was sent), so a trusted device can show pending ones to approve.

#### Lost device: one-time code and cooling-off

When no trusted device is available, from the **new** device (its own proof; the device in the path must be the caller):

1. `POST /v1/devices/{id}/recover/start` → `{ "sentTo": "a***e@example.com" }`. A code goes to the account email, or the phone if there is no email.
2. `POST /v1/devices/{id}/recover/verify` `{ "otpCode": "123456" }` → `{ "status": "cooling_off", "coolingOffUntil": "…" }`.
3. The customer is emailed a notice with a cancel link. If it was not them, the link (or `POST /v1/devices/{id}/recover/cancel` `{ "token" }`, no customer token needed) revokes the device immediately.
4. After `coolingOffUntil` the device is `trusted`.

The cancel link in the email opens Rift's app (`/devices/cancel`). Tell Rift if your institution needs it pointed elsewhere.

#### Remove

`DELETE /v1/devices/{id}` from a trusted device → `{ "status": "revoked" }`. A customer cannot remove the only trusted device they are using (`409 LAST_TRUSTED_DEVICE`).

### Which routes need a proof

When enforcement is on, these routes require a proof from a **trusted** device whenever the request carries a customer token:

| Area | Routes |
|---|---|
| Transfers and user operations | `POST /v1/transactions`, `POST /v1/wallet/user-operations`, `POST /v1/wallet/user-operations/submit-prepared`, `POST /v1/bridge/transfers` |
| Signing | `POST /v1/wallet/signatures/message`, `POST /v1/wallet/signatures/transaction` (removed: always `410`) |
| Payouts | `POST /v1/offramps`, `POST /v1/offramps/finalize`, `POST /v1/offramps/{id}/refund` |
| Onramp | `POST /v1/onramps` |
| Approvals and dApps | `POST /v1/approvals/{id}/approve`, `POST /v1/wallet-connect/requests/{id}/approve` |
| Passkeys | `POST /v1/wallet/passkeys`, `POST /v1/wallet/passkeys/confirm`, `DELETE /v1/wallet/passkeys/{id}`, `POST /v1/wallet/passkeys/{id}/confirm-removal` |
| Beneficiaries and statements | `POST`, `PATCH`, `DELETE /v1/beneficiaries…`, `POST /v1/statements` |

Previews, quotes, reads and `init` do not. The device-management routes above (approve, recover, remove) always check the proof, even in shadow mode.

> **Server-side calls with a customer token**
The gate keys on the customer token, not on where the request comes from. Once enforcement is on, a one-phase call your **server** makes with the customer's token (for example `POST /v1/offramps`, which returns `202 APPROVAL_REQUIRED`) also needs a device proof. Requests with no customer token (Platform API calls with `psk_…`, API-key-only reads) are not gated. Plan for this before enforcement: have the customer's device produce the proof, or move the flow to two-phase on the device.

### Errors

| Code | HTTP | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `DEVICE_NOT_TRUSTED` | 403 | No header, unknown device, another customer's device, or a device that is not trusted. Body: `deviceStatus` (`unknown`, `pending`, `cooling_off`, `revoked`) and, for `cooling_off`, `coolingOffUntil`. |
| `DEVICE_PROOF_INVALID` | 401 | Header present but rejected. Body: `reason` = `malformed`, `stale` (clock skew over 120 s), `signature` or `replay`. |
| `DEVICE_CHECK_UNAVAILABLE` | 503 | Rift could not check the proof. Retry. In shadow mode the gate lets the request through instead. |
| `DEVICE_MISMATCH` | 403 | Recovery called from a device other than the one in the path. |
| `DEVICE_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | Not one of the customer's devices. |
| `DEVICE_NOT_PENDING` | 409 | Approve or recover on a device that is not pending (or cooling off, for approve). |
| `LAST_TRUSTED_DEVICE` | 409 | Removing the only trusted device in use. |
| `CHALLENGE_EXPIRED` | 400 | Approval challenge expired or already used. Request a new one. |
| `INVALID_PUBLIC_KEY` | 400 | `publicKey` is not a base64 SPKI P-256 key. |
| `OTP_REQUIRED` / `OTP_INVALID` | 400 | Recovery code missing or wrong. |
| `OTP_SEND_FAILED` | 502 | The code could not be sent. |
| `NO_OTP_TARGET` | 409 | The account has neither email nor phone. |
| `INVALID_TOKEN` | 400 | Cancel link invalid or already used. |
| `PASSKEY_SETUP_REQUIRED` | 409 | Approving a device needs a passkey on the account. |

## Gas sponsorship & policies

Source: https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/gas-sponsorship/

---
title: Gas sponsorship & policies
description: Customers never need a native token. Sponsor gas for them, let them pay it in USDC or USDT, or mix both with a gas policy.
---



Every Rift Wallets operation is an ERC-4337 UserOperation, so gas is paid by a **paymaster**, not by a native-token balance in the customer's wallet. There are two ways the paymaster is funded:

| Mode | Who pays | How |
|---|---|---|
| Sponsored | Your institution | Rift's sponsoring paymaster  covers gas; it is accounted to your project. |
| Customer pays | The customer | An ERC-20 paymaster takes gas in **USDC or USDT** from the Safe, in the same UserOperation. On Celo, Rift's own paymaster accepts USDC and USDT. |

Either way the customer sees one passkey prompt and never needs ETH, POL, BNB or CELO.

**Passkey setup and wallet migration are always sponsored**, so a customer can secure a new or existing wallet without holding anything.

### Today

Gas is sponsored by default for your project. Your plan's sponsored-transaction allowance applies; when a free-tier allowance is exhausted, fund-moving calls answer `402` (`"Free plan gas allowance exhausted"`). See [pricing & sales](https://riftfi.com/docs/pricing/) for allowances on paid plans.

### Gas policy API

> Beta: this feature is rolling out and may change.


`GET /v1/platform/gas-policy` and `PUT /v1/platform/gas-policy` (platform key `psk_…`, server-side) set who pays, per operation type. The policy is applied when Rift prepares each UserOperation:

```json
PUT /v1/platform/gas-policy
{
  "mode": "hybrid",
  "monthlySponsorCapUsd": 2500,
  "perTxSponsorCapUsd": 0.5,
  "sponsoredOps": ["transfer", "payout", "passkey_admin"]
}
```

| `mode` | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `sponsored` | You sponsor every operation. |
| `customer_pays` | The customer pays gas in USDC/USDT for every operation (except passkey setup and migration). |
| `hybrid` | You sponsor the operations in `sponsoredOps` while under `perTxSponsorCapUsd` and `monthlySponsorCapUsd`; otherwise the customer pays in USDC/USDT. |

`sponsoredOps` values: `transfer`, `payout`, `swap`, `bridge`, `walletconnect`, `contract_call`, `passkey_admin`. An invalid policy is rejected with `400 INVALID_REQUEST` and a message naming the field. Over a cap, gas falls back to the customer paying in USDC/USDT on that chain.

> **Current limits**
- **WalletConnect sends are not governed by the gas policy yet.** `eth_sendTransaction` from a dApp currently pays gas in the customer's stablecoin regardless of the policy.
- Passkey administration (setup, adding or removing passkeys, migration) is always sponsored, whatever the policy says.

Monthly spend is reported by [`GET /v1/platform/usage`](https://riftfi.com/docs/api/own-wallet/operations/get_v1_platform_usage/) as `gasSponsoredUsd` and `gasPaidByCustomersUsd`. These USD figures are **estimates** for monitoring; do not use them for invoicing or accounting.

### Fees on operations

Rift's service fee and any fee you add are taken as separate transfers **inside the same UserOperation** as the customer's action, so the customer approves the total once. Ledger entries carry it in `fee` and `feeToken`. Your project's markup is configured in the dashboard (`PATCH /v1/projects/{id}/markup`). Fees earned appear in `GET /v1/platform/usage` as `feesEarned`.

### Things to plan for

- **Customer-pays needs a stablecoin balance.** A customer with no USDC or USDT on that chain cannot pay gas there. Sponsor `transfer` (or use `hybrid`) if customers may arrive with only one token.
- **First operation on a chain costs more**, because it deploys the Safe there.
- **Bridges** pay gas on the source chain only; the destination fill is handled by bridge relayers.

# Guides: money movement


## Payment corridors & limits

Source: https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/payment-corridors/

You call one API for every country. Rift routes each request from the currency, the recipient type and the chain and token being spent, and settles it in local money.

> **Read coverage at runtime**
Availability changes during the day. [`GET /v1/payouts/countries`](https://riftfi.com/docs/api/public/operations/get_v1_payouts_countries/) (public, no auth, cached about 10 minutes) returns each country's rails, whether sending and buying are active right now, and the limits. Build country pickers and amount validation from it rather than from this page.

### Corridors

| Country | Currency | Send (offramp) | Buy (onramp) | Rails for sending |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Kenya | KES | Mobile money, bank, till, paybill | Mobile-money prompt | Safaricom (M-Pesa), Airtel; bank; till (Buy Goods); paybill |
| Nigeria | NGN | Bank | Transfer to a virtual account | Bank |
| Tanzania | TZS | Mobile money (Rift-operated) | Mobile-money prompt (Rift-operated); USDC on Base | Vodacom, Halotel, Airtel, Yas / Tigo |
| Uganda | UGX | Mobile money | Mobile-money prompt | MTN, Airtel |
| Ghana | GHS | Mobile money (Rift-operated) | Mobile-money prompt (Rift-operated); USDC on Base | MTN, AirtelTigo, Telecel |
| Malawi | MWK | Mobile money, bank | Mobile-money prompt (Rift-operated); USDC on Base | Airtel Money, TNM Mpamba; bank |

When a corridor pauses, `offrampActive` or `onrampActive` turns `false` in the countries response. When no route can settle a request, the call fails with `400 PAYOUT_ROUTE_UNAVAILABLE` and a message naming the corridor.

Kenya bank transfers are paid through the bank's paybill; the account name is looked up from the bank account first.

#### Chains and tokens

| Direction | Accepted |
|---|---|
| Send | USDC on Base works for every corridor. USDC and USDT on Ethereum, Polygon, Arbitrum, Celo and BNB Chain work for most; an unsupported combination fails with `400 PAYOUT_ROUTE_UNAVAILABLE`. |
| Buy, Kenya, Uganda | USDC on Base, or USDT on Celo |
| Buy, Tanzania, Ghana, Malawi | USDC on Base (`onrampAssets` in the countries response) |
| Buy, Nigeria | USDC or USDT on Base, Polygon, BNB Chain or Ethereum |

Onramp always delivers to the customer's own Safe. See the [onramp guide](https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/onramp/).

### Rift-operated corridors

Tanzania (both directions), Ghana (both directions) and Malawi (buy) run on Rift's own liquidity. The API is the same; what differs is behind it:

- **Rates** come from live peer-to-peer USDT markets, so they track what local currency actually trades at.
- **Buy:** Rift collects local money from the customer's mobile money, then releases USDC on Base from Rift's payout vault. The quote checks the vault first: when it is short, the quote and create calls fail with `400 AMOUNT_OUT_OF_RANGE` and `reason: "liquidity"`, and `max` is the largest amount Rift can serve right now.
- **Send:** Rift confirms the customer's deposit, then pays local money to the recipient from Rift's own float. When the float is short, the corridor shows `offrampActive: false`.
- Every money-moving step runs exactly once. A step with an unknown outcome is parked for Rift operations rather than retried, so an order on these corridors can stay `processing` longer while it is resolved.
- Failed payouts on these corridors are not refunded through [`POST /v1/offramps/{id}/refund`](https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/offramp/#refunds); Rift resolves them directly.

### Limits

Limits are per transaction, in local currency. Rift caps every transaction at about **1,800 USD** converted at the live rate, except Kenya (**KES 245,000**) and Tanzania (**TZS 4,800,000**), which have fixed caps.

| Currency | Send min – max | Buy min – max |
|---|---|---|
| KES | 20 – 245,000 | 100 – 245,000 |
| NGN | 100 – 1,000,000 | The naira value of 1 USDC or USDT plus 2% – about 1,800 USD |
| TZS | 500 – 4,800,000 | 500 – 4,800,000, and the available USDC |
| UGX | 500 – 5,000,000 | 500 – 5,000,000 |
| GHS | 5 – 1,000 | 10 – 5,000, and the available USDC |
| MWK | 100 – 5,000,000, capped at about 1,800 USD | 2,000 – 5,000,000, capped at about 1,800 USD, and the available USDC |

`limits` (send) and `onrampLimits` (buy) in the countries response already apply the cap at the current rate.

| Check | Error |
|---|---|
| Over the per-transaction cap, or outside a corridor's min / max | `400 AMOUNT_OUT_OF_RANGE` with `{ min, max, currency }` |
| Nigeria order under 1 unit of the stablecoin | Onramp: `400 AMOUNT_OUT_OF_RANGE` with the minimum; payout: `400 AMOUNT_BELOW_MINIMUM` |
| Rift-operated buy above the available USDC | `400 AMOUNT_OUT_OF_RANGE` with `reason: "liquidity"` |

### Reading the countries endpoint

```ts
// corridors.ts: build a country picker and validate amounts from live coverage.
// GET /v1/payouts/countries is public; cache it for a few minutes.
const BASE_URL = process.env.RIFT_BASE_URL ?? "https://sandbox.riftfi.com";

interface Limits {
  min: number;
  max: number;
}

export interface PayoutCountry {
  country: string;
  currency: string;
  phoneCode: string;
  rails: { mobile: string[]; bank: boolean; till: boolean; paybill: boolean };
  offrampActive: boolean;
  payoutProvider?: string; // internal routing label; don't build on it
  onrampActive: boolean;
  onrampProvider: string | null; // internal routing label
  onrampAssets?: { token: string; chain: string }[];
  limits?: Limits;
  onrampLimits?: Limits;
}

export async function payoutCountries(): Promise<PayoutCountry[]> {
  const res = await fetch(`${BASE_URL}/v1/payouts/countries`);
  if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`countries failed: ${res.status}`);
  return (await res.json()) as PayoutCountry[];
}

/** Countries a customer can send to right now, with the rails to offer. */
export async function sendableCountries() {
  return (await payoutCountries())
    .filter((c) => c.offrampActive)
    .map((c) => ({ currency: c.currency, country: c.country, rails: c.rails, limits: c.limits }));
}

/** Client-side pre-check; the API still enforces the same limits (400 AMOUNT_OUT_OF_RANGE). */
export function checkAmount(c: PayoutCountry, side: "send" | "buy", amount: number): string | null {
  const lim = side === "send" ? c.limits : c.onrampLimits;
  if (!lim) return null; // Nigeria onramp: the quote returns the minimum
  if (amount < lim.min) return `Minimum is ${lim.min.toLocaleString()} ${c.currency}`;
  if (amount > lim.max) return `Maximum per transaction is ${lim.max.toLocaleString()} ${c.currency}`;
  return null;
}
```

```json
[
  {
    "country": "Tanzania",
    "currency": "TZS",
    "phoneCode": "255",
    "rails": { "mobile": ["Vodacom", "Halotel", "Airtel", "Yas / Tigo"], "bank": false, "till": false, "paybill": false },
    "offrampActive": true,
    "onrampActive": true,
    "onrampAssets": [{ "token": "USDC", "chain": "BASE" }],
    "limits": { "min": 500, "max": 4800000 },
    "onrampLimits": { "min": 500, "max": 4800000 }
  }
]
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `offrampActive` | Payouts to this country work now. |
| `onrampActive` | Buying with this currency works now. `false` on an environment where Rift has not enabled onramp. |
| `onrampAssets` | Present when only specific assets can be bought. |
| `rails` | Mobile networks and whether bank, till and paybill are available. |
| `limits` / `onrampLimits` | Per-transaction min / max, already capped. |

The response also carries internal routing fields (`payoutProvider`, `onrampProvider` and similar). Don't build on them; they can change without notice.

### What to expect as an institution

- **Statuses are uniform.** Every order uses one vocabulary (`awaiting_payment`, `processing`, `completed`, `refunding`, `refunded`, `expired`, `cancelled`, `failed`). A compliance hold is `processing`: never ask the customer to pay again.
- **Settlement is asynchronous.** Payouts and onramps reach a final state in the background. Track orders by id or subscribe to `transaction.updated` [webhooks](https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/webhooks/).
- **Names are advisory.** Recipient name lookups never block a payout; show the returned name and let the customer confirm. A payout to a bad account fails: either the funds come back on their own (`refunding`, then `refunded`), or the customer can [refund](https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/offramp/#refunds) it when the ledger says `refundable: true`.
- **Corridors pause.** Check `GET /v1/payouts/countries` before showing a corridor, and handle `PAYOUT_ROUTE_UNAVAILABLE`, `ONRAMP_UNAVAILABLE` and `NO_PROVIDER_AVAILABLE` as temporary.
- **KYC before buying.** Every onramp needs a verified identity first ([onramp](https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/onramp/#identity-verification)).

## Offramp & refunds

Source: https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/offramp/

An offramp (payout) moves USDC or USDT from the customer's Safe to a liquidity provider, which pays local money to the recipient. One passkey approval covers both legs. Which provider pays which country, and the limits, are on [payment corridors & limits](https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/payment-corridors/).

### The flow

1. **Pick the corridor.** [`GET /v1/payouts/countries`](https://riftfi.com/docs/api/public/operations/get_v1_payouts_countries/) (public) for countries, rails and limits; `GET /v1/rails/{currency}/institutions` and `GET /v1/rails/{currency}/payment-methods` for banks and mobile networks.
2. **Look up the recipient's name.** `POST /v1/payouts/validate` returns the registered name. Show it and let the customer confirm.
3. **Quote.** `POST /v1/rates/quote` and `GET /v1/rates/withdrawal-fee`, or let `init` price the order.
4. **Request the payout.** From your server, `POST /v1/offramps` returns `202 APPROVAL_REQUIRED`; or, with passkeys on your domain, `POST /v1/offramps/init` → passkey → `POST /v1/offramps/finalize`.
5. **Track it** with [`GET /v1/offramps/{id}`](https://riftfi.com/docs/api/rift-wallet/operations/get_v1_offramps_transactioncode/), the [ledger](https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/ledger-and-statements/) or [webhooks](https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/webhooks/) until `status` is final.
6. **Refund** a failed payout with [`POST /v1/offramps/{id}/refund`](https://riftfi.com/docs/api/rift-wallet/operations/post_v1_offramps_id_refund/) when its ledger entry says `refundable: true`.

### Recipient name lookup

```bash
curl -X POST https://sandbox.riftfi.com/v1/payouts/validate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CUSTOMER_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "currency": "KES", "type": "MOBILE", "phone": "+254712345678", "network": "Safaricom" }'
```

```json
{ "valid": true, "accountName": "JANE W*** DOE" }
```

| `type` | Fields | Checked by |
|---|---|---|
| `MOBILE` | `phone`, `network` | Kenya (network defaults to Safaricom), Uganda, Ghana, Tanzania |
| `BUY_GOODS` | `till` | Kenya |
| `PAYBILL` | `paybill` | Kenya |
| `BANK` | `accountNumber`, `bankCode` | Kenya, Nigeria and other bank corridors |

`400 VALIDATION_UNSUPPORTED` means names can't be looked up on that rail. Rate limit: 30 lookups per 10 minutes per customer.

**A lookup never blocks a payout.** Networks often cannot return a name for a valid number or account, so Rift looks the recipient up again at `init`, attaches the name to the order when one comes back, and continues either way. When no name comes back, ask the customer to double-check the details. A truly bad account fails and the funds are returned or refundable.

### Request the payout

#### From your server: approval request

```ts
// payout.ts: validate the beneficiary, then request the payout.
// Kenya: MOBILE (M-Pesa / Airtel), BUY_GOODS (till), PAYBILL, BANK.
import { isApprovalRequired, OfframpCurrency, RampChain, RampToken } from "@rift-finance/wallet";
import { riftFor } from "./rift";

const BASE_URL = process.env.RIFT_BASE_URL ?? "https://sandbox.riftfi.com";

/** POST /v1/payouts/validate (Beta): name check before money moves. */
export async function validateMpesa(customerAccessToken: string, phone: string) {
  const res = await fetch(`${BASE_URL}/v1/payouts/validate`, {
    method: "POST",
    headers: {
      "Content-Type": "application/json",
      "X-API-Key": process.env.RIFT_API_KEY!,
      Authorization: `Bearer ${customerAccessToken}`,
    },
    body: JSON.stringify({ currency: "KES", type: "MOBILE", phone, network: "Safaricom" }),
  });
  if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`validate failed: ${res.status}`);
  return (await res.json()) as { valid: boolean; accountName: string | null };
}

export async function payToMpesa(customerAccessToken: string, phone: string, usdc: number) {
  const check = await validateMpesa(customerAccessToken, phone);
  if (!check.valid) throw new Error("Recipient could not be validated");
  // Show check.accountName to the customer and let them confirm it first.

  const rift = riftFor(customerAccessToken);
  const res = await rift.offramp.createOrder({
    token: RampToken.USDC,
    chain: RampChain.BASE,
    amount: usdc,
    currency: OfframpCurrency.KES,
    recipient: JSON.stringify({ type: "MOBILE", accountIdentifier: phone, institution: "Safaricom" }),
  });

  if (isApprovalRequired(res)) return res; // the customer approves with a passkey
  return res;
}
```

```bash
curl -X POST https://sandbox.riftfi.com/v1/offramps \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CUSTOMER_TOKEN" \
  -H "X-API-Key: sk_test_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "token": "USDC", "chain": "BASE", "amount": 10, "currency": "KES",
    "recipient": { "type": "MOBILE", "accountIdentifier": "+254712345678", "institution": "Safaricom" }
  }'
```

Without a passkey proof the call returns **202** `{ status: "APPROVAL_REQUIRED", approvalId, approvalUrl, expiresAt, summary }`. The customer approves with a passkey; see [approvals](https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/approvals/). No transaction OTP is involved: the passkey is the consent. Send `localAmount` instead of `amount` to fix what the recipient receives.

When Rift's compliance gates are on for the environment, the route also requires merchant approval (`403`) and, once the customer passes the KYC-free volume limit, completed KYC (`400`, `code: "KYC_REQUIRED"`). `init` has the same gates.

#### Recipient shapes

| Recipient | `recipient` |
|---|---|
| Mobile money | `{ "type": "MOBILE", "accountIdentifier": "+254712345678", "institution": "Safaricom" }` |
| Till (Buy Goods) | `{ "type": "BUY_GOODS", "accountIdentifier": "123456" }` |
| Paybill | `{ "type": "PAYBILL", "accountIdentifier": "400200", "accountNumber": "ACC-001" }` |
| Bank | `{ "type": "BANK", "institution": "<bank name>", "bankCode": "<code>", "accountIdentifier": "" }` |

Take institution names and codes from `GET /v1/rails/{currency}/institutions`; do not hard-code them. Kenya bank transfers are paid through the bank's paybill with your account number as the reference; the account holder's name is looked up from the bank account itself. A saved beneficiary can replace `recipient`: pass `beneficiaryId`.

#### In the browser: two-phase

With passkeys on your domain there is no approval step:

```text
POST /v1/offramps/init       { token, amount | localAmount, currency, chain, recipient }
  → { success: true, data: { orderId, ticketId, hashToSign, allowCredentials, rpId, expiresAt,
                              transferAmount, fiatAmount, feeFiat, exchangeRate, … } }
passkey signs hashToSign     → authProof
POST /v1/offramps/finalize   { orderId, ticketId, authProof }       + X-Rift-Device
  → { success: true, data: { orderId, txHash, transactionCode, status, fiatAmount, currency } }
```

`init` routes and prices the order and enforces the per-transaction cap. `init` and `finalize` wrap errors as `{ success: false, error: <message>, code }`, unlike most routes; read `code`. See [two-phase signing](https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/two-phase-signing/) and [device binding](https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/device-binding/).

### Track settlement

```bash
curl https://sandbox.riftfi.com/v1/offramps/$ORDER_ID -H "Authorization: Bearer $CUSTOMER_TOKEN"
```

```json
{
  "id": "…",
  "status": "processing",
  "recipient": { "type": "MOBILE", "accountIdentifier": "+2547…", "accountName": "JANE W*** DOE" },
  "fiatAmount": "1290",
  "currency": "KES",
  "cryptoAmount": "10",
  "token": "USDC",
  "chain": "BASE",
  "fee": "12.9",
  "txHash": "0x…",
  "receiptNumber": null,
  "transactionCode": "…",
  "createdAt": "…",
  "updatedAt": "…"
}
```

Use the Rift `orderId` (from `init`, `finalize` or a ledger entry's `orderId`). `status` moves through `processing` to `completed`, or ends in `failed`, `refunding` / `refunded`, `expired` or `cancelled`. A compliance hold stays `processing`: **do not ask the customer to pay again**. `receiptNumber` carries the network receipt (an M-Pesa code, for example) once paid.

### Refunds

> Beta: Some failed payouts come back on their own (`refunding`, then `refunded`). Payouts on Rift-operated corridors (Tanzania, Ghana) are resolved by Rift operations. For the rest, the customer can refund.

A failed payout whose stablecoins already left the wallet can be returned to the customer, once. The ledger tells you which:

```json
{ "id": "…", "type": "offramp", "status": "failed", "orderId": "8a1f…", "refundable": true, … }
```

`refundable` is `true` only when the order is `failed`, can be returned by Rift, has an on-chain transaction hash and has not been refunded before. Then:

```bash
curl -X POST https://sandbox.riftfi.com/v1/offramps/$ORDER_ID/refund \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CUSTOMER_TOKEN" \
  -H "X-Rift-Device: $DEVICE_PROOF"
```

```json
{ "id": "8a1f…", "status": "refunding", "message": "Refund started" }
```

```ts
// refund.ts: find failed payouts the customer can refund, and refund one.
// The refund call is a money call: send it once, never retry it automatically.
const BASE_URL = process.env.RIFT_BASE_URL ?? "https://sandbox.riftfi.com";

interface LedgerEntry {
  id: string;
  type: string;
  status: string;
  amount: string;
  token: string;
  orderId?: string;
  refundable: boolean;
}

export async function refundableEntries(accessToken: string): Promise<LedgerEntry[]> {
  const res = await fetch(`${BASE_URL}/v1/ledger?type=offramp&limit=100`, {
    headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${accessToken}` },
  });
  if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`ledger failed: ${res.status}`);
  const { entries } = (await res.json()) as { entries: LedgerEntry[] };
  return entries.filter((e) => e.refundable && e.orderId);
}

/**
 * `deviceProof` is a fresh X-Rift-Device value from the customer's trusted
 * device (required once device binding is enforced).
 */
export async function refundPayout(accessToken: string, orderId: string, deviceProof?: string) {
  const path = `/v1/offramps/${encodeURIComponent(orderId)}/refund`;
  const res = await fetch(`${BASE_URL}${path}`, {
    method: "POST",
    headers: {
      Authorization: `Bearer ${accessToken}`,
      ...(deviceProof ? { "X-Rift-Device": deviceProof } : {}),
    },
  });
  const body = await res.json();
  if (res.ok) return body as { id: string; status: "refunding"; message: string };
  // 409 NOT_REFUNDABLE / REFUND_IN_PROGRESS, 400 REFUND_REJECTED: show the message.
  // 502 REFUND_PENDING_REVIEW: outcome unknown; Rift reviews it. Do not call again.
  throw Object.assign(new Error(body.message ?? body.error), { status: res.status, code: body.error });
}
```

| Response | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `200` `status: "refunding"` | The refund was accepted. The order and its ledger entry move to `refunding`, then `refunded`. |
| `404 ORDER_NOT_FOUND` | Not this customer's order. |
| `409 NOT_REFUNDABLE` | Not failed, not refundable through this endpoint, no transaction hash, or already refunded. |
| `409 REFUND_IN_PROGRESS` | Another refund request claimed the order first. |
| `400 REFUND_REJECTED` | The refund was declined. The order is back to `failed`; the message says why. |
| `502 REFUND_PENDING_REVIEW` | The outcome is unknown. The order stays claimed and Rift reviews it. **Do not call again.** |

Only the customer can refund their own order (customer token, plus a device proof once [device binding](https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/device-binding/) is enforced).

### Saved beneficiaries

> Beta: this feature is rolling out and may change.

Save recipients so customers do not retype them. Every endpoint is scoped to the signed-in customer.

| Endpoint | What it does |
|---|---|
| `GET /v1/beneficiaries?type=mobile` | List, most recently used first. |
| `POST /v1/beneficiaries` | Save. `201` when new, `200` with the existing row when already saved (deduped on type, identifier and bank code). |
| `PATCH /v1/beneficiaries/{id}` | Change `label`, `network` or `bankName`. The identifier is the identity and cannot change. |
| `DELETE /v1/beneficiaries/{id}` | Delete (`204`). |

```json
POST /v1/beneficiaries
{ "type": "mobile", "currency": "KES", "network": "Safaricom", "identifier": "+254712345678", "label": "Mum" }
```

- `type`: `wallet`, `mobile`, `till`, `paybill` or `bank`. Fiat types need `currency`; `bank` needs `bankCode`; `wallet` needs an EVM address.
- On save, fiat recipients get the same name lookup as payouts. **An unconfirmed name never blocks the save**: the beneficiary is stored with `accountName: null`.
- Pass `beneficiaryId` to `POST /v1/offramps` (fiat) or `POST /v1/transactions` (wallet) instead of the recipient. `useCount` and `lastUsedAt` update when the payment completes.
- Writes need a device proof once device binding is enforced.

### Errors

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `400 PAYOUT_ROUTE_UNAVAILABLE` | This currency can't be paid from that chain and token. Offer another chain or token. |
| `400 AMOUNT_OUT_OF_RANGE` | Over the per-transaction cap. |
| `400 AMOUNT_BELOW_MINIMUM` | Nigeria payout under 1 unit of the stablecoin. |
| `400 VALIDATION_UNSUPPORTED` | The name lookup is not available for that rail. Does not affect payouts. |
| `400 INVALID_BENEFICIARY` | `beneficiaryId` is not a fiat beneficiary. |
| `400 KYC_REQUIRED` (in `code`) | The customer must complete KYC to go past the KYC-free volume limit. |
| `403` merchant approval required | Compliance gates require merchant (KYB) approval for this customer. |
| `409 PASSKEY_SETUP_REQUIRED` | No passkey yet. |
| `404 ORDER_NOT_FOUND` / `410 TICKET_EXPIRED` | `finalize` after the order expired. Call `init` again. |
| `502 SUBMIT_FAILED` / `PAYOUT_FAILED` | Failure after submission. Look the order up before doing anything else; never resend automatically. |

The full list is on [errors](https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/errors/).

## Onramp

Source: https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/onramp/

> Beta: Onramp is off on an environment until Rift enables it there; until then every onramp route answers `404 ONRAMP_DISABLED`. The endpoints are in the [Core API reference](https://riftfi.com/docs/api/rift-wallet/operations/post_v1_onramps/) under Onramps (Beta).

Onramp turns local money into stablecoins in the customer's **own Safe**. The recipient is always the customer's wallet address; an onramp cannot be pointed anywhere else.

| Currency | The customer pays by | Delivers |
|---|---|---|
| KES, UGX | Approving a mobile-money prompt on their phone | USDC on Base, or USDT on Celo |
| TZS, GHS, MWK | Approving a mobile-money prompt on their phone (Rift-operated) | USDC on Base only |
| NGN | Bank transfer to a virtual account | USDC or USDT on Base, Polygon, BNB Chain or Ethereum |

Per-order limits and the liquidity check on Rift-operated corridors are on [payment corridors & limits](https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/payment-corridors/#limits).

### Identity verification

**Every onramp needs a verified identity first** ([`GET /v1/onramps/kyc`](https://riftfi.com/docs/api/rift-wallet/operations/get_v1_onramps_kyc/)), in every country. Rift reuses the customer's verified KYC session (matched by customer id or by the same email, phone or external id), so a verified customer never repeats it and you never collect identity data in a form.

```bash
curl "https://sandbox.riftfi.com/v1/onramps/kyc?currency=NGN" -H "Authorization: Bearer $CUSTOMER_TOKEN"
```

```json
{ "verified": true, "ready": false, "missing": ["idDocument (NGN needs BVN or NIN, 11 digits, issuerCountry NG)"], "kycUrl": "https://…/kyc?purpose=onramp" }
```

| Currency | Needs |
|---|---|
| KES, TZS, UGX, GHS, MWK | `verified: true` |
| NGN | `ready: true`: full name, date of birth (18 or over), an ID document with issuing country, and a BVN or NIN (11 digits, issued in NG). |

The response never contains the identity values themselves. When the requirement is not met, send the customer to `kycUrl`. Creating an order without it fails with:

```json
409 { "error": "ONRAMP_KYC_REQUIRED", "message": "Verify your identity to buy crypto", "missing": ["verification"], "kycUrl": "https://…" }
```

### Quote

```bash
curl "https://sandbox.riftfi.com/v1/onramps/quote?currency=KES&amount=1300&token=USDC&chain=BASE" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CUSTOMER_TOKEN"
```

```json
{
  "currency": "KES", "fiatAmount": "1300", "token": "USDC", "chain": "BASE",
  "cryptoAmount": "9.88", "rate": "129.5", "fee": "19.5",
  "expiresAt": "2026-11-11T09:01:00.000Z"
}
```

`amount` is the fiat amount; `token` defaults to USDC and `chain` to BASE. Quotes are indicative for 60 seconds; the order is priced again at creation. Out of range:

```json
400 { "error": "AMOUNT_OUT_OF_RANGE", "message": "We can only process up to 2,000,000 TZS right now. Try a smaller amount.",
      "min": 500, "max": 2000000, "currency": "TZS", "reason": "liquidity" }
```

`reason: "liquidity"` appears only for Tanzania, when Rift's USDC float is below the amount; `max` is what can be served now (0 when nothing can).

### Create the order

```bash
curl -X POST https://sandbox.riftfi.com/v1/onramps \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CUSTOMER_TOKEN" \
  -H "X-Rift-Device: $DEVICE_PROOF" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "currency": "KES", "fiatAmount": 1300, "token": "USDC", "chain": "BASE",
        "phone": "+254712345678", "mobileNetwork": "Safaricom" }'
```

```ts
const body = JSON.stringify({ currency: "KES", fiatAmount: 1300, token: "USDC", chain: "BASE", phone, mobileNetwork: "Safaricom" });
const res = await fetch("https://sandbox.riftfi.com/v1/onramps", {
  method: "POST",
  headers: {
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    Authorization: `Bearer ${accessToken}`,
    "X-Rift-Device": await deviceHeader("POST", "/v1/onramps", body), // see Device binding
  },
  body,
});
const order = await res.json(); // 201
```

**Mobile money (every currency except NGN).** Send `phone` (defaults to the customer's profile phone) and `mobileNetwork` (alias `network`). The customer gets a payment prompt on that phone. The order has `providerAccount: null` and `collection: { phone, network, prompt: true }`.

```json
201 {
  "id": "…", "status": "processing",
  "providerAccount": null, "collection": { "phone": "+254712345678", "network": "Safaricom", "prompt": true },
  "fiatAmount": "1300", "currency": "KES", "cryptoAmount": "9.88", "token": "USDC", "chain": "BASE",
  "rate": "129.5", "fee": "19.5", "txHash": null, "expiresAt": null, "createdAt": "…", "updatedAt": "…"
}
```

**Bank transfer (NGN).** Send `refundAccount { institution, accountIdentifier, accountName? }`: where the naira goes if the order fails. The order returns `providerAccount`; tell the customer to transfer **exactly** `amountToTransfer` before `validUntil`. A different amount or a late payment may not be matched.

```json
201 {
  "id": "…", "status": "awaiting_payment",
  "providerAccount": { "institution": "…", "accountIdentifier": "…", "accountName": "…",
                       "amountToTransfer": "15000", "currency": "NGN", "validUntil": "…" },
  "fiatAmount": "15000", "currency": "NGN", "cryptoAmount": "9.71", "token": "USDC", "chain": "BASE", …
}
```

Creating an order is a money call: send it once. If it times out, list the customer's orders (`GET /v1/onramps`) before creating another.

### Track it

`GET /v1/onramps/{id}` and `GET /v1/onramps?limit=50` (max 200) return orders in the shape above. Every onramp is also a [ledger](https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/ledger-and-statements/) `onramp` credit and emits `transaction.created` / `transaction.updated` [webhooks](https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/webhooks/).

| `status` | What it means | Show the customer |
|---|---|---|
| `awaiting_payment` | NGN order created; no transfer received yet. | Payment instructions and the deadline. |
| `processing` | Mobile-money prompt sent, or money received and in flight, including compliance holds. | "Payment received / waiting for confirmation." **Do not ask them to pay again.** |
| `completed` | Stablecoins delivered; `txHash` set. | Done. |
| `failed` / `cancelled` | The prompt was declined or failed, or the order failed. | Start a new order. |
| `expired` | NGN order not paid before `validUntil`. | Start a new order. |
| `refunding` / `refunded` | The fiat is being returned, or has been returned. | Refund in progress / done. |

Mobile-money orders start at `processing` (there is no separate "awaiting payment" step: the prompt is the payment). An order on a Rift-operated corridor (Tanzania, Ghana, Malawi) stays `processing` until Rift has released the USDC; if the release needs manual handling it stays `processing`, never `failed`, because the customer has already paid.

### Errors

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `404 ONRAMP_DISABLED` | Onramp is not enabled on this environment. |
| `409 ONRAMP_KYC_REQUIRED` | No usable verified identity; body has `missing` and `kycUrl`. |
| `409 PASSKEY_SETUP_REQUIRED` | The customer has no wallet yet. |
| `400 INVALID_AMOUNT` | `fiatAmount` is not a positive number. |
| `400 UNSUPPORTED_CURRENCY` / `UNSUPPORTED_TOKEN` / `UNSUPPORTED_CHAIN` / `UNSUPPORTED_PAIR` | Outside the corridors above (Kenya, Uganda: BASE+USDC or CELO+USDT; Tanzania, Ghana, Malawi: BASE+USDC). |
| `400 AMOUNT_OUT_OF_RANGE` | Outside the per-order limits, or above the USDC available on a Rift-operated corridor (`reason: "liquidity"`). Body has `min`, `max`, `currency`. |
| `400 PHONE_REQUIRED` / `NETWORK_REQUIRED` | Mobile-money order without a phone or mobile network. |
| `400 REFUND_ACCOUNT_REQUIRED` | NGN order without `refundAccount`. |
| `400` / `502` `*_ONRAMP_FAILED` / `*_COLLECT_FAILED` | The order could not be started; nothing was collected. Safe to try again. |
| `503 ONRAMP_UNAVAILABLE` / `NO_PROVIDER_AVAILABLE` | Corridor paused or no liquidity right now. Try later. |
| `400 KYC_REQUIRED` (in `code`) | Compliance gates on: past the KYC-free volume limit. |
| `401 DEVICE_PROOF_INVALID` / `403 DEVICE_NOT_TRUSTED` | Device binding enforced and the device proof is missing, invalid or from an untrusted device. |

## Rift Accounts

Source: https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/accounts/

> Beta: Rift Accounts are in beta. Open accounts and test small amounts first; tell us before you move volume.

A Rift Account is a local-currency account that belongs to your project. You **collect** money into it from mobile money, keep a balance, and **pay out** from it to mobile money, banks, tills and paybills. Each project gets one account per currency:

| Currency | Country | Collect from | Pay out to |
|---|---|---|---|
| `KES` | Kenya | M-Pesa (Safaricom), Airtel | Mobile money, bank, till, paybill |
| `TZS` | Tanzania | Vodacom, Halotel, Airtel, Yas / Tigo | Mobile money |
| `GHS` | Ghana | MTN, AirtelTigo, Telecel | Mobile money |
| `UGX` | Uganda | MTN, Airtel | Mobile money |
| `MWK` | Malawi | Airtel Money, TNM Mpamba | Mobile money |

### How your money stays separate

The money itself sits in Rift's settlement wallet for each currency. Rift runs a **double-entry ledger** on top of it, and every account has its own balance in that ledger. Many businesses can hold accounts in the same currency and their money never mixes:

- Every movement is written as balanced entries in the ledger. Money is never created or lost between accounts.
- A balance only changes inside one database transaction, together with its ledger entries. A payout either reserves the money or is refused. Two payouts can't both spend the same balance.
- Your API key only reaches your project's accounts. Another project's account ID returns `404`, so its balance can't even be read.
- Every day Rift checks that the total of all account balances is covered by the real settlement balance, and that Rift's own operating funds are kept apart from it, and that every ledger entry balances. If anything is off, a person is alerted before the next payout window.

#### Available and held

Each account shows two numbers:

- **`available`**: what you can pay out right now.
- **`held`**: money reserved for payouts that are on their way. When a payout completes, the held amount leaves the account. When it fails, the held amount goes back to `available`. Either way it happens exactly once.

### Authentication

Call these endpoints from your server with your **platform key**, the same key as the [Platform API](https://riftfi.com/docs/quickstarts/platform/), in one header:

```text
x-api-key: psk_live_…
```

(`Authorization: Bearer psk_live_…` works too.) Every `POST` that moves money also needs an **`Idempotency-Key`**: any unique string, such as a UUID. If a request times out, send it again with the **same key**. You get the original result back, with the header `Idempotent-Replayed: true`, and the money moves only once. If you reuse a key for a different request, you get `409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`.

The dashboard calls the same endpoints with your signed-in session.

### Fees

Rift charges **0.99%** on each collection and each payout, unless your agreement says otherwise. Your rate is on every account as `feeBps` (99 = 0.99%). The fee is shown in every response before and after the money moves:

- **Collection:** the payer pays `amount`. Your account receives `net` = `amount − fee`.
- **Payout:** the recipient gets exactly `amount`. Your account pays `total` = `amount + fee`.

Use the `preview` endpoints to show the fee (and the recipient's registered name) before you confirm. They don't move any money.

### Open an account

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.riftfi.com/v1/accounts \
  -H "x-api-key: $RIFT_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"currency":"TZS"}'
```

```json
{
  "id": "6f1c2b9e-1d4a-4d8e-9a43-0b7f3c5e2a10",
  "currency": "TZS",
  "reference": "RA-TZS-7K2Q",
  "status": "active",
  "available": "0.00",
  "held": "0.00",
  "feeBps": 99,
  "createdAt": "2026-11-14T08:00:00.000Z"
}
```

Opening the same currency again returns the existing account (`200`). Amounts are decimal strings. KES, TZS, UGX and MWK amounts are whole numbers; GHS allows two decimals.

### Collect from mobile money

The payer gets a prompt on their phone. The transaction stays `pending` until they approve it.

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.riftfi.com/v1/accounts/$ACCOUNT_ID/collections \
  -H "x-api-key: $RIFT_API_KEY" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: 3f0e2c1a-collect-order-123" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"amount":100000,"phone":"+255712345678","network":"Vodacom","reference":"order-123"}'
```

```json
{
  "id": "b0c4…",
  "accountId": "6f1c…",
  "type": "collection",
  "status": "pending",
  "currency": "TZS",
  "amount": "100000.00",
  "fee": "990.00",
  "net": "99010.00",
  "rail": "mobile",
  "counterparty": { "phone": "*********678", "network": "Vodacom", "accountName": null, "bank": null, "bankCode": null, "accountNumber": null, "till": null, "paybill": null },
  "reference": "order-123",
  "providerRef": "TZC1A2B3",
  "failureReason": null,
  "createdAt": "2026-11-14T08:01:00.000Z",
  "completedAt": null,
  "events": [{ "status": "pending", "at": "2026-11-14T08:01:00.000Z" }]
}
```

When the payer approves, the status becomes `completed` and `net` is added to `available`. If they decline or the prompt times out, the status becomes `failed` and nothing moves.

KES collections can pause briefly while Rift tops up collateral. While paused, they return `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`. Nothing is created; try again later.

### Pay out

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.riftfi.com/v1/accounts/$ACCOUNT_ID/disbursements \
  -H "x-api-key: $RIFT_API_KEY" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: 9a7d-payout-inv-881" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"amount":50000,"type":"mobile","phone":"+255712345678","network":"Vodacom","reference":"inv-881"}'
```

The response is the transaction with `status: "held"`, `fee` and `total`. Recipient fields by `type`:

| `type` | Fields | Currencies |
|---|---|---|
| `mobile` | `phone`, `network` | All |
| `bank` | `accountNumber`, `bankCode` (from `GET /v1/accounts/banks?currency=KES`) | KES |
| `till` | `till` | KES |
| `paybill` | `paybill`, `accountNumber` | KES |

If `available` doesn't cover `amount + fee`, you get `402 INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS` and nothing is reserved. If Rift can't pay out in that currency right now, you get `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` and nothing is reserved.

#### When the outcome is unclear

If the payment network doesn't answer clearly (for example, a timeout), Rift **does not send the payout again**. The transaction stays `held` while a person confirms with the network, then it becomes `completed` or `failed`. You never pay twice, and the reserved money is never lost.

### Statuses

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `pending` | Collection started; waiting for the payer. |
| `held` | Payout money is reserved and the payout is on its way. |
| `completed` | Done. Collections: `net` is in `available`. Payouts: the recipient was paid. |
| `failed` | Didn't happen. Payouts: the held amount is back in `available`. `failureReason` says why. |
| `reversed` | Reserved for corrections made by Rift. |

### Webhooks

Subscribe your [webhook endpoint](https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/webhooks/) to these events. `data` is the transaction object shown above.

| Event | When |
|---|---|
| `account.collection.completed` | The money arrived (`net` added to `available`). |
| `account.collection.failed` | The payer declined, or the prompt timed out. |
| `account.disbursement.completed` | The recipient was paid. |
| `account.disbursement.failed` | The payout failed; the held amount is back in `available`. |

Each event is sent once per transaction, even when Rift learns the result from more than one source.

### Transactions and statements

```bash
## Newest first; filter by status and type; follow nextCursor for more.
curl "https://api.riftfi.com/v1/accounts/$ACCOUNT_ID/transactions?limit=25&status=completed&type=disbursement" \
  -H "x-api-key: $RIFT_API_KEY"

## One transaction
curl https://api.riftfi.com/v1/accounts/transactions/$TXN_ID -H "x-api-key: $RIFT_API_KEY"

## Statement (UTC days; `to` includes the whole day). format=json or csv.
curl -OJ "https://api.riftfi.com/v1/accounts/$ACCOUNT_ID/statement?from=2026-11-01&to=2026-11-30&format=csv" \
  -H "x-api-key: $RIFT_API_KEY"
```

A list returns `{ "transactions": [...], "nextCursor": "…" | null }`. A statement includes the opening balance, every completed movement with a running balance, and the closing balance. Money that is only `held` shows up once the payout completes.

### TypeScript

```ts
const RIFT = "https://api.riftfi.com";
const headers = { "x-api-key": process.env.RIFT_API_KEY!, "Content-Type": "application/json" };

// Open (or fetch) the TZS account.
const account = await (await fetch(`${RIFT}/v1/accounts`, {
  method: "POST", headers, body: JSON.stringify({ currency: "TZS" }),
})).json();

// Show fee + recipient name before paying.
const preview = await (await fetch(`${RIFT}/v1/accounts/${account.id}/disbursements/preview`, {
  method: "POST", headers,
  body: JSON.stringify({ amount: 50000, type: "mobile", phone: "+255712345678", network: "Vodacom" }),
})).json(); // { amount, fee, total, available, enoughBalance, recipientName }

// Pay out. Keep the key: retry with the same one if the request times out.
const key = crypto.randomUUID();
const res = await fetch(`${RIFT}/v1/accounts/${account.id}/disbursements`, {
  method: "POST",
  headers: { ...headers, "Idempotency-Key": key },
  body: JSON.stringify({ amount: 50000, type: "mobile", phone: "+255712345678", network: "Vodacom", reference: "inv-881" }),
});
if (res.status === 402) throw new Error("Not enough balance for amount + fee");
const payout = await res.json(); // status "held" → webhook account.disbursement.completed | failed
```

### Endpoints

| Method | Path | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `POST` | `/v1/accounts` | Open the account for `{ currency }` (returns the existing one if already open). |
| `GET` | `/v1/accounts` | Your accounts with `available` and `held`. |
| `GET` | `/v1/accounts/{id}` | One account. |
| `GET` | `/v1/accounts/banks?currency=KES` | Banks for `type: "bank"` payouts. |
| `POST` | `/v1/accounts/{id}/collections` | Collect from mobile money (`Idempotency-Key`). |
| `POST` | `/v1/accounts/{id}/collections/preview` | Fee and net, without moving money. |
| `POST` | `/v1/accounts/{id}/disbursements` | Pay out (`Idempotency-Key`). |
| `POST` | `/v1/accounts/{id}/disbursements/preview` | Fee, total and recipient name, without moving money. |
| `GET` | `/v1/accounts/{id}/transactions` | `?cursor=&limit=&status=&type=` |
| `GET` | `/v1/accounts/transactions/{txnId}` | One transaction. |
| `GET` | `/v1/accounts/{id}/statement` | `?from=YYYY-MM-DD&to=YYYY-MM-DD&format=csv\|json` |

Errors always look like `{ "error": "INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS", "message": "…" }`. See [errors](https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/errors/).

### Compliance

You attest that your end users are KYC'd under your platform terms; Rift runs KYB on your business before accounts go live. Rift can freeze an account (`status: "frozen"`). A frozen account refuses new collections and payouts, but money already on its way still settles.

## Own-wallet ramps

Source: https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/own-wallet-ramps/

> Beta: Own-wallet ramps are in beta. Start with small amounts.

Use these endpoints when the stablecoins are in **your own wallet** (a treasury, an exchange hot wallet, or a wallet you already run), not in a Rift customer wallet. Authenticate exactly like [Rift Accounts](https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/accounts/): one header, `x-api-key: psk_live_…`, from your server.

### Offramp: your USDC → local money

Three steps: **quote**, **send**, **submit**.

#### 1. Quote

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.riftfi.com/v1/ramps/offramp/quotes \
  -H "x-api-key: $RIFT_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "currency": "KES",
    "amount": 5000,
    "chain": "BASE",
    "token": "USDC",
    "fromAddress": "0xYourWallet…",
    "recipient": { "type": "mobile", "phone": "+254712345678", "network": "Safaricom" }
  }'
```

```json
{
  "quoteId": "1d6b…",
  "currency": "KES",
  "depositAddress": "0x8005ee53E57aB11E11eAA4EFe07Ee3835Dc02F98",
  "sendAmount": "39.147287",
  "token": "USDC",
  "chain": "BASE",
  "rate": "129",
  "fee": "50.00",
  "recipientGets": "5000.00",
  "recipient": { "type": "mobile", "phone": "*********678", "network": "Safaricom", "accountName": "JOHN KAMAU" },
  "expiresAt": "2026-11-14T08:15:00.000Z"
}
```

- Send **either** `amount` (what the recipient gets, in local currency) **or** `usdcAmount` (what you send).
- `recipient` takes the same fields as [account payouts](https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/accounts/#pay-out): `type` is `mobile`, `bank`, `till` or `paybill`. Bank, till and paybill are Kenya only.
- `fromAddress` is optional, but **send it**. Rift then only accepts a transfer that comes from that wallet, so nobody else can claim your deposit.
- `fee` is Rift's fee in local currency, already included in `sendAmount`.
- Supported chains: `BASE`, `CELO`, `POLYGON`, `ARBITRUM`. For KES, UGX and MWK the token must be USDC on Base. For TZS and GHS, USDC or USDT.

If the corridor can't pay out right now, the quote returns `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`. If the amount is above the per-transaction cap, it returns `400 AMOUNT_OUT_OF_RANGE` with the `max`.

#### 2. Send

From `fromAddress`, transfer **at least `sendAmount`** of `token` on `chain` to `depositAddress` **before `expiresAt`** (15 minutes). Use a plain ERC-20 transfer.

#### 3. Submit

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.riftfi.com/v1/ramps/offramp/quotes/$QUOTE_ID/submit \
  -H "x-api-key: $RIFT_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"txHash":"0xabc…"}'
```

Rift reads the transaction on-chain and checks all of this before paying anything:

- it succeeded and is mined;
- it moved the quoted token, from `fromAddress`, to `depositAddress`;
- the amount is at least `sendAmount`;
- it was sent after the quote was created;
- the hash has never been used for any other payout.

| Response | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `201` order, `status: "processing"` | Verified. The payout is on its way. |
| `200` same order | You already submitted this hash for this quote. Safe to retry. |
| `409 TX_NOT_CONFIRMED` | Not mined yet. Submit again in a few seconds. |
| `400 DEPOSIT_NOT_FOUND` / `DEPOSIT_TOO_SMALL` / `DEPOSIT_BEFORE_QUOTE` | The transaction doesn't match the quote. |
| `409 TX_ALREADY_USED` / `QUOTE_ALREADY_USED` | That hash or quote was already used. |

How the recipient is paid depends on the country, but the API is the same:

- **Tanzania, Ghana:** the deposit goes to Rift's wallet and the recipient is paid from Rift's local float. If the float is being topped up, the order waits and pays as soon as it can.
- **Kenya, Uganda, Malawi:** the deposit goes to the settlement address in the quote, and Rift pays the recipient once your transaction confirms.

#### Track the order

```bash
curl https://api.riftfi.com/v1/ramps/orders/$ORDER_ID -H "x-api-key: $RIFT_API_KEY"
```

```json
{ "id": "7a2e…", "direction": "offramp", "status": "completed", "currency": "KES",
  "amount": "5000.00", "fee": "50.00", "cryptoAmount": "39.147287", "token": "USDC", "chain": "BASE",
  "quoteId": "1d6b…", "depositTxHash": "0xabc…", "recipient": { "phone": "*********678" },
  "failureReason": null, "createdAt": "…", "completedAt": "…" }
```

`status` is `processing`, `completed` or `failed`. If a payout fails after your deposit arrived, Rift support contacts you to pay it again or refund it. If the payment network doesn't answer clearly, Rift never pays twice: the order stays `processing` until a person confirms the outcome.

### Onramp: mobile money → USDC at any address

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.riftfi.com/v1/ramps/onramp \
  -H "x-api-key: $RIFT_API_KEY" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: 5c1d-onramp-42" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"currency":"KES","amount":1000,"phone":"+254712345678","network":"Safaricom","toAddress":"0xYourWallet…","chain":"BASE","token":"USDC"}'
```

The payer gets a prompt on their phone. Once they approve, USDC on Base goes to `toAddress`, and the order becomes `completed` with `releaseTxHash`.

- **Kenya, Uganda:** the money is collected and the USDC is sent once it clears.
- **Tanzania, Ghana, Malawi:** Rift collects the money and sends the USDC from its payout vault on Base, exactly once. If Rift's USDC is low, the request returns `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` before anything is collected.

`Idempotency-Key` is required. Retrying with the same key returns the same order.

### TypeScript

```ts
const RIFT = "https://api.riftfi.com";
const headers = { "x-api-key": process.env.RIFT_API_KEY!, "Content-Type": "application/json" };

const quote = await (await fetch(`${RIFT}/v1/ramps/offramp/quotes`, {
  method: "POST", headers,
  body: JSON.stringify({
    currency: "KES", amount: 5000, chain: "BASE", token: "USDC", fromAddress: wallet.address,
    recipient: { type: "mobile", phone: "+254712345678", network: "Safaricom" },
  }),
})).json();

// Send quote.sendAmount USDC to quote.depositAddress (ethers v5 shown).
const usdc = new ethers.Contract(USDC_BASE, ["function transfer(address,uint256) returns (bool)"], wallet);
const tx = await usdc.transfer(quote.depositAddress, ethers.utils.parseUnits(quote.sendAmount, 6));
await tx.wait();

let res;
do {
  res = await fetch(`${RIFT}/v1/ramps/offramp/quotes/${quote.quoteId}/submit`, {
    method: "POST", headers, body: JSON.stringify({ txHash: tx.hash }),
  });
  if (res.status === 409 && (await res.clone().json()).error === "TX_NOT_CONFIRMED") await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 3000));
  else break;
} while (true);
const order = await res.json(); // then ramp.offramp.completed | failed
```

### Webhooks

| Event | When |
|---|---|
| `ramp.offramp.completed` | The recipient was paid. |
| `ramp.offramp.failed` | The payout failed; Rift support follows up on your deposit. |
| `ramp.onramp.completed` | USDC was sent to `toAddress`. |
| `ramp.onramp.failed` | The payer declined, or the collection failed. Nothing was sent. |

`data` is the order object. Set up endpoints in [webhooks](https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/webhooks/).

### Compliance

You attest that the people you pay and collect from are KYC'd under your platform terms. Rift runs KYB on your business.

## Liquidity providers (own wallet)

Source: https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/liquidity-providers/

> Beta: The LP pool ("Rift Yield") is in beta. Read the LP terms (`GET /v1/lp/terms`) before you deposit.

Liquidity providers (LPs) put USDC or USDT into the pool that funds Rift's local payouts, and earn a share of the fees on the volume it serves. If you hold stablecoins in **your own wallet**, you don't need a Rift account: you sign in with that wallet.

All endpoints live under `/v1/lp`.

### 1. Look at the pool (public)

```bash
curl https://api.riftfi.com/v1/lp/pool
```

The response includes `totalUsd`, `providers`, 30-day `volume30dUsd` and `lpFees30dUsd`, an estimated APY (`estApy`, with the formula in `estApyNote`), the `depositAddress`, supported `chains` and `assets`, `lockDays`, `lpFeeBps` and the current `termsVersion`. `estApy` is an estimate from the last 30 days, not a promise, and it can be zero.

`GET /v1/lp/pool/activity` lists recent anonymous pool usage. `GET /v1/lp/terms` returns the versioned LP terms.

### 2. Sign in with your wallet (SIWE)

```bash
## Get a message to sign (valid for 10 minutes, single use)
curl -X POST https://api.riftfi.com/v1/lp/auth/nonce \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"address":"0xYourWallet…"}'
## → { "message": "lp.riftfi.com wants you to sign in…", "nonce": "…", "expiresAt": "…" }

## Sign `message` with the wallet (personal_sign), then:
curl -X POST https://api.riftfi.com/v1/lp/auth/verify \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"address":"0xYourWallet…","message":"<the exact message>","signature":"0x…"}'
## → { "token": "…", "expiresIn": 7200, "provider": { "id": "…", "walletAddress": "0x…" } }
```

Signing only proves you own the wallet. It doesn't move funds or approve any transaction. Send the token as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on the calls below. It lasts 2 hours.

```ts

const RIFT = "https://api.riftfi.com";
const wallet = new ethers.Wallet(process.env.LP_PRIVATE_KEY!);
const post = (path: string, body: unknown, token?: string) =>
  fetch(`${RIFT}${path}`, {
    method: "POST",
    headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json", ...(token ? { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` } : {}) },
    body: JSON.stringify(body),
  }).then((r) => r.json());

const { message } = await post("/v1/lp/auth/nonce", { address: wallet.address });
const { token } = await post("/v1/lp/auth/verify", { address: wallet.address, message, signature: await wallet.signMessage(message) });
```

### 3. Accept the terms

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.riftfi.com/v1/lp/terms/accept \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $LP_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"version":"<termsVersion from /v1/lp/pool>"}'
```

### 4. Deposit

Send USDC or USDT **from your signed-in wallet** to the pool's `depositAddress`, on one of the listed chains (`BASE`, `ETHEREUM`, `POLYGON`, `ARBITRUM`). Then tell Rift about it:

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.riftfi.com/v1/lp/deposits/crypto \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $LP_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"chain":"BASE","txHash":"0xabc…"}'
```

Rift checks the transfer on-chain. A transfer sent from another wallet is refused (`403 SENDER_MISMATCH`), and a hash can only be recorded once (`409 ALREADY_RECORDED`). Deposits sent from your registered wallet are also picked up automatically, even if you forget this call.

You can also deposit local money with mobile money: `POST /v1/lp/deposits/fiat` `{ currency, amount, phone, network }` (KES, UGX, TZS, GHS, MWK).
