### 5. Track and withdraw

| Method | Path | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/v1/lp/me` | Your dashboard: principal, accrued earnings, what you can withdraw now. |
| `GET` | `/v1/lp/me/accruals?cursor=&limit=` | Earnings per pool-funded order. |
| `GET` | `/v1/lp/me/withdrawals` | Your withdrawal requests. |
| `POST` | `/v1/lp/withdrawals` | `{ amountUsd, chain, asset, toAddress }`: request a withdrawal. |

Deposits are locked for `lockDays` from when they arrive. A withdrawal above what you can withdraw now returns `400 EXCEEDS_WITHDRAWABLE` with `withdrawableUsd`. Withdrawals and monthly earnings payouts are reviewed and paid by Rift, and you see the payment `txHash` in `/v1/lp/me/withdrawals`.

### Errors

Errors look like `{ "error": "TERMS_NOT_ACCEPTED", "message": "…" }`. Deposits or withdrawals can be paused for maintenance (`503 DEPOSITS_PAUSED` / `WITHDRAWALS_PAUSED`).

### Related

- [Own-wallet ramps](https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/own-wallet-ramps/): cash out or buy USDC from your own wallet.
- [Rift Accounts](https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/accounts/): local-currency accounts for your business.

## Swaps & bridges

Source: https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/swaps-and-bridges/

---
title: Swaps & bridges
description: Move stablecoins across chains between chains, and run swaps or any contract call as a passkey-signed UserOperation from the customer's Safe.
---



> Not yet verified end to end: Written from the SDK and API source; the swap path (aggregator calldata through the Safe) has not been exercised end-to-end here.


### Bridges

The customer's Safe has the same address on every chain, so by default a bridge sends funds to **their own Safe** on the destination chain.

```ts
const routes = await rift.bridge.getRoutes();                  // GET /v1/bridge/routes
const quote = await rift.bridge.getQuote({                      // POST /v1/bridge/quotes
  sourceChain: "BASE", destinationChain: "POLYGON", token: "USDC", amount: "25",
});
```

**From a server** (approval request):

```ts
const res = await rift.bridge.execute({
  sourceChain: "BASE", destinationChain: "POLYGON", token: "USDC", amount: "25",
});
if (isApprovalRequired(res)) notifyCustomer(res.approvalUrl);
```

**Two-phase** (passkeys on your domain): `rift.bridge.previewTransfer({ sourceChain, destChain, token, amount, recipient? })` pulls a fresh bridge quote and builds the approve + deposit calls; sign `hashToSign` and submit with `rift.signer.submitPreparedUserOp({ ticketId, authProof })`.

Gas is paid on the source chain; the destination fill comes from bridge relayers. Quotes move with liquidity, so quote close to execution.

### Swaps and contract calls

There is no dedicated swap endpoint. A swap is a contract call from the customer's Safe, built from your swap aggregator's quote and executed as a UserOperation. The same path runs any contract call.

```ts
// One call built from your swap aggregator's quote
const call = { to: routerAddress, value: "0", data: swapCalldata };

// Server: approval request
const res = await rift.signer.sendTransaction({ chain: "BASE", transactionData: call });

// Browser, passkeys on your domain: two-phase
const preview = await rift.signer.previewUserOp({ chain: "BASE", transactionData: call });
const authProof = await createPasskeyAuthProof(getHashToSign(preview), { rpId, allowCredentials: preview.allowCredentials });
await rift.signer.submitPreparedUserOp({ ticketId: preview.ticketId, authProof });
```

- The approval `summary` describes the call; show the customer what the swap does in your own UI as well.
- `transactionData` takes **one call** per operation. If the router needs an ERC-20 allowance first, send the `approve` as its own operation before the swap (two approvals for the customer), or use a route that does not need a separate allowance.
- `rift.defi.swap()` is deprecated; its endpoint is no longer served.

### Message signatures

`rift.signer.previewMessage({ chain, message })` (or `typedData`) → passkey → `rift.signer.submitMessage({ ticketId, authProof })` returns an ERC-1271 signature from the Safe (ERC-6492-wrapped when the Safe is not deployed on that chain). `rift.signer.signMessage()` without a proof returns an approval request.

## WalletConnect

Source: https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/walletconnect/

---
title: WalletConnect
description: Let customers use their Rift Safe with any WalletConnect v2 dApp. Every dApp request is approved with a passkey.
---



> Not yet verified end to end: Written from the SDK and API source; not yet exercised end-to-end against a live dApp session.


A customer can pair their Safe with any dApp that supports WalletConnect v2. Requests from the dApp (`eth_sendTransaction`, `personal_sign`, typed data) queue in Rift until the customer approves them with a passkey.

### Pair

The customer scans or pastes the dApp's `wc:` URI in your app:

```ts
const session = await rift.walletConnect.pair({ uri: "wc:…", chain: "BASE" });
// { success, topic, smartWalletAddress, chain, chainId }
```

`POST /v1/wallet-connect/pairings` over HTTP. The dApp sees the customer's Safe address.

### Handle requests

```ts
const { data: requests } = await rift.walletConnect.getRequests(); // pending dApp requests
```

Approve one of two ways:

**Approval request** (server, or the widget handles the passkey):

```ts
const res = await rift.walletConnect.approveRequest(requestId);
// 202 → { status: "APPROVAL_REQUIRED", approvalId, approvalUrl, … }
```

**Two-phase** (passkeys on your domain):

```ts
const preview = await rift.walletConnect.previewRequest(requestId);
const authProof = await createPasskeyAuthProof(getHashToSign(preview), {
  rpId: "app.example.com",
  allowCredentials: preview.allowCredentials,
});
await rift.walletConnect.approveRequest(requestId, { ticketId: preview.ticketId, authProof });
```

Reject with `rift.walletConnect.rejectRequest(id)`.

### What gets signed

- **`eth_sendTransaction`** becomes a UserOperation through the Safe. Gas follows your [gas policy](https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/gas-sponsorship/); with customer-pays, gas is taken in the customer's stablecoin.
- **`personal_sign` and typed data** are signed by the Safe as an ERC-1271 contract signature. If the Safe is not deployed on that chain yet, the signature is wrapped as ERC-6492 so dApps using a 6492-aware verifier (such as viem's `verifyMessage`) still accept it.
- **`eth_signTransaction`** (a raw EOA transaction) is not possible: there is no EOA key.

### Sessions

```ts
await rift.walletConnect.getSessions();
await rift.walletConnect.disconnectSession(topic);
```

Show customers their connected dApps and let them disconnect. Every request still needs their passkey, but fewer connected dApps means fewer requests to judge.

# Guides: data and events


## Ledger & statements

Source: https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/ledger-and-statements/

> Beta: this feature is rolling out and may change.

Every customer transaction is recorded once, in one ledger: transfers in and out, payouts, onramps, swaps, bridges, WalletConnect transactions, payment links and fees. You read it three ways:

| Who | Endpoint | Auth |
|---|---|---|
| The customer (your app on their behalf) | `GET /v1/ledger` | Customer token |
| Your institution, one customer | `GET /v1/platform/customers/{id}/ledger` | Platform key `psk_…`, server-side |
| Your institution, everyone | `GET /v1/platform/ledger?format=json\|csv` | Platform key `psk_…`, server-side |

### Ledger entry

```json
{
  "id": "…",
  "createdAt": "2026-11-10T09:12:33.000Z",
  "updatedAt": "2026-11-10T09:13:02.000Z",
  "type": "offramp",
  "direction": "debit",
  "status": "completed",
  "providerStatus": "COMPLETE",
  "amount": "10",
  "token": "USDC",
  "chain": "BASE",
  "fiatAmount": "1290",
  "fiatCurrency": "KES",
  "fee": "12.9",
  "feeToken": "KES",
  "counterparty": { "phone": "+2547…", "accountName": "JANE W*** DOE", "receiptNumber": "TKA1B2C3D4" },
  "reference": "…",
  "txHash": "0x…",
  "orderId": "8a1f…",
  "refundable": false
}
```

- `type`: `onramp`, `offramp`, `transfer_out`, `transfer_in`, `swap`, `bridge`, `walletconnect`, `payment_link`, `fee`, `other`. Any other value is `400 INVALID_REQUEST`.
- `direction`: `credit` or `debit`.
- `status`: the order vocabulary (`awaiting_payment`, `processing`, `completed`, `refunding`, `refunded`, `expired`, `cancelled`, `failed`); the raw network value is in `providerStatus`.
- `counterparty` holds whichever applies: `address`, `phone`, `bankName` + `accountNumber`, `accountName`, `till`, `paybill`, and `receiptNumber` (the network receipt, such as an M-Pesa code).
- `orderId` (payout entries): the Rift order id for [`GET /v1/offramps/{id}`](https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/offramp/#track-settlement) and refunds.
- `refundable`: `true` on a failed payout the customer can [refund](https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/offramp/#refunds); always present, `false` otherwise.
- Optional fields (`fiatAmount`, `fiatCurrency`, `fee`, `feeToken`, `reference`, `txHash`, `orderId`) are omitted when empty rather than sent as `null`.

### Filtering and paging

Filter with `from` and `to` (ISO 8601, both inclusive) and `type`; page with `cursor` → `nextCursor` (`null` on the last page). Entries are newest first. `limit` defaults to 50 on the customer ledgers (max 500) and 100 on the platform ledger (max 500 as JSON, 10,000 as CSV). The platform ledger also filters by `status` and `customerId`, and each row carries the customer's `consent` flags.

```bash
curl "https://sandbox.riftfi.com/v1/ledger?type=offramp&from=2026-11-01T00:00:00Z&to=2026-11-30T23:59:59.999Z" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CUSTOMER_TOKEN"
```

> **End dates**
A date-only `to` (`2026-11-10`) is read as **00:00:00 UTC** on that day, so it leaves out that day's transactions. To include the whole day send `to=2026-11-10T23:59:59.999Z`, or the next day's date. The same applies to statements and the platform ledgers.

### Reconciliation

- Match your payment records on `txHash`, `reference`, `orderId` or the approval's `result.transactionHash`.
- Entries change status as settlement progresses. Re-read entries that are not final, or subscribe to `transaction.updated` [webhooks](https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/webhooks/).
- `GET /v1/platform/ledger?format=csv` exports everything for a period in one file.

### Customer statements

A customer can request their own statement, by email or download, as CSV or PDF. It needs a fresh passkey signature, so nobody holding only their session can pull it.

1. `POST /v1/statements/challenge` → `{ challengeId, hashToSign, rpId, allowCredentials, allowCredentialEntries, expiresAt }` (single use, 5 minutes).
2. The passkey signs `hashToSign`.
3. `POST /v1/statements` `{ challengeId, authProof, from, to, format, delivery }`, with an `X-Rift-Device` proof once [device binding](https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/device-binding/) is enforced. `to` defaults to now, `format` to `pdf`, `delivery` to `download`. The challenge is consumed by any attempt, successful or not.

```ts
// statement.ts (Beta): the customer signs for their own statement.
import { createPasskeyAuthProof } from "@rift-finance/wallet";
import { deviceHeader } from "./device-binding";

const BASE_URL = "https://sandbox.riftfi.com";

interface StatementChallenge {
  challengeId: string;
  hashToSign: string;
  rpId: string;
  allowCredentials: string[];
  expiresAt: string;
}

/** `to` is inclusive: pass an end-of-day timestamp, e.g. "2026-11-30T23:59:59.999Z". */
export async function emailStatement(accessToken: string, from: string, to: string) {
  const headers = { "Content-Type": "application/json", Authorization: `Bearer ${accessToken}` };

  const challengeRes = await fetch(`${BASE_URL}/v1/statements/challenge`, { method: "POST", headers });
  const challenge = (await challengeRes.json()) as StatementChallenge;

  const authProof = await createPasskeyAuthProof(challenge.hashToSign, {
    rpId: challenge.rpId,
    allowCredentials: challenge.allowCredentials,
  });

  // Serialise once: the device proof signs these exact bytes.
  const body = JSON.stringify({ challengeId: challenge.challengeId, authProof, from, to, format: "pdf", delivery: "email" });
  const res = await fetch(`${BASE_URL}/v1/statements`, {
    method: "POST",
    headers: { ...headers, "X-Rift-Device": await deviceHeader("POST", "/v1/statements", body) },
    body,
  });
  return (await res.json()) as { status: "sent"; to: string }; // `to` is masked
}
```

- `delivery: "email"` → `{ "status": "sent", "to": "a***@example.com" }`, sent to the customer's notification email (or their account email). `409 NO_EMAIL` if they have none.
- `delivery: "download"` → the file itself in the response body (`Content-Disposition: attachment`).
- Rate limit: 5 statements per hour per customer (`429 RATE_LIMITED`).

Columns: date (UTC and EAT), type, direction, description, counterparty, amount, token, network, fiat amount and currency, fee, status, reference, transaction hash; opening and closing totals per token for the period.

#### Statements for your institution

`GET /v1/platform/customers/{id}/statement?from&to&format=csv|pdf` returns the same statement for one customer with your platform key, for servicing and support. Using that data beyond operating the account needs the customer's [consent](https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/customer-history-credit/).

## Customer history for credit

Source: https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/customer-history-credit/

> Beta: this feature is rolling out and may change.

A Rift Wallets customer's ledger is a complete, timestamped record of money in and out, with on-chain hashes for every crypto leg and payment references for every fiat leg. Lenders can use it to assess income regularity, cash-flow and repayment capacity, **only with the customer's consent**.

### Record consent first

Ask the customer in your own product (with your own terms), then record it from your server with a platform key (`psk_…`):

```json
POST /v1/platform/customers/{id}/consents
{
  "purpose": "credit_scoring",
  "grantedAt": "2026-11-10T09:00:00Z",
  "evidence": "terms-v3 accepted in app, session 7f2c…"
}
```

- `purpose` is `credit_scoring` or `statements`.
- `evidence` is your reference for the consent record; keep the full record on your side.
- List with `GET /v1/platform/customers/{id}/consents`; revoke with `DELETE /v1/platform/customers/{id}/consents/{consentId}` the moment the customer withdraws it.

### Read only consenting customers

Every customer and platform-ledger row carries `consent: { credit_scoring: boolean }`:

```ts
// GET /v1/platform/ledger?from=2026-05-01T00:00:00Z&to=2026-11-01T00:00:00Z
const rows = page.entries.filter((e) => e.consent?.credit_scoring);
```

Filter on it **every time**, not once. A customer who revokes consent must drop out of your next scoring run.

### Signals in the ledger

| Signal | From |
|---|---|
| Inflows and their regularity | `transfer_in` and `onramp` credits, by `createdAt` |
| Outflows to real-world payees | `offramp` debits with `counterparty` (mobile, bank, till, paybill) |
| Balances over time | Running totals per token, or `GET /v1/platform/customers/{id}` for current balances |
| Verification | `txHash` on-chain; `reference` for the fiat leg |
| Identity confidence | `kycStatus` on the customer |

### Obligations stay yours

Rift records and serves the data; you decide how it is used. Make sure your consent wording, retention, adverse-action notices and data-protection obligations meet the rules where you lend, and revoke access promptly when consent ends.

## Webhooks

Source: https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/webhooks/

---
title: Webhooks
description: Receive signed transaction, customer and approval events. Verify the Rift-Signature header in Node or Python.
---




> Beta: Platform webhooks are rolling out. Where they are not enabled on your environment yet, poll `GET /v1/approvals/{id}` and the ledger.


### Register an endpoint

Webhook management is part of the [Platform API](https://riftfi.com/docs/api/own-wallet/): call it from your server with a platform key (`X-API-Key: psk_…`), or use the dashboard.

```json
POST /v1/platform/webhooks
{ "url": "https://api.example.com/webhooks/rift",
  "events": ["transaction.created", "transaction.updated", "customer.created", "approval.created", "approval.updated"] }

201 Created
{ "id": "…", "url": "…", "events": [ … ], "secret": "…", "createdAt": "…" }
```

**`secret` (`whsec_…`) is shown once.** Store it in your secret manager. Manage endpoints with `GET /v1/platform/webhooks`, `DELETE /v1/platform/webhooks/{id}`, send a test with `POST /v1/platform/webhooks/{id}/test`, and inspect attempts with `GET /v1/platform/webhooks/{id}/deliveries`.

### Events

| Event | When |
|---|---|
| `customer.created` | A new customer signed up through your project. |
| `transaction.created` | A ledger entry was recorded. |
| `transaction.updated` | A ledger entry changed status (for example `processing` → `completed`). |
| `approval.created` | An approval request was created for one of your customers. |
| `approval.updated` | An approval became `approved`, `rejected`, `expired` or `failed`. |
| `account.collection.completed` / `account.collection.failed` | A [Rift Accounts](https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/accounts/) collection finished. |
| `account.disbursement.completed` / `account.disbursement.failed` | A Rift Accounts payout finished (a failed payout's hold is back in `available`). |
| `ramp.offramp.completed` / `ramp.offramp.failed` | An [own-wallet](https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/own-wallet-ramps/) offramp finished. |
| `ramp.onramp.completed` / `ramp.onramp.failed` | An own-wallet onramp finished. |

Every delivery is a `POST` with a JSON body:

```json
{ "id": "evt_…", "type": "approval.updated", "createdAt": "2026-11-10T09:14:02Z", "data": { … } }
```

### Verify the signature

Each delivery carries:

```text
Rift-Signature: t=1794306242,v1=b3aa4b14c715cba063ecce6a6a7982585a2c4e400ce71ed835eba4e4c36c8425
```

`v1` is the hex HMAC-SHA256 of `"<t>.<raw body>"` keyed with your endpoint secret. To verify:

1. Read the **raw** body bytes. Re-serialising parsed JSON changes the bytes and breaks the signature.
2. Compute the HMAC and compare in constant time.
3. Reject timestamps outside a tolerance window (5 minutes below) to stop replays.


  
**Node (TypeScript)**

    ```ts
// verify.ts (Beta): verify a Rift-Signature header on a platform webhook.
//   Rift-Signature: t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256("<t>.<raw body>", secret)>
// Use the RAW request body bytes, before any JSON parsing.
import { createHmac, timingSafeEqual } from "node:crypto";

const TOLERANCE_SECONDS = 300;

export function verifyRiftSignature(rawBody: Buffer, header: string | undefined, secret: string): boolean {
  if (!header) return false;
  const parts = new Map(
    header.split(",").map((kv) => {
      const i = kv.indexOf("=");
      return [kv.slice(0, i).trim(), kv.slice(i + 1).trim()] as const;
    })
  );
  const t = Number(parts.get("t"));
  const v1 = (parts.get("v1") ?? "").toLowerCase();
  if (!Number.isInteger(t) || !/^[0-9a-f]{64}$/.test(v1)) return false;
  if (Math.abs(Date.now() / 1000 - t) > TOLERANCE_SECONDS) return false; // replay window

  const expected = createHmac("sha256", secret).update(`${t}.`).update(rawBody).digest("hex");
  return timingSafeEqual(Buffer.from(expected, "utf8"), Buffer.from(v1, "utf8"));
}

type RiftEventType =
  | "transaction.created"
  | "transaction.updated"
  | "customer.created"
  | "approval.created"
  | "approval.updated";

// Express: app.post("/webhooks/rift", express.raw({ type: "application/json" }), (req, res) => {
//   res.sendStatus(handleRiftWebhook(req.body, req.get("Rift-Signature")));
// });
export function handleRiftWebhook(rawBody: Buffer, signature: string | undefined): number {
  if (!verifyRiftSignature(rawBody, signature, process.env.RIFT_WEBHOOK_SECRET!)) return 400;
  const event = JSON.parse(rawBody.toString("utf8")) as {
    id: string;
    type: RiftEventType;
    createdAt: string;
    data: Record<string, unknown>;
  };
  // Deliveries are retried (up to 5 attempts): de-duplicate on event.id,
  // and answer 2xx quickly. Do slow work after acknowledging.
  console.log(event.type, event.id);
  return 200;
}
```
  
  
**Python**

    ```python
## verify.py (Beta): verify a Rift-Signature header on a platform webhook.
##   Rift-Signature: t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256("<t>.<raw body>", secret)>
## Use the RAW request body bytes, before any JSON parsing.
import hashlib
import hmac
import time
from typing import Optional

TOLERANCE_SECONDS = 300

def verify_rift_signature(raw_body: bytes, header: Optional[str], secret: str) -> bool:
    if not header:
        return False
    parts = dict(kv.strip().split("=", 1) for kv in header.split(",") if "=" in kv)
    try:
        t = int(parts.get("t", ""))
    except ValueError:
        return False
    v1 = parts.get("v1", "").lower()
    if abs(time.time() - t) > TOLERANCE_SECONDS:  # replay window
        return False
    expected = hmac.new(secret.encode(), f"{t}.".encode() + raw_body, hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
    return hmac.compare_digest(expected, v1)

## Flask:
#
##   @app.post("/webhooks/rift")
##   def rift_webhook():
##       if not verify_rift_signature(request.get_data(), request.headers.get("Rift-Signature"), SECRET):
##           abort(400)
##       event = request.get_json()  # { id, type, createdAt, data }; de-duplicate on event["id"]
##       return "", 200
```
  


### Delivery semantics

- Answer `2xx` quickly; do slow work after acknowledging.
- A non-`2xx` response is retried, **up to 5 attempts** in total, with backoff of 30 seconds, 2 minutes, 10 minutes and 1 hour; after the last attempt the delivery is marked failed (see `GET /v1/platform/webhooks/{id}/deliveries`). The same event can arrive more than once: de-duplicate on `id`.
- Order is not guaranteed. For status, trust the latest `GET` of the resource over the order events arrived in.
- Treat a webhook as a prompt to re-read when it matters (for example before releasing goods): fetch the approval or ledger entry by id.

# Guides: operating


## Errors

Source: https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/errors/

### Error envelope

Errors are JSON with a machine-readable code and a human message:

```json
{ "error": "PASSKEY_SETUP_REQUIRED", "message": "Secure your wallet with a passkey before signing (POST /v1/wallet/passkeys)." }
```

Some codes add fields at the top level (`missing` and `kycUrl` on `ONRAMP_KYC_REQUIRED`; `min`, `max`, `currency`, `reason` on `AMOUNT_OUT_OF_RANGE`; `deviceStatus` on `DEVICE_NOT_TRUSTED`) or under `details`.

Older routes use other shapes. `POST /v1/offramps/init` and `/finalize`, and the KYC gate, return `{ "success": false, "error": "<sentence>", "code": "KYC_REQUIRED" }`; a few legacy middlewares return only a sentence in `error`. Read the code as `body.code ?? body.error`, switch on that, and never on message text.

`500` responses carry no internal detail:

```json
{ "message": "Internal server error", "requestId": "3f2c9a1e-…" }
```

Every response has an `X-Request-Id` header. Log it and quote it to Rift support.

`202 { "status": "APPROVAL_REQUIRED", … }` is not an error: the request is waiting for the customer's passkey ([approvals](https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/approvals/)).

### Error codes

| Code | HTTP | Area | Meaning and what to do |
|---|---|---|---|
| `AMOUNT_BELOW_MINIMUM` | 400 | Payouts | Nigeria payout under 1 unit of the stablecoin. |
| `AMOUNT_OUT_OF_RANGE` | 400 | Payouts, onramp | Over the per-transaction cap or outside corridor limits. Body: `min`, `max`, `currency`; `reason: "liquidity"` for the Tanzania float. See [limits](https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/payment-corridors/#limits). |
| `AMOUNT_TOO_LOW` | 400 | Bridge | Below the bridge's minimum deposit. |
| `APPROVAL_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | Approvals | Unknown id, or the caller is neither the customer nor the creating project. |
| `APPROVAL_NOT_PENDING` | 409 | Approvals | Already approved, rejected, expired or failed. Create a new one if still wanted. |
| `BRIDGE_QUOTE_FAILED` | 502 | Bridge | No bridge quote. Retry later. |
| `CHALLENGE_EXPIRED` | 400 | Statements, devices | Passkey challenge expired or already used (single use, 5 minutes). Request a new one. |
| `CREDENTIAL_EXISTS` | 409 | Passkeys | That passkey is already registered. |
| `DEVICE_CHECK_UNAVAILABLE` | 503 | Device binding | Rift could not check the device proof. Retry. |
| `DEVICE_MISMATCH` | 403 | Device binding | Recovery called from a device other than the one in the path. |
| `DEVICE_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | Device binding | Not one of the customer's devices. |
| `DEVICE_NOT_PENDING` | 409 | Device binding | Approve or recover on a device that is not pending. |
| `DEVICE_NOT_TRUSTED` | 403 | Device binding | Missing proof, unknown device or untrusted device (enforced environments). Body: `deviceStatus`, `coolingOffUntil`. See [device binding](https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/device-binding/). |
| `DEVICE_PROOF_INVALID` | 401 | Device binding | Proof rejected. Body `reason`: `malformed`, `stale`, `signature`, `replay`. Sign a new proof. |
| `EOA_SIGNING_REMOVED` | 410 | Wallet | Raw transaction signing no longer exists; go through the Safe (two-phase). |
| `FORBIDDEN` | 403 | General, platform | Authenticated but not allowed: another customer's order, wrong project, or a dashboard-only route. |
| `INTERNAL_ERROR` | 500 | General | Unexpected failure. Quote `requestId`. |
| `INVALID_AMOUNT` | 400 | Onramp, KYC gate | Amount missing, zero or not a number. |
| `INVALID_ATTESTATION` | 400 | Passkeys | The registration response is malformed (challenge missing or not base64url). |
| `INVALID_BENEFICIARY` | 400 | Payouts | `beneficiaryId` is not a usable fiat beneficiary. |
| `INVALID_CURRENCY` | 400 | KYC gate, rates | Unknown currency code. |
| `INVALID_EVENTS` | 400 | Platform webhooks | `events` must be a non-empty subset of the supported events. |
| `INVALID_PASSKEY_SIGNATURE` | 400 | Signing | The assertion does not verify against this ticket or challenge. Sign the current one again. |
| `INVALID_PUBLIC_KEY` | 400 | Device binding | `publicKey` is not a base64 SPKI P-256 key. |
| `INVALID_REQUEST` | 400 | General | Missing or invalid fields; the message names them. |
| `INVALID_TOKEN` | 400 | Device binding | Cancel link invalid or already used. |
| `INVALID_URL` | 400 | Platform webhooks | Webhook URL must be `https://`. |
| `KYC_CHECK_UNAVAILABLE` | 503 | KYC gate | The KYC volume check could not run. Retry. |
| `KYC_REQUIRED` | 400 | KYC gate | Compliance gates on: the customer must complete KYC (past the KYC-free volume limit, or for a KYC-only feature). Returned in `code`. |
| `LAST_OWNER` | 409 | Passkeys | Removing this passkey would leave a Safe without an owner. |
| `LAST_PASSKEY` | 409 | Passkeys | Cannot remove the only passkey; add another first. |
| `LAST_TRUSTED_DEVICE` | 409 | Device binding | Cannot remove the only trusted device in use. |
| `LEGACY_KEY_MISMATCH` | 409 | Wallet upgrade | A pre-passkey wallet's stored key does not match its owner. Contact Rift. |
| `LEGACY_KEY_UNRECOVERABLE` | 409 | Wallet upgrade | A pre-passkey wallet's key cannot be recovered for the owner swap. Contact Rift. |
| `MIGRATION_FAILED` | 409 | Wallet upgrade | The wallet could not be switched to passkey ownership on that chain. Body `details.chainId`. |
| `MIGRATION_NEEDS_GAS` | 409 | Wallet upgrade | The owner swap on that chain needs gas the wallet does not have. |
| `MIGRATION_REQUIRED` | 409 | Wallet upgrade | That chain has not been switched to passkey ownership yet. |
| `MIGRATION_UNAVAILABLE` | 503 | Wallet upgrade | Owner swap temporarily unavailable. Retry later. |
| `NETWORK_REQUIRED` | 400 | Onramp | Mobile-money onramp without `mobileNetwork`. |
| `NO_EMAIL` | 409 | Statements | `delivery: "email"` and the customer has no email. Use `download`. |
| `NO_OTP_TARGET` | 409 | Device binding | The account has neither email nor phone for a recovery code. |
| `NO_PROVIDER_AVAILABLE` | 503 | Onramp | No onramp liquidity right now. Retry later. |
| `NO_WALLET` | 409 | Wallet | The customer has no wallet yet. |
| `NOT_FOUND` | 404 | General | Resource not found, or not visible to this caller. Another project's resources are always 404. |
| `NOT_REFUNDABLE` | 409 | Refunds | Order is not a refundable failed payout with a transaction hash, or was already refunded. |
| `NOTHING_PENDING` | 404 | Passkeys | No pending passkey signatures to confirm. Start again. |
| `ONRAMP_DISABLED` | 404 | Onramp | Onramp is not enabled on this environment. |
| `ONRAMP_KYC_REQUIRED` | 409 | Onramp | No usable verified identity. Body: `missing`, `kycUrl`. |
| `ONRAMP_UNAVAILABLE` | 503 | Onramp | The corridor is paused. |
| `ORDER_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | Payouts, refunds | Unknown order, or the two-phase order expired. Call `init` again. |
| `OTP_INVALID` / `OTP_REQUIRED` | 400 | Device binding | Recovery code wrong or missing. |
| `OTP_SEND_FAILED` | 502 | Device binding | The recovery code could not be sent. |
| `PASSKEY_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | Passkeys | Not one of the customer's passkeys. |
| `PASSKEY_NOT_PENDING` | 409 | Passkeys | Confirm called on a passkey that is not pending. |
| `PASSKEY_POSSESSION_REQUIRED` | 400 | Passkeys | Registration without a `possession` assertion by the new passkey. |
| `PASSKEY_POSSESSION_UNVERIFIED` | 409 | Wallet upgrade | A passkey has no verified proof of possession; the owner swap is refused. |
| `PASSKEY_REQUIRED` | 400 | Signing | Submit without a passkey proof, or with a Google/Apple token as the proof. Google/Apple are login only. |
| `PASSKEY_SETUP_REQUIRED` | 409 | Signing, money movement | The customer has no passkey. Register one (`POST /v1/wallet/passkeys`). |
| `PASSKEY_UNSUPPORTED_ON_CHAIN` | 409 | Signing | That chain has no passkey signer contract. |
| `PAYOUT_FAILED` | 502 | Payouts | The fiat leg failed after the on-chain transfer. Look the order up; never resend. |
| `PAYOUT_ROUTE_UNAVAILABLE` | 400 | Payouts | That currency can't be paid from that chain and token (or rail). |
| `PHONE_REQUIRED` | 400 | Onramp | Mobile-money onramp with no phone on the order or the profile. |
| `*_ONRAMP_FAILED` / `*_COLLECT_FAILED` / `*_RATE_FAILED` | 400 / 502 | Onramp | The order could not be started. Nothing was collected. |
| `*_FUND_UNAVAILABLE` | 502 | Payouts (Rift-operated corridors) | No funding rate right now. Retry later. |
| `RATE_LIMITED` | 429 | General | Back off. Platform: 60/min per key. Statements: 5/hour. Payout lookups: 30 per 10 min. OTP lockout is also 429. |
| `REFUND_ACCOUNT_REQUIRED` | 400 | Onramp | NGN onramp without `refundAccount`. |
| `REFUND_FAILED` | 500 | Refunds | Unexpected failure before the refund was sent. Check the order before retrying. |
| `REFUND_IN_PROGRESS` | 409 | Refunds | Another refund request claimed the order. |
| `REFUND_PENDING_REVIEW` | 502 | Refunds | Outcome unknown; Rift reviews it. Do not call again. |
| `REFUND_REJECTED` | 400 | Refunds | The refund was declined; the order is back to `failed`. |
| `REPLACED_BY_PASSKEY_WALLETS` | 410 | Wallet | Removed pre-passkey endpoint. Use `/v1/wallet/passkeys`. |
| `REQUEST_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | WalletConnect | The WalletConnect request is gone or not the customer's. |
| `SMART_WALLET_ERROR` | 502 | Signing | The wallet service failed. Check status before retrying a submit. |
| `SUBMIT_FAILED` | 502 | Signing, payouts | The operation did not land on-chain, or the outcome is unknown. Check status before anything else. |
| `TICKET_EXPIRED` | 410 | Signing | Preview again. |
| `TICKET_MISMATCH` | 400 | Signing | The ticket belongs to another operation, order or customer. |
| `TICKET_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | Signing | Unknown or expired ticket. Preview again. |
| `UNAUTHENTICATED` / `UNAUTHORIZED` | 401 | General | Missing or expired customer token, or invalid / revoked platform key. Refresh the session or sign in again. |
| `UNSUPPORTED_CHAIN` / `UNSUPPORTED_CURRENCY` / `UNSUPPORTED_PAIR` / `UNSUPPORTED_TOKEN` | 400 | Onramp | Outside the onramp corridors. |
| `UPSTREAM_ERROR` | 502 | Onramp, ledger, payouts | A downstream call failed. Retry reads; check status before retrying writes. |
| `USER_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | General | The customer no longer exists. |
| `VALIDATION_UNSUPPORTED` | 400 | Payouts | Names can't be looked up on that rail. Does not affect payouts. |
| (sentence) | 401 | API key | Missing `X-API-Key`, bad format, or not a live project key. |
| (sentence) | 402 | Plans | Plan limit reached: monthly active wallets or free gas allowance. |
| (sentence) | 403 | Compliance |  |

The [API reference](https://riftfi.com/docs/api/) lists the responses of each endpoint.

### Retries and idempotency

The API does not take idempotency keys. Double payment is prevented by three rules instead:

1. **Tickets, challenges and approvals are single use.** A submitted ticket cannot be submitted again; an approved approval cannot be approved again; a refund claims its order before it is sent.
2. **The SDK never retries fund-moving or signing calls**, whatever `retries` is set to.
3. **You don't either.** After a timeout or `5xx` on a money call, the operation may have happened. Look it up first:

| You sent | Look it up with |
|---|---|
| A one-phase call that should return `202` | Your stored `approvalId` → `GET /v1/approvals/{id}`; without one, `GET /v1/approvals?status=pending`. |
| A submit (`submit-prepared`, `finalize`, approve) | `GET /v1/approvals/{id}`, `GET /v1/ledger`, or `GET /v1/offramps/{id}`. |
| A payout or refund | `GET /v1/offramps/{id}` or the ledger entry's `status` and `refundable`. |
| An onramp | `GET /v1/onramps`. |

Set `retries: 0` on the SDK in any server that proxies non-idempotent calls (sign-up, send, pay). Its default retries are meant for reads.

**Safe to retry:** `GET` requests, quotes, previews (a new preview returns a new ticket; the old one expires), registration options and name lookups. Back off on `429` and `503`. A device proof is single use: sign a new one for each attempt.

## Sandbox vs production

Source: https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/sandbox-vs-production/

Sandbox and production run the same API, SDKs and widget. You choose by base URL (or SDK environment) and use a project key from that environment.

| | Sandbox | Production |
|---|---|---|
| API base URL | `https://sandbox.riftfi.com` | `https://api.riftfi.com` |
| Widget | `https://widget.sandbox.riftfi.com/embed.js` | `https://widget.riftfi.xyz/embed.js` |
| `@rift-finance/react` | `<RiftProvider environment="sandbox">` | `<RiftProvider>` (default `"production"`) |
| `@rift-finance/wallet` | `environment: Environment.SANDBOX` | `environment: Environment.PRODUCTION` |
| Wallet owners | Customer passkeys, verified on-chain | Customer passkeys, verified on-chain |
| Funds | Sandbox wallets and test payment routes | Real customer funds |

### What is the same

- Signing: every fund move needs a passkey signature from the customer, in both environments.
- Approvals, two-phase tickets, error codes and response shapes.
- The dashboard: projects, keys, allowed origins and RP IDs are per environment. Configure both.

### What differs

- **Keys and customers don't cross.** Use the key from the environment you are calling. Customers and wallets created in sandbox do not exist in production.
- **Corridors.** Sandbox routes payouts and onramp to test paths; some corridors may be unavailable or blocked there (`SANDBOX_PAYOUT_BLOCKED`).
- **Feature flags.** Onramp and other Beta features are enabled per environment. Check with `GET /v1/payouts/countries` (`onrampActive`).
- **Compliance gates** such as KYC requirements are configured per environment.

### Recommended setup

1. Build and run CI against sandbox with a dedicated sandbox project.
2. Keep keys in environment variables (`RIFT_API_KEY`, `RIFT_ENV`), never in source.
3. Before launch, work through the [going-live checklist](https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/going-live/) against production with a small real amount.

## Going-live checklist

Source: https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/going-live/

### Project and keys

- [ ] A **production** project exists, separate from sandbox, with its own API key in your secret manager.
- [ ] The key is only in server environment variables and in the widget embed; it is not in source control, logs or mobile app bundles beyond what the widget needs.
- [ ] You know how to rotate the key (dashboard, or `POST /v1/projects/{id}/api-keys/rotate`) and who is allowed to.
- [ ] Platform API calls use a **platform key** (`psk_…`) held only on servers, one key per service, and you know how to revoke one in the dashboard.

### Origins and passkeys

- [ ] Every production origin that renders the widget, `<RiftAuth>` or `<RiftApprove>` is in **allowed origins**.
- [ ] If you run passkey ceremonies on your own domain, its RP ID is in the project's allowed RP IDs.
- [ ] Onboarding asks for a **second passkey** and the security screen lists passkeys, warns at one and blocks removing the last.
- [ ] Customers who skip passkey setup are routed back to it before any money action (`409 PASSKEY_SETUP_REQUIRED`).

### Money movement

- [ ] Every fund-moving call handles `202 APPROVAL_REQUIRED`, stores `approvalId` and shows the approval to the customer.
- [ ] Nothing retries money calls automatically; SDK `retries: 0` on servers. Timeouts trigger a status lookup, not a resend.
- [ ] Payouts validate the beneficiary and show the account name before the customer approves.
- [ ] Your payment states map Rift statuses (`processing`, `completed`, `refunding`, `refunded`, `expired`, `cancelled`, `failed`), and compliance holds never prompt a second payment.
- [ ] Amount limits per corridor are enforced in your UI ([payment corridors & limits](https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/payment-corridors/#limits)).
- [ ] Gas: you know who pays for which operations and what happens when a free allowance or sponsor cap is reached.

### Reconciliation and events

- [ ] A daily job reconciles your records against the ledger (`GET /v1/platform/ledger`, Beta) or per-customer ledgers.
- [ ] Webhook endpoints (Beta) verify `Rift-Signature` on the raw body, reject stale timestamps and de-duplicate on event `id`.
- [ ] You log `X-Request-Id` / `requestId` for every failed call.

### Data and compliance

- [ ] Consent for statements or credit scoring is captured in your product and recorded with the consents API before you use the data.
- [ ] Revocation is wired: withdrawing consent deletes the consent record and your next jobs exclude the customer.
- [ ] KYC and sanctions requirements for your jurisdiction and use case are configured with Rift for the production project.
- [ ] Your terms explain that the customer's passkeys are the only way to move their funds, and what that means if all are lost.

### Launch

- [ ] One small real transfer, payout and (if enabled) onramp end to end in production, approved with a real passkey.
- [ ] Support knows where to find the approval, ledger entry and order for a customer complaint.
- [ ] You have a Rift contact for incidents. See [pricing & sales](https://riftfi.com/docs/pricing/).

# SDK reference


## @rift-finance/wallet

Source: https://riftfi.com/docs/sdk/wallet/

TypeScript SDK for servers and trusted runtimes, with browser helpers for passkey ceremonies. **v4** is the passkey-wallet release; earlier versions predate approvals and passkeys.

```bash
npm install @rift-finance/wallet@^4.0.0
```

### Configure

```ts

const rift = new Rift({
  apiKey: process.env.RIFT_API_KEY,     // sk_…
  environment: Environment.SANDBOX,     // SANDBOX | PRODUCTION | DEVELOPMENT
  baseUrl: undefined,                   // override the environment's default URL
  timeout: 30_000,                      // ms
  retries: 0,                           // retries on 5xx / network errors for non-money calls (default 3)
});

rift.setBearerToken(customerAccessToken); // per instance; or rift.auth.login(...) stores it
```

| Method | |
|---|---|
| `setApiKey(key)` / `hasApiKey()` | Set or check the project key. |
| `setBearerToken(token)` / `clearBearerToken()` | Customer session for every service on this instance. |
| `isAuthenticated()` | Whether a bearer token is set. |
| `getEnvironment()` / `getBaseUrl()` | Current settings. |

Default base URLs: `SANDBOX` → `https://sandbox.riftfi.com`; `PRODUCTION` → the production API.

### Services

| Service | Methods |
|---|---|
| `rift.auth` | `sendOtp`, `verifyOtp`, `signup`, `login`, `loginWithGoogle`, `loginWithApple`, `getUser`, `updateUser`, `logout`, `isAuthenticated`, recovery-method helpers |
| `rift.wallet` | `status()`, `getChainBalance({ chain? })`, `getTokenBalance({ token, chain? })` |
| `rift.passkeys` | `getRegistrationOptions`, `register`, `confirm`, `list`, `remove`, `confirmRemoval`, `setup(opts)`, `removeWithPasskey(id, sign)` |
| `rift.approvals` | `get(id)`, `list({ status? })`, `preview(id)`, `approve(id, { ticketId, authProof })`, `reject(id)`, `approveWithPasskey(id, sign)` |
| `rift.transactions` | `send(req)` → `MaybeApproval`, `previewSpend(req)`, `getHistory`, `getFee` |
| `rift.signer` | `sendTransaction(req)` → `MaybeApproval`, `previewUserOp`, `submitPreparedUserOp`, `signMessage(req)` → `MaybeApproval`, `previewMessage`, `submitMessage`, `getWalletInstance` |
| `rift.bridge` | `getRoutes`, `getQuote`, `execute(req)` → `MaybeApproval`, `previewTransfer` |
| `rift.offramp` | `previewExchangeRate`, `getSupportedInstitutions(currency)`, `getWithdrawalFee(amount)`, `pay` / `createOrder` → `MaybeApproval`, `previewOrder`, `pollOrderStatus`, `getOrders` |
| `rift.walletConnect` | `pair`, `getRequests`, `previewRequest(id)`, `approveRequest(id, proof?)` → `MaybeApproval`, `rejectRequest`, `getSessions`, `disconnectSession` |
| `rift.kyc` | `getToken`, `checkUserExists`, `getStatus`, `verify`, `isVerified`, `getJobStatus`, `verifyAndSendOtp` |
| `rift.assets` | Chains and tokens catalog |
| `rift.merchant`, `rift.notifications`, `rift.deposits`, `rift.userManagement` | Invoices and merchant status, push notifications, deposit history, project-owner user management |

Not in the SDK yet: the Beta [Platform API](https://riftfi.com/docs/api/own-wallet/) (server-side, `psk_` keys) and the Beta onramp, payout-validation, ledger and statement endpoints of the [Core API](https://riftfi.com/docs/api/rift-wallet/). Call them with `fetch`; the guides show how.

### Money methods return approvals

Every one-phase fund-moving method returns `MaybeApproval<T>`: the result, or

```ts
interface ApprovalRequiredResponse {
  status: "APPROVAL_REQUIRED";
  approvalId: string;
  approvalUrl: string;
  expiresAt: string;        // ISO, default 30 minutes
  summary: ApprovalSummary;
}
```

```ts

const res = await rift.transactions.send({ to, value: "5", token: "USDC", chain: "BASE" });
if (isApprovalRequired(res)) { /* hand res.approvalUrl / res.approvalId to the customer */ }

const receipt = assertNoApproval(res); // or throw ApprovalRequiredError
```

These calls are **never retried**, whatever `retries` is set to.

### Passkey helpers (browser)

| Export | |
|---|---|
| `createPasskeyAuthProof(hashToSign, { rpId?, allowCredentials?, timeout? })` | Runs `navigator.credentials.get` over the 32 hash bytes with user verification and returns the `authProof`. |
| `registerPasskey(options, { authenticatorAttachment?, timeout? })` | Creation ceremony (ES256 only, resident key, UV) plus the possession assertion. Returns `{ attestation, possession }`. |
| `getHashToSign(preview)` | Reads `hashToSign`, `hash_to_sign` or `userOpHashHex`. |
| `bytesToBase64`, `base64ToBytes`, `hexToBytes`, `PASSKEY_ALG_ES256` | Encoding helpers. |
| `isPasskeySupported()`, `isPlatformPasskeySupported()` | Feature detection. |

### Key types

```ts
type PasskeyAuthProof = {
  kind: "passkey";
  cred_id_b64: string;
  client_data_json_b64: string;
  authenticator_data_b64: string;
  signature_b64: string;        // DER, base64
};

interface TwoPhasePreview { ticketId: string; hashToSign: string; chainId: number; allowCredentials?: string[]; expiresAt: string; summary?: ApprovalSummary }

interface WalletStatus {
  mode: "none" | "legacy" | "passkey";
  walletAddress: string | null;
  previousAddress?: string | null;
  passkeyCount: number;
  chains: { chainId: number; deployed: boolean; ownerMode: "legacy_eoa" | "passkey" | "undeployed" }[];
  needsPasskeySetup: boolean;
}

type ApprovalStatus = "pending" | "approved" | "rejected" | "expired" | "failed";
```

### Errors

The SDK throws `{ status, message, code?, error?, requestId? }`. Passkey-wallet codes get a readable `message`: `PASSKEY_SETUP_REQUIRED`, `PASSKEY_REQUIRED`, `PASSKEY_POSSESSION_REQUIRED`, `INVALID_PASSKEY_SIGNATURE`, `LAST_PASSKEY`, `EOA_SIGNING_REMOVED`, `REPLACED_BY_PASSKEY_WALLETS`. See [errors](https://riftfi.com/docs/guides/errors/).

### Upgrading from v3

| v3 | v4 |
|---|---|
| One-phase methods return `T` | Return `MaybeApproval<T>`; check `isApprovalRequired`. |
| `OidcHelper` (Google signing) | Removed: Google/Apple are login only. |
| `signer.signTransaction` | Throws `410 EOA_SIGNING_REMOVED`. Use `sendTransaction` or two-phase. |
| `auth.migrateToV3`, `wallet.listMethods` / `addMethod*` | Deprecated (`410 REPLACED_BY_PASSKEY_WALLETS`). Use `rift.passkeys`. |
| `defi.swap` | Deprecated; endpoint removed. Use `signer` calls. |
| `password` / OTP on signing calls | Ignored for passkey wallets. |
| `retries: 0` treated as 3 | `0` disables retries. |

## @rift-finance/react

Source: https://riftfi.com/docs/sdk/react/

React bindings for the hosted Rift widget. Sign-in, passkey setup and approvals run in a Rift iframe; your app gets typed components, hooks and the customer's session.

```bash
npm install @rift-finance/react@^0.4.0
```

`<RiftApprove>` and `useRiftApproval()` need **0.4.0 or later**. React 18 or 19.

Register every origin that renders these components in the dashboard (project → Origins); passkey setup and approvals from unlisted origins are rejected.

### RiftProvider

Wrap the app once.

| Prop | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `apiKey` | `string` | required | Project API key (`sk_…`). |
| `environment` | `"production" \| "sandbox"` | `"production"` | Picks the widget: `widget.riftfi.xyz` or `widget.sandbox.riftfi.com`, and so the backend. |
| `widgetUrl` | `string` | | Overrides `environment` (self-hosted widget, local build). |
| `autoOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | Open sign-in on mount when signed out. |
| `persist` | `boolean` | `true` | Remember the signed-in identity across reloads. The access token itself stays in memory. |

### RiftAuth

Mount once inside the provider. Renders nothing until `useRift().open()`.

| Prop | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `onSuccess` | `(user: RiftUser) => void` | Sign-in finished (including passkey setup when it ran). |
| `onError` | `(message: string) => void` | Sign-in failed. |
| `onClose` | `() => void` | Modal closed. |
| `maxHeight` | `number \| string` | Cap the modal height (`600` or `"70vh"`); the iframe scrolls inside. |
| `maxWidth` | `number \| string` | Default `480`. |
| `radius` | `number \| string` | Default `18`. |
| `backdrop` | `{ color?: string; blur?: number }` | Backdrop colour and blur (px). `blur: 0` disables it. |
| `backdropStyle`, `iframeStyle` | `CSSProperties` | Escape hatches, applied last. |

### RiftApprove

Shows one approval request and asks for the customer's passkey.

| Prop | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `approvalId` | `string` | required. From the `202 APPROVAL_REQUIRED` body. |
| `onResult` | `(r: RiftApprovalResult) => void` | Fires once with `{ approvalId, status, result? }`; `status` is `approved`, `rejected`, `expired` or `failed`; `result` is `{ transactionHash, userOpHash }` when approved. |
| `onError` | `(message: string) => void` | Non-terminal problems (prompt cancelled, network). The customer can retry. |
| `onClose` | `() => void` | The customer closed it. Unmount here. |
| `inline` | `boolean` | Render in place instead of as a modal, for example on your own `/approve/:id` page. |
| `maxHeight`, `maxWidth`, `radius`, `backdrop`, `backdropStyle`, `iframeStyle` | | As on `RiftAuth`. |

### useRift

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `user` | `RiftUser \| null` | Signed-in customer. |
| `isAuthenticated` | `boolean` | |
| `isOpen` | `boolean` | Whether the modal is open. |
| `open(opts?)` | `({ mode?: "signin" \| "signup" }) => void` | Open sign-in. |
| `close()` | `() => void` | |
| `signOut()` | `() => Promise<void>` | Revokes the session and clears local state. |
| `getAccessToken()` | `() => Promise<string>` | A valid token, refreshed through a hidden iframe when near expiry. Use this instead of `user.accessToken`. |
| `error` | `string \| null` | Last sign-in error. |

### useRiftApproval

```ts
const { requestApproval, approvalElement, approvalId, dismiss } = useRiftApproval(props?);
```

| Field | |
|---|---|
| `requestApproval(input)` | `input` is an `approvalId` or the `202` body. Shows the widget and resolves with `{ approvalId, status, result? }` once the customer acts, or `{ status: "dismissed" }` if they close it first. |
| `approvalElement` | Render it inside the provider. `null` when idle. |
| `approvalId` | The approval being shown. |
| `dismiss()` | Close it programmatically. |

`props` are passed to `<RiftApprove>` (visual options, `onError`, `inline`).

### RiftUser

```ts
interface RiftUser {
  user: string;            // Rift user id
  address: string;         // the customer's Safe address
  btcAddress?: string;
  accessToken: string;     // short-lived; prefer getAccessToken()
  expiresAt?: string;
  walletStatus?: RiftWalletStatus;   // at sign-in; not persisted across reloads
  passkeySetup?: {                   // when passkey setup ran in this sign-in
    status: "active" | "migrated" | "migrating" | "new_wallet" | "pending_signature";
    walletAddress?: string;
    previousAddress?: string;
  };
}
```

Exported types: `RiftUser`, `RiftConfig`, `RiftMode`, `RiftEvent`, `RiftWalletStatus`, `RiftPasskeySetup`, `RiftApprovalStatus`, `RiftApprovalResult`, `RiftApproveProps`, `RiftApprovalOutcome`.

### Theming

The frame around the iframe is yours (size, radius, backdrop). The widget's content follows your project branding from the dashboard and stays Rift-branded, so customers know who is asking for their passkey.

## Widget (embed.js)

Source: https://riftfi.com/docs/sdk/widget/

### Script tag

```html
<script src="https://widget.riftfi.xyz/embed.js" data-project-key="sk_…" async></script>
```

| Attribute | |
|---|---|
| `src` | `https://widget.riftfi.xyz/embed.js` (production) or `https://widget.sandbox.riftfi.com/embed.js` (sandbox). The widget origin decides the backend. |
| `data-project-key` | Your project API key. Required. |

Elements with `data-rift-trigger` open the modal on click; `data-rift-mode` sets the mode (`signin` default, `signup`).

### Methods

| | |
|---|---|
| `Rift.open(opts?)` | `opts.mode`: `"signin"` · `"signup"` · `"approve"`. `opts.approvalId`: required for `approve`. `opts.theme`: `"light"` · `"dark"`. |
| `Rift.close()` | Close the modal. |
| `Rift.on(event, handler)` / `Rift.off(event, handler)` | Subscribe / unsubscribe. |

Without `opts.theme` the widget matches the page: `data-theme` on `<html>`, a `light`/`dark` class on `<html>` or `<body>`, then `prefers-color-scheme`.

### Events

| Event | Payload |
|---|---|
| `ready` | `{}` |
| `open` | `{ mode }` |
| `close` | `{}` |
| `signin-success` | `{ user, address, btcAddress, accessToken, walletStatus, passkeySetup }` |
| `signin-error` | `{ message }` |
| `approval-result` | `{ approvalId, status, result }` |
| `approval-error` | `{ approvalId, message }` |

Messages from the iframe are accepted only from the widget's own origin.

### Modes

- **Sign-in / sign-up**: email OTP, phone OTP, Google and Apple. Followed by **Secure your wallet with a passkey** when `walletStatus.needsPasskeySetup` is true (two taps: create, then confirm).
- **Approve**: shows the approval summary, signs in the customer if needed, asks for their passkey, then reports the result.

### Requirements

- The embedding origin is in the project's allowed origins.
- The iframe is allowed `publickey-credentials-create; publickey-credentials-get` (set by `embed.js` and `@rift-finance/react`).

### Self-hosting

For white-labelling or compliance isolation, the widget is a static Vite app you can host yourself. Build-time settings:

| Variable | Default | |
|---|---|---|
| `VITE_API_BASE_URL` | `https://api.riftfi.com` | Backend the widget calls. |
| `VITE_PASSKEY_RP_ID` | eTLD+1 of the widget host | WebAuthn RP ID when the backend's options do not name one, and for approvals. |
| `VITE_PASSKEY_RP_NAME` | `Rift` | Name in the passkey prompt. |

Point `<RiftProvider widgetUrl>` or your script `src` at your host, and register its RP ID with Rift. Note that passkeys are bound to an RP ID: customers' passkeys created under Rift's widget will not work on a widget served under a different RP ID.

## MCP server tools

Source: https://riftfi.com/docs/sdk/mcp/

The Rift MCP server exposes 83 tools. Setup is in the [MCP quickstart](https://riftfi.com/docs/quickstarts/mcp/). Tools marked **approval** return an approval link instead of executing; the customer approves with a passkey.

### Passkey wallet & approvals

| Tool | |
|---|---|
| `rift_get_wallet_status` | Wallet mode, passkey count, per-chain owner mode, `needsPasskeySetup`. |
| `rift_get_approval` | Status and result of an approval (API key alone is enough). |
| `rift_list_approvals` | The customer's approvals (default: pending). |

### Setup & docs

`rift_set_api_key`, `rift_set_api_url`, `rift_status`, `rift_search_docs`, `rift_get_api_endpoints`, `rift_get_supported_chains`.

### Auth & user

`rift_signup`, `rift_send_otp`, `rift_verify_otp`, `rift_login`, `rift_logout`, `rift_get_user`, `rift_update_user`, `rift_delete_user`, `rift_create_recovery`, `rift_get_recovery_options`, `rift_request_password_reset`, `rift_reset_password`.

### Money movement

| Tool | |
|---|---|
| `rift_get_balance` | Balance by chain / token. |
| `rift_send_crypto` | Send (gasless). **Approval.** |
| `rift_get_transaction_history`, `rift_get_transaction_fee` | History and fees. |
| `rift_preview_exchange_rate`, `rift_get_payment_methods`, `rift_get_withdrawal_fee` | Payout rates, methods, fees. Set `type="offramp"` or `"onramp"` correctly; the rates differ. |
| `rift_offramp`, `rift_offramp_create_order` | Cash out to mobile money or bank. **Approval.** |
| `rift_poll_offramp_status`, `rift_get_offramp_orders` | Track payouts. |
| `rift_buy_crypto`, `rift_get_onramp_status`, `rift_get_onramp_orders` | Onramp. |
| `rift_get_bridge_routes`, `rift_bridge_quote` | Bridge routes and quotes. |
| `rift_bridge_execute` | Bridge. **Approval.** |
| `rift_swap` | Swap. **Approval.** |

### WalletConnect

`rift_wc_pair`, `rift_wc_get_requests`, `rift_wc_approve` (**approval**), `rift_wc_reject`, `rift_wc_sessions`, `rift_wc_disconnect`.

### Signer

| Tool | |
|---|---|
| `rift_get_wallet_instance` | Wallet for a chain. |
| `rift_send_transaction` | UserOperation through the Safe. **Approval.** |
| `rift_sign_message` | ERC-1271 message signature. **Approval.** |
| `rift_sign_transaction` | Removed upstream (`410 EOA_SIGNING_REMOVED`); kept to return a clear error. |

### Other

- **KYC:** `rift_kyc_get_token`, `rift_kyc_check_user_exists`, `rift_kyc_status`, `rift_kyc_verify`, `rift_kyc_is_verified`, `rift_kyc_job_status`.
- **Merchant:** `rift_create_invoice`, `rift_get_invoices`, `rift_merchant_status`.
- **Notifications:** `rift_notifications_register`, `rift_notifications_send`, `rift_notifications_subscriptions`.
- **Assets:** `rift_get_tokens`, `rift_get_user_tokens`, `rift_get_chains`.
- **User management** (project owner's session): `rift_suspend_user`, `rift_unsuspend_user`, `rift_get_suspended_users`, `rift_get_user_status`.
- **Deposits:** `rift_get_deposits`.

# Endpoint catalogue

The per-project API: every operation you call with your project API key or a project id you own (tier "per-project"), the server-only platform tier (psk_ key) and public reference data. End-user flows that the Rift widget, React components and SDK run for you are listed after the catalogue and are not an integration surface. Notation: METHOD path [auth] summary | params (* = required, in parentheses where it goes) | example JSON body. "customer token" = Authorization: Bearer; "project key" = X-API-Key. Full per-endpoint detail: https://riftfi.com/docs/api/core/ and https://riftfi.com/docs/api/platform/. Try any of them live: https://riftfi.com/docs/playground/

### Assets

- GET /v1/assets [none] (per-project) List all supported assets.
- GET /v1/assets/by-type/{type} [none] (per-project) List assets by type (stable, erc20, native). | params: type*(path)
- GET /v1/assets/by-category/{category} [none] (per-project) List assets by category. | params: category*(path)

### Auth

- POST /v1/auth/sign-up [project key] (per-project) Create a new user account. | body: {}
- POST /v1/auth/sign-in [project key] (per-project) Authenticate existing user. | body: {}
- POST /v1/auth/sign-in/google [none] (per-project) Verify a Google ID token and find-or-create the user. | body: {"idToken":"string","referrer":"string"}
- POST /v1/auth/sign-in/apple [none] (per-project) Verify an Apple identity token and find-or-create the user. | body: {"idToken":"string","displayName":"string","referrer":"string"}

### Billing

- GET /v1/billing/plans [none] (per-project) Get the public billing plan catalogue.
- GET /v1/billing/payment-info [none] (per-project) Get the on-chain payment configuration (admin payout address + supported chains).

### Chains

- GET /v1/chains [none] (per-project) List all supported chains.
- GET /v1/chains/{id} [none] (per-project) Get a single chain by id. | params: id*(path)
- GET /v1/chains/{chainId}/tokens [none] (per-project) List tokens for a specific chain. | params: chainId*(path)

### Invoices

- POST /v1/invoices/{id}/payments [project key] (per-project) Mark an invoice as paid via an on-chain transaction. | params: id*(path) | body: {"transactionHash":"string","chain":"string"}
- GET /v1/invoices [customer token + project key] (per-project) List invoices. | params: status(query), sortBy(query), sortOrder(query), startDate(query), endDate(query), page(query), limit(query)
- POST /v1/invoices [customer token + project key] (per-project) Create a new invoice. | body: {"chain":"string","token":"string","amount":1}
- POST /v1/invoices/{id}/notifications [project key] (per-project) Deliver an invoice link via email or SMS to a recipient. | params: id*(path) | body: {"paymentLink":"string","message":"string","recipientEmail":"string","recipientPhone":"string"}

### One-time codes

- POST /v1/one-time-codes [none] (per-project) Send a one-time code via SMS or email. | body: {"phone":"string","email":"string"}
- POST /v1/one-time-codes/verify [none] (per-project) Verify a one-time code. | body: {"phone":"string","email":"string","code":"string"}

### Own-wallet ramps

- POST /v1/ramps/offramp/quotes [none] (per-project) Quote an offramp | body: {"currency":"KES","recipient":{"type":"mobile"}}
- POST /v1/ramps/offramp/quotes/{quoteId}/submit [none] (per-project) Submit the deposit and pay out | params: quoteId*(path) | body: {"txHash":"0xabc…"}
- POST /v1/ramps/onramp [none] (per-project) Onramp to any address | body: {"currency":"KES","amount":"string","phone":"+254712345678","toAddress":"string"}
- GET /v1/ramps/orders/{id} [none] (per-project) Get a ramp order | params: id*(path)

### Payouts (Beta)

- GET /v1/payouts/countries [none] (per-project) Countries, rails and limits for payouts and onramp (public, cached about 10 minutes).
- POST /v1/payouts/validate [customer token] (per-project) Look up a payout recipient's registered name before paying. | body: {"currency":"string"}
- POST /v1/payouts/validate [customer token] (per-project) Look up a payout recipient's registered name before paying. | body: {"currency":"string"}

### Platform (Beta)

- GET /v1/platform/keys [platform key (psk_)] (per-project) List platform secret keys (owner session only)
- POST /v1/platform/keys [platform key (psk_)] (per-project) Create a platform secret key (owner session only); the key is returned once | body: {"label":"string"}
- DELETE /v1/platform/keys/{id} [platform key (psk_)] (per-project) Revoke a platform key (owner session only) | params: id*(path)
- GET /v1/platform/customers [platform key (psk_)] (per-project) List customers | params: search(query), kyc(query), cursor(query), limit(query)
- GET /v1/platform/customers/{id} [platform key (psk_)] (per-project) Customer detail | params: id*(path)
- GET /v1/platform/customers/{id}/ledger [platform key (psk_)] (per-project) Customer ledger | params: id*(path), from(query), to(query), type(query), cursor(query), limit(query)
- GET /v1/platform/customers/{id}/statement [platform key (psk_)] (per-project) Customer statement file | params: id*(path), from(query), to(query), format(query)
- GET /v1/platform/customers/{id}/consents [platform key (psk_)] (per-project) List consents | params: id*(path)
- POST /v1/platform/customers/{id}/consents [platform key (psk_)] (per-project) Record a consent | params: id*(path) | body: {"purpose":"credit_scoring","grantedAt":"2026-01-01T00:00:00Z","evidence":"string"}
- DELETE /v1/platform/customers/{id}/consents/{consentId} [platform key (psk_)] (per-project) Revoke a consent | params: id*(path), consentId*(path)
- GET /v1/platform/ledger [platform key (psk_)] (per-project) All-customer ledger (JSON or CSV) | params: from(query), to(query), type(query), status(query), customerId(query), cursor(query), limit(query), format(query)
- GET /v1/platform/webhooks [platform key (psk_)] (per-project) List webhook endpoints (secret never returned)
- POST /v1/platform/webhooks [platform key (psk_)] (per-project) Create a webhook endpoint; the signing secret (whsec_...) is returned once | body: {"url":"string","events":["transaction.created"],"description":"string"}
- DELETE /v1/platform/webhooks/{id} [platform key (psk_)] (per-project) Disable a webhook endpoint | params: id*(path)
- POST /v1/platform/webhooks/{id}/test [platform key (psk_)] (per-project) Send a webhook.test event now | params: id*(path)
- GET /v1/platform/webhooks/{id}/deliveries [platform key (psk_)] (per-project) Delivery log | params: id*(path)
- GET /v1/platform/gas-policy [platform key (psk_)] (per-project) Get gas policy
- PUT /v1/platform/gas-policy [platform key (psk_)] (per-project) Set gas policy | body: {"mode":"sponsored","sponsoredOps":["transfer"],"monthlySponsorCapUsd":1,"perTxSponsorCapUsd":1}
- GET /v1/platform/usage [platform key (psk_)] (per-project) Monthly usage | params: month(query)

### Projects

- GET /v1/projects/{id} [customer token] (per-project) Get a project's details. | params: id*(path)
- PATCH /v1/projects/{id} [customer token] (per-project) Update a project (name, branding, custom widget domain). | params: id*(path) | body: {}
- GET /v1/projects/{id}/stats [customer token] (per-project) Get a project's usage stats. | params: id*(path)
- GET /v1/projects/{id}/api-logs [customer token] (per-project) Get a paginated API call log for a project. | params: id*(path), page(query), limit(query), status(query), onlyErrors(query)
- PATCH /v1/projects/{id}/markup [customer token] (per-project) Configure the project's markup (custom service-fee on transfers). | params: id*(path) | body: {"markup_bps":1,"markup_treasury_address":"string"}
- POST /v1/projects/{id}/api-keys/rotate [customer token] (per-project) Rotate the project's API key. | params: id*(path) | body: {"otpCode":"string","email":"string","phoneNumber":"string","externalId":"string","password":"string"}
- POST /v1/projects/{id}/origins [customer token] (per-project) Add an allowed origin to a project's CORS whitelist. | params: id*(path) | body: {"origin":"string","phoneNumber":"string","email":"string","otpCode":"string","externalId":"string","password":"string"}

### Projects (Billing)

- GET /v1/projects/{id}/billing/subscription [customer token] (per-project) Get the current billing subscription and usage. | params: id*(path)
- GET /v1/projects/{id}/billing/payments [customer token] (per-project) List the project's billing payment history. | params: id*(path)
- POST /v1/projects/{id}/billing/payments [customer token] (per-project) Submit an on-chain payment to upgrade or renew a plan. | params: id*(path) | body: {"tier":"string","chain":"string","txHash":"string"}

### Rails

- GET /v1/rails/{currency}/institutions [none] (per-project) List supported payment institutions for a currency. | params: currency*(path)
- GET /v1/rails/{currency}/payment-methods [none] (per-project) Get the full payment-method catalogue for a currency. | params: currency*(path)

### Rates

- GET /v1/rates [none] (per-project) Public live FX rates with IP-derived default currency.
- POST /v1/rates/quote [none] (per-project) Get an exchange-rate + fee quote (onramp or offramp). | body: {"currency":"string","amount":1,"type":"string"}
- GET /v1/rates/withdrawal-fee [none] (per-project) Get the withdrawal fee (bid-ask spread) for a currency. | params: currency(query)

### Recovery

- GET /v1/identifier-recovery/options/{externalId} [project key] (per-project) Get masked recovery options for an externalId. | params: externalId*(path)
- GET /v1/identifier-recovery/options [project key] (per-project) Get masked recovery options by primary identifier. | params: identifier*(query), identifierType*(query)
- GET /v1/identifier-recovery/tokens/{token} [project key] (per-project) Validate a recovery token. | params: token*(path)
- POST /v1/identifier-recovery/password-reset [project key] (per-project) Send a password-reset link via email or SMS. | body: {"externalId":"string","method":"string"}
- POST /v1/identifier-recovery/password-reset/complete [project key] (per-project) Reset a user's password with a previously issued token. | body: {"token":"string","newPassword":"string"}
- POST /v1/identifier-recovery/account-recovery [project key] (per-project) Send an account-recovery link (re-establish primary identifier). | body: {"identifier":"string","identifierType":"string","method":"string"}
- POST /v1/identifier-recovery/account-recovery/complete [project key] (per-project) Complete an account-recovery flow by changing the primary identifier. | body: {"token":"string","newIdentifier":"string","identifierType":"string","otpCode":"string"}

### Reference

- GET /v1/reference/kenya/bank-paybills [none] (per-project) Reference list of Kenyan bank paybills.

### Tokens

- GET /v1/tokens [none] (per-project) List all tokens.
- GET /v1/tokens/{id} [none] (per-project) Get a single token by id. | params: id*(path)

### Users

- GET /v1/users [customer token] (per-project) List all users in the project (project owner only, paginated). | params: search(query), page(query), limit(query)
- GET /v1/users/lookup [customer token + project key] (per-project) Look up a user's suspension status by identifier. | params: phoneNumber(query), email(query), externalId(query), userId(query)
- GET /v1/users/suspended [customer token + project key] (per-project) List suspended users in the project (project owner or admin key).
- POST /v1/users/{id}/suspend [customer token + project key] (per-project) Suspend a user (project owner or admin key). | params: id*(path) | body: {"reason":"string"}
- POST /v1/users/{id}/unsuspend [customer token + project key] (per-project) Lift a user's suspension (project owner or admin key). | params: id*(path)
- GET /v1/users/status [customer token + project key] (per-project) Get a user's suspension status (alias of /v1/users/lookup). | params: phoneNumber(query), email(query), externalId(query), userId(query)
- POST /v1/users/suspend [customer token + project key] (per-project) Suspend a user identified in the body (project owner or admin key). | body: {"userId":"string","email":"string","phoneNumber":"string","externalId":"string","reason":"string"}
- POST /v1/users/unsuspend [customer token + project key] (per-project) Lift the suspension of a user identified in the body (project owner or admin key). | body: {"userId":"string","email":"string","phoneNumber":"string","externalId":"string"}

### Virtual accounts

- GET /v1/accounts [none] (per-project) List your accounts
- POST /v1/accounts [none] (per-project) Open a virtual account | body: {"currency":"KES"}
- GET /v1/accounts/banks [none] (per-project) Bank codes for disbursement | params: currency(query)
- GET /v1/accounts/{id} [none] (per-project) Get one account | params: id*(path)
- POST /v1/accounts/{id}/collections/preview [none] (per-project) Preview a collection | params: id*(path) | body: {"amount":"string","rail":"mobile"}
- POST /v1/accounts/{id}/collections [none] (per-project) Collect into the account | params: id*(path) | body: {"amount":"string","phone":"+254712345678","network":"Safaricom","reference":"string"}
- POST /v1/accounts/{id}/disbursements/preview [none] (per-project) Preview a disbursement | params: id*(path) | body: {"amount":"string","recipient":{"type":"mobile"}}
- POST /v1/accounts/{id}/disbursements [none] (per-project) Disburse from the account | params: id*(path) | body: {"amount":"string","recipient":{"type":"mobile"},"reference":"string"}
- GET /v1/accounts/{id}/transactions [none] (per-project) List transactions | params: id*(path), type(query), status(query), limit(query), cursor(query)
- GET /v1/accounts/{id}/statement [none] (per-project) Account statement | params: id*(path), from(query), to(query)
- GET /v1/accounts/transactions/{txnId} [none] (per-project) Get one transaction | params: txnId*(path)

### Widget

- GET /v1/widget-config [project key] (per-project) Get the project's public widget configuration (name, branding, origins).

# Used by the Rift widget and app (not an integration surface)

End-user flows authenticated with the customer access token, often needing a passkey signature on the customer device. The widget, React components and SDK call them for you; do not build against them directly.
